review_headline: Cute teapot, but the circular handle is tricksy
review_body:
I give it three stars, because it's a super cute little teapot, and I like that the lid is removable. It would be great to use at home.

However, I'm returning it. I bought the teapot to make tea at work, where I have a bit of a walk to get from my desk to the hot water. I've found that the rounded shape of the pot makes getting it underneath the hot water spigot challenging. Even worse, the perfectly round handle shape makes the full, hot teapot challenging to carry any distance. The weight of 24 ounces of water and the teapot tend to make your hand to slip around the circular handle. I found that I wanted to press a finger against the body of the teapot to keep it upright, but I'd just poured boiling hot water into it, and the teapot got too hot. I suppose I could support it from the bottom, but I'd have to use a napkin or something to protect myself from the heat...but I also usually have my lunch in my other hand as I toddle back to my office.

The spout does dribble just a bit when you pour, but that's a minor complaint. If I was using this teapot in a more traditional way, I'd probably keep it. It's cute as a button!

product_title: Energy Tea - Blue Lady Black High Caffeine Tea - As Much Caffeine As Coffee Per Bag (20 Tea Sachets)
review_body:
Trying to reduce the fat and sugar I ingest with my daily coffee; I am drinking Zest Energy Tea, Apple Cinnamon flavor, lately. I do get a surge of energy from it without any crash like can happen with coffee; since I use cream and sugar unless I have it bulletproof (but that is a story for another day). Now this tea has three times the caffeine of regular tea and even more than caffeinated coffee. Possibly you would like to be sure to drink it earlier in the day if you are one of those affected by caffeine and unable to sleep afterward. As for me, I need the caffeine and am having it with my first meal of the day. I need the mental clarity it provides, plus the energy, so trying this for me was a no-brainer.

The bag is attractive. It contains 50g, which is 20 sachets, inside. It smells heavenly, which sets you up to want to drink it. I drink it without cream or sugar, but you can certainly add them if you like, too. Honey or coconut sugar come to mind as healthy sweetening options that would pair well with this cup. I highly recommend Zest Tea Apple Cinnamon Black Tea. I want to try their others varieties now that I like this one so much.

product_title: Betty Crocker Potatoes Mashed Potatoes
review_headline: Tastes Better Than Most Rehydrated Potatoes, Especially If You Don't Read The Ingredients List
review_body:
Yukon Gold potatoes are my favorite since they are moist with a naturally buttery flavor. Better Crocker combines them with regular garden variety Russets, add margarine, with partially hydrogenated soy bean oil and a bit of real butter, skim milk powder and 4 different preservatives and calls them Yukon Gold Mashed Potatoes.

They are a convenience food, no doubt, but the taste is actually better than the majority of rehydrated potato products out there. Prices do tend to wildly fluctuate, but we are happy to order 7 packets of these for a nice add-on price every so often. 3 stars for ingredients list, 5 stars for flavor, averaging out to 4 stars overall. One tip: I often use mashed potato flakes instead of flour to thicken sauces, stews and chowders. Essentially gluten free but contains soy, whey and milk.

product_title: Tuscan Dairy Whole Vitamin D Milk, Gallon, 128 oz
review_headline: The worst part of the purchase was awaiting its arrival and ...
review_body:
After reading the reviews and seeing the price on this milk I decided that it must be life changing and I had to have it. The worst part of the purchase was awaiting its arrival and I missed two days of work worried with anticipation.
The sound of a diesel engine and squeaky brakes was the climax of my anticipation knowing that the FedEx truck was certainly near. Before the driver could unbuckle his seat belt I was already rummaging through the myriad of packages looking for my milk. After nearly 5 minutes of frantic searching, there it was, like a beacon in the night my Tuscan Whole Milk!
I rushed into the house shaking like a dog passing peach pits, ready to pour the nectar of the gods over a bowl of cinnamon toast crunch that had been carefully prepared the night before. Unfortunately the packaging was like trying to break into Fort Knox and I nearly wet myself with excitement. After locating a razor knife I ever so carefully made the necessary cuts to free my Tuscan Whole Milk from the restraints that imprisoned the ecstasy I had been anticipating. Finally free from its containment I removed the milk and to my utter dismay the jug was filled with a rancid chunk of clumpy, congealed, foulness that had no similarity to the dairy delight I envisioned so many nights in my dreams.
At this point I absolutely lost my cool. I ran screaming from the house literally smashing through the patio door nearly severing my finger but that would have to wait. I smashed my car window with a brick and kicked in the door like an MMA fighter would kick his opponent. At this point I guess you could say the entire neighborhood was "aware" that I was unhappy. My neighbor came over to try and diffuse the situation which didn't turn out well for him when he found himself on the receiving end of a nasty throat punch! I vaguely remembering hearing someone saying "call 911" but that was no deterrent for my anger. I took my anger out of shrubs, fences, mailboxes, small forest animals, and a stray cat or two. The flashing red and blues had no effect on my rage and soon I found myself on the receiving end of a tazer which caused my bladder and bowels to leak all over the street. After being treated for multiple cuts, bruises, contusions, and a concussion I was booked into jail and given a court date. Luckily I found another inmate that had a similar experience with Tuscan Whole Milk and he contacted his wife to place another order for the both of us. My new gallon of Tuscan Whole Milk should be just in time for my homecoming and I know that this time it will be everything I anticipate it to be.

product_title: Boost Nutritional Drinks Compact Complete Nutrition Drink, 4 Count (Pack of 4)
review_headline: easy way to increase calorie intake
review_body:
As a high calorie, high protein supplement these boost compact drinks taste pretty good. As a beverage unto themselves, not so much. I can best describe it as cold, thickened hot chocolate. It has a bit of a chalky taste and the chocolate flavor tastes like just that, chocolate flavoring. While the taste is tolerable the texture is the difficult part. The thickness borders on gloppy and I found it much improved by being thinned with some milk. That said, this is a drink intended to be a concentrated source of calories and protein and for this purpose it's good. I have experience with high calorie liquid medical foods since one of our children has required them on and off. Suffice to say they're not know for their delicious taste. Comparatively this boost drink tastes good.

After reading other reviews I'd like to note that this is not for weight loss. If anything it is to promote weight gain. Drinking it as a replacement for a full meal might work for weight loss but the small size (half a cup) would almost certainly leave you feeling hungry.

Bottom line, this is a solid option for those needing a supplemental food but who aren't always able to drink the larger 8oz containers. In my opinion, as someone who has dealt with high calorie prescription foods, those needing this product should discuss its use with their doctor so as to be sure they are taking in the correct number of calories for their needs while staying hydrated.

product_title: Enjoy Life Plentils
review_headline: delicious (but don't eat the whole bag at once)
review_body:
These are pretty good. They have a light and airy texture, but they're still crunchy (not too hard, though). The salt level is just perfect as far as taste goes (but the sodium in these is quite high at 420 mg (18% of the daily value in one serving).

These have a nice bit of protein with not much fiber (probably because the second ingredient is starch). These are made in a nut-free and certified gluten-free facility which is great if you have allergies or food intolerances.

You can see the full nutrition facts panel in the product images. The only thing I don't love is how easy it is to eat the whole bag in 1 or 2 sittings (I *may* be guilty of doing that). These do stay fresh if the bag is rolled up for a day (at least) after being open. These will remind you a little of potato chips because they do contain potato starch (they are also quite high in starch).

I did have some broken pieces at the bottom of the bag. They weren't as small as the dust I see in some other potato chip bags, but these do have something of a tendency to break during transit.

product_title: Two Rivers Coffee Bit of Everything Sampler Packs for Single-Cup Keurig K-Cup Brewers
review_headline: There's quite a fun variety of potential flavors in here
review_body:
There's quite a fun variety of potential flavors in here. When I first saw that the title was a cocoa sampler pack, I wasn't thinking that it would be an array of candy flavors. It definitely sets a much lighter mood than most of the K-cup variety packs I've ever seen, and I like that they applied some creative thinking to come up with the idea of using popular candies as flavors. They work as standard K-cups, and the flavors are good.

These are kind of a stretch in the end to present as K-cups, though, because the cups themselves are pretty wasteful and there's really no reason you can't tear open a (biodegradable) packet of cocoa and dump it into a mug and have the Keurig add hot water for you. Same cocoa powder, probably even more compact for storage in your home, probably better results (no chance some of the mix gets stuck in the cup), and really not any harder. Also, they didn't provide much information about what's in them that it really seems ought to be there. This isn't just a bit of coffee or a tea bag anymore, it's cocoa and it's probably got a decent amount of sugar along for the ride. People ought to have easier ways to know how much.

They can definitely be fun, but it's not something I'd be wanting to get all the time.

product_title: Food Should Taste Good Multigrain Tortilla Chips 1.5 oz. (Pack of 24)
review_headline: I'm a big fan of their Multigrain variety
review_body:
I buy these locally, but I wanted to post here and say how good I think these are. That, and mention that you may want to look for them at your local grocer or Target (or wherever you shop). I can get these at either Target or Safeway for between ~$3.50 and $5 for a 5.5-ounce bag depending on the day, and you can check the expiration date when you buy locally. Buying directly from Amazon is a good way to go, though, as I know that they'll make it right if you get a bad batch from them. Prices fluctuate so much on Amazon, though, that you certainly may find them cheaper here than locally.

I really like the flavor, texture, and size of the Multigrain version (and it's the only one that I've tried, although I've seen some of the others). They have a nice, healthy taste to them - not overly salty or oily, and I love the addition of the seeds. Btw, the seeds aren't obtrusive or make them more difficult to eat. Instead, they just add some nice additional taste to the corn. Although not triangular like a lot of tortilla chips, the shape is still good for dipping into salsa.

I enjoy these chips either with salsa or simply plain. They taste good, and while likely still not a health food :), they sure seem healthier to me than a lot of the regular corn tortilla chips that I get.

Two big thumbs up from me for the Multigrain. I highly recommend them.

review_headline: It is super spicy and has a different taste
review_body: Don't listen to the 5 star reviews. They are either fake or uninformed. There is no way this product is real Wasabi Rhizome. I regularly purchase real 100% wasabi from New Zealand- Namida Wasabi; it's way more expensive and totally different. It is super spicy and has a different taste. Super Sonic Wasabi tastes like it is about 5% wasabi and 95% corn starch. I wondered why the jar I purchased was a such a good deal after spending 3 x the amount on New Zealand Wasabi which is the real deal. I am not affiliated with any company. I am a low level paper pusher for Oklahoma State government and spend a lot of time at work researching health food on the internet (after I am all caught up with my work, I'm fast). I've read about all the health benefits of real Wasabi and I also know that cultivating it is a painstaking process only achieved in running, fresh water, in very specific climates. There are few climates where Wasabi can even be grown, so it is possible that this jar is made entirely of an inferior product that was improperly grown. It is like any product you purchase, the quality is in the production. It is apparent with the first taste of Super Sonic Real Wasabi that the production value of the product is not up to snuff. Real Wasabi will make your stomach churn with just a 1/4 teaspoon, regardless of if it is WET OR NOT! There explanation is watered down, just like the product. You'll do better if you spend the extra money and purchase the expensive stuff, plus some cheap gelatin capsules and swallow a pill once a day. It's expensive, but really you don't need to take it every day for the rest of your life. Take it for couple months if you are currently sick, or if not sick just buy a bottle a couple times a year and do a "Wasabi Cleanse" by adding it to your diet daily for a few weeks. Just don't waste your money or hopes on Sushi Sonic.

review_body:
Every so often, I will find a recipe I want to bake that calls for casting sugar. These recipes usually originate in the UK. Casting sugar is a super fine sugar that is used in baking. I have found the India Tree Superfine Cadpting Sugar to be the best. Casting sugar can be fairly expensive do look for the best price.

I am including a recipe for a sponge cake with blueberries and cream. This is a recipe that everyone will love. A summertime treat to be sure .

From The Olive

Lemon Victoria Sponge Cake

Ingredients:

175g (6 oz) unsalted butter
175g (3/4 cup) golden caster sugar (I used this brand which is easy to find in the USA)
175g (1 1/2 cups) self-rising flour
1 tsp baking powder
1 tsp vanilla extract
1 lemon, zested
3 eggs
2 Tbs milk
4 Tbs strawberry jam
300ml heavy cream,, whipped
Blueberries
Red sprinkles or red sanding sugar

Directions:

1. Preheat the oven to 180℃/350℉. Grease and line 2 (21cm or 8 inch) cake tins.

2. Put the butter, sugar, flour, baking powder, vanilla, zest and eggs into the bowl of a mixer and beat until well combined. Add the milk and beat until smooth.

3. Divide batter evenly between the tins, smooth the top and put in the oven for 20-25 minutes until golden and a tester inserted into the center comes out clean.

4. Remove pans from the oven and set aside to cool for 5 minutes. Run a palette or rounded butter knife around the edge of the tin and carefully turn the cakes out onto a cooling rack. Set aside to cool completely.

5. To assemble the cake, place one cake upside down onto a plate and spread it with jam. Spread over half of the whipped cream. Top with the second cake, top-side up. Spread with the rest of the cream and sprinkle over the berries and red sugar.

Serves 8 to 10

review_headline: First I loved it Now I don't. Two stars because it's great for everyday cooking.
review_body:
I'm changing my star rating based on my apple pie filling which I made today. I'll try to take pictures to explain the review.
First I was very happy with Ultra Gel for replacing corn starch and flour in my daily cooking. Today I made apple pie filling according to the recipe I found on Cornaby's website. I should point out that I've been canning for 50 years, since I was a young girl. OK, the recipe is very basic - the usual suspects. When I started adding the Ultra Gel it l had to whisk like mad which was OK too. BUT the filling started to turn into dumplings. I finally got my immersion blender and whizzed the heck out of it and it smoothed out great. I'll also point out that I always follow a recipe to the 'T' the first time I make it. My old recipe called for 1 inch of head space and 25 minutes for quarts and pints in HWB canner. This recipe called for 35 minutes for quarts with 1/2 inch of head space. Imagine my surprise to open the canner and find a quart of apples floating in it. I started lifting the jars out of the canner and moving them to the towel and they started evacuating. and I have pie filling all over the kitchen. I guess I'll have to make half dozen pies for Hambone to eat because I surely can't put these up for the year in the pantry. I tried to do the pictures. Bummer. I just was telling Hambone I was going to buy the Cornaby cookbook. Nope. Not after this epic fail.
Mrs Hambone

product_title: Horizon Organic Super Squeeze Pouch, 4 Count (Pack of 6)
review_body:
This is essentially a yogurt in a squeeze pouch. 1/2 my kids liked it, 1/2 did not. Personally, I thought it was too sweet, although they kind of need it to be sweet in order to counteract the tangy-tartness that is also present. The overall flavor, in my opinion was fine, but not great. I'd eat it if I was hungry and there wasn't anything else around, but I'd likely choose something else first if that was an option.

The color is very unappetizing, but that's a good thing--it means they didn't add artificial colors to try hide it. Since you have to go out of your way to see the color, it doesn't really matter, anyway.

As I understand it, Horizon is a dues-paying member of the Grocery Manufacturer's Association (GMA) which has donated millions of dollars to campaigns to prevent mandatory labeling and as such, their whole "We're organic and we care about your health" thing is kind of lost on me.

Bottom line:
It's fine. I won't get it again--I'd rather give my kids lower sugar yogurts or perhaps applesauce in a pouch than this stuff.

product_title: Barney Butter Almond Butter
review_body: I decided to try this product based on a bunch of positive reviews and the fact that almond butter tends to be super expensive in groceries and health food stores. I am definitely disappointed after trying this out several times. The first thing I noticed was that the consistency was a bit weird - much stiffer than normal almond butter. It's almost like when you have regular almond butter on the sides of the jar that tends to dry out a little and it becomes more chunky - except I found the whole jar to be like that. It's difficult to spread and since I like to eat my almond butter with slices of apples, I ended up slapping a big unsightly chunk on there and having to take small bites from it as I make my way through the apple slice. The flavour was also disappointing - I figured it would taste similar to any roasted almond butter, however when I received the jar I noticed the ingredients list states "blanched roasted almonds". Not sure if that's why, but it definitely has a bland taste. If I want a sugar-free product I would be more satisfied with a raw almond butter that is literally just raw almonds. It's much tastier and smoother. I guess almond butter is a little more expensive for a reason - I would personally rather pay more for a product that I will enjoy.

I know I will be trying it on white fish with some capers and garlic, as I think this oil will be a nice complement to those flavors.  The Cornicabra oil has a more distinct almost spicy flavor with a bit of bitterness and a slightly almond/fruity aftertaste.  I made a decent salad dressing with it.  I haven't used to cook with the Cornicabra yet but am sure it'll find it's place in our house.  My plan is to try it in a marinade or in a sauce next.  This is coming from an every day wife and mom, who loves cooking and eating well.  While we have eaten at many highly rated restaurants and enjoy quality food, I am no means a professional critic. product_title: H P Sauce, 15-Ounce Plastic Bottles (Pack of 4)
review_headline: A classic sauce - still as good as ever!
review_body:
My wife and I both grew up in Great Britain and like in many British homes, this sauce was a staple item in our pantries and probably more popular than ketchup. Its a savoury, but mild, brown sauce that's made from a malt vinegar base, thickened with tomatoes, dates, tamarind, and other spices. It's delicious as a condiment to either hot or cold foods - we particularly like it on sausages (bangers), bacon or chips (fries), but it also makes a really good spread to liven up cold cheese or ham sandwiches. Its a bit similar to a brown steak sauce such as 'A1', but has a thicker, less runny consistency that clings better to food, like a good ketchup does.

My kids have grown to love it and frankly, a bottle doesn't seem to last for very long in our house! So the 425g (about 15 oz) size is best for us - plus, we prefer it in the squeeze bottle, which reduces that annoying little amount that usually gets stuck in the bottom of a sauce bottle! You can find this on the shelf at some U.S. grocery stores and pay more, but given this is imported, these seem to be a really good prices here for the quantities. If you shop around, you can also find variations from this 'original' flavour - such as 'HP Fruity' (sweeter, which I don't think is quite as good), 'HP Bold' (spicier) and 'HP BBQ'.

I noticed that some folks have complained that the expiration (or 'sell by') date on the bottle has passed, or is very close. Don't forget that Brits use a 'DD-MM-YYYY' format, not the 'MM-DD-YYYY' format used in the U.S. so that may be the reason. My recent order had an expiry date of
'08-01-2016', but whether that means August 1st or January 8th is a moot point in my house, as it will never last until either one!

A bit of trivia - as the image on the bottle suggests, the 'HP' stands for Houses of Parliament, where it was supposedly served since its introduction around 1900. And in the 1960's, it had a nickname of 'Wilson's Gravy' in Britain, as the then Prime Minister Harold Wilson apparently doused everything he ate with it!

So, are you buying a traditional, authentic British product here? Well not really any more, as HP Foods is now owned by Heinz and this sauce is made in the Netherlands. But fortunately, they don't seem to have messed with the recipe and it still tastes as good as ever to me!

product_title: Cafejo K-Cups
review_body:
Coffee preferences are very much individual tastes. One person's great brew is another person's swill. With that in mind, here's my review:

I enjoyed this Cafejo Signature Blend K-cup coffee a lot. I usually prefer a dark roast, but this medium roast seemed very full-bodied to me. It was also very mellow, without any bitterness at all. It tastes good black or with cream and sweetener.

The one and only downside is the price. It's up toward the higher end of the K-cup range. Is it worth it? Well, again, coffee preferences are very individualized. I personally think the quality justifies the price.

My bottom line: This is a very good coffee, the kind you sit on the patio and linger over. I recommend it very highly.

product_title: The Spice Lab's Pure Himalayan Salt - Finely Ground .5mm
review_body:
This is a good brand and has been my to-go brand for a while.
Recently I needed a replacement batch and ended up with another brand because price and quantity matter if the quality is the same.

I recommend this salt if you are on the market for Himalayan salt. I also recommend that you do your due diligence in price and quantity comparisons.

To help you out, I am listing the other salts I have purchased on Amazon based on price and quantity and only those I am equally satisfied with for your own comparison. (remember that prices change on Amazon frequently)

The Spice Labs (2 lb bags and (twice) 4 lbs bags) *based on price and quantity at the time, I have purchased this brand 3 times.
Sherpa Pink Himalayan Gourmet Salt. (very good too)
WBM Himalayan Himalayan Pink Salt with 84 Minerals - Fine Salt Naturally Pure, 2-Pounds (Pack of 3) - My original purchase of 3 lbs for $23.00 - for 6 lbs. Which I thought was expensive. Now, this salt is not available on Amazon, but available from some vendor for $45 plus $8.00 shipping and from what I am reading, you only get a 2 lb bag. Ridiculous!

The Spice Lab comes conveniently shipped in its own storage-resealable bag and it dissolves well in liquids and not much is needed to season dry foods. A little goes a long way.

product_title: Great Value Mango Drink Mix, 6 Count, 1.69 Oz (Pack of 2)
review_headline: DeeeLicious!  But it's $2 at the W-M store.
review_body: I didn't purchase this on Amazon, but at WalM- because it is $2 a box there.  Each individual packet mixes up 2 Quarts of drink and there are 6 packets in each container, so for $2, you get 3 gallons of a delicious drink...and I mean DELICIOUS!  This is the best drink mix ever!  I love, love, love, love, LOVE it!  It tastes just exactly like a cold, juicy, ripe mango.  If you have ever tasted a nice RIPE mango, I'm sure you love them.  If you've ever tasted a mango and thought it was disgusting, it probably wasn't ripe enough.  When they aren't ripe, they have a turpentine/pine taste.  Anyway, this drink mix is DELICIOUS, sweet, has none of that "you can tell it's artificial sweetener" taste.  But it IS sugar free!!  I sometimes mix this and other of the GV or Crystal Lite flavors half and half with lemonade for a variety lemonade, toss in a little fruit, serve in a large container or an infusing pitcher, and my friends and family are always impressed with my "recipes."  If you just throw in a little of this or the watermelon kiwi or the cherry limeade, no one is the wiser.  Add lemon or lime slices, kiwi or mango, ice it down, and you're good to go.  Nice summertime drinks that are sure to impress.  But I'd never pay $15 for a two pack!  Are people INSANE? Buy it at the Wally World store.  Oh, and the empty containers make wonderful little bento boxes for lunch boxes or little storage containers for all sorts of things.  I've used them in my toolbox, camping backpack, utility drawer, and let my grandkids make mini piggy banks with them.  The lids stay on well and they are the perfect size for all sorts of things.  I even have one in my desk at work with salt & pepper pkts and such in them so at lunch time, I have seasoning pkts handy.  Anyway, you cannot go wrong with this drink mix.  Matter of fact, I'm craving it now.

review_headline: Best for a prank, not a challenge
review_body:
After viewing an episode from YouTube star, Pewdiepie I took the challenge to try these deceptive jelly beans. I assumed Pewdiepie was over reacting the taste, but.... no.
I used these jelly beans as a challenge with my brother. We played Halo 4 on the highest difficulty and if one of us dies we randomly choose and eat a jelly bean (Man, did this teach true team work after tasting our first jelly bean). I died first and selected brown…. Chocolate pudding or canned dog food, both I don’t care for, but I assumed the worst in getting dog food and predicted it would taste like meatloaf or corn beef hash. NOPE! I started chewing rapidly for the first 3 motions till I stopped and noticed….. “Hell this is worse.” You’d want to throw up, but you can contain it, it’s like a heavy fertilized …IDK, but no. We looked through all the colors and found one black jelly bean… skunk spray or licorice…. Gave that to the dog and he spit it out multiple times. After my dog finished the jelly bean I smelt his breath (in Pewdiepie you can smell it)….and yep, fresh road kill skunk smell. We used mountain dew for the acid to wash away the taste, yet the flavoring is so deep in my gums I bought a professional tooth brush to abolish the dog food taste.
All in all, throw away the juicy pear/ grass clippings, both aren’t good. The white and blue are compatible. Blue is either berry or tooth paste (aahh tooth paste childhood memories, when I thought it was astronaut food). The white is coconut or baby wipes, which reminds me of powdered sugar.
The price is reasonable seeing the demand is so low. It’s the best to use this as a prank more than a challenge. The down side was there was only 5 out of the 22 jelly beans that were good.

product_title: Mission Low Carb Soft Taco Flour Tortilla's 12oz./8 Ct. (Pack of 6) by Mission Ltd
review_body:
As a low carb "lifestylist" and a diabetic, I'm always looking for guilt-free ways to cut out excess carbs from my diet. When these low carb tortillas first came out several years back, I did not like them AT ALL. I thought they were chewy, sweet, and even a little undercooked. But over the years, Mission has greatly improved the taste and texture of these tortillas. These tortillas make awesome fajitas, soft tacos, burritos, taco salads, tortilla chips, and EXCELLENT quesadillas. They're also great with refried beans or another low carb/low GI Mexican/Tex Mex side dish you can think of.

For anybody buying these tortillas here on Amazon or in the store, here's a tip on how to serve them: Heat up a pan or griddle and place a tortilla on the surface for about 20-30 seconds or until the bottom is in the early stages of crisping up. Then flip over and do the same thing with the other side. If you heat up these tortillas using a pan or griddle instead of a microwave (which in my opinion, only makes them soggy), I guarantee that they'll taste like they're homemade and not store-bought. If you serve them this way, you'll fool many people into thinking that they're just regular tortillas!

product_title: Colorado Spice Caribe Hot Jerk Spice, 32-Ounce
review_headline: This is a particularly amazing spice, and not too far from Walker's dry ...
review_body:
This is a particularly amazing spice, and not too far from Walker's dry which is a Jamaican standard for all jerk spice. While Walkers has a few more variety of peppers, the Colorado Spice version here concentrates a bit more on the Allspice side of things. This however, is quite acceptable since there are two theories of jerk found down in the island, based on heat. Both theories include high volumes of Jamaican whole allspice, as does this one where it is listed as the first ingredient. Each producer of jerk has their own recipe and this mimics several that I've tasted.

While this spice can indeed be used as a condiment, that is not it's primary purpose. It's purpose is meat! Chicken, beef, lamb, pork all do well with jerk spice. While you can apply this directly to the meat, the best way of pulling all that flavor into the meat is to mix the spice with a very light oil at least a couple of hours ahead of time. My preference is grape seed oil since it is so light and imparts no additional flavors. However, I have also used an olive oil and it works well too. Just leave it out at room temperature to allow the become infused with the spice mix, then apply it as a paste to the meat.

Liberally apply the paste to the meat a couple hours ahead of time for the best result, and then massage it in to help incorporate the spice paste into the surface of the meat. Then refrigerate the meat until about 15 minutes before putting it on the grill.

review_headline: Non GMO, organic, super food, super good!!
review_body:
If you are not familiar with Hemp protein let me tell you how great it is - if you are, skip this paragraph ;) Hemp is a great source of plant base protein. Its flavor is nutty like a combination of walnuts and hazelnuts - if you ask me. It is very filling and nutritious especially if you are on a vegetarian or any other restricted diet. It can be mixed with smoothies, shakes, baked goods, and if it is high quality you can simply sprinkle it on top of fruit. Full of nutrients and just one of those things that make you feel good about what you are consuming and putting in your body.

Now then, what makes this protein powder different than others? Well, besides being non GMO and organic, it is finely ground like the consistency of cornstarch. It is not chalky at all! It has a fresh nutty flavor. Some hemp powders are not as fresh and taste stale, but not this brand, it’s very tasty. Since it has a very powdery consistency, it is very easy to dissolve. You don’t necessarily need a smoothie blender, especially if you already have things pre-mixed like pureed fruit or just milk (any kind). Honestly, I simply sliced an apple and dipped it in the hemp powder. The hemp powder dissolved in my mouth so easily while I was chewing the apple, it tasted like apples with nut butter DELICIOUS!!

I recommend this Hemp protein powder to those trying to increase their protein intake, lose some weight, looking for a post workout shake, or even those who just want to have a more balanced snack during the day. Excellent price at the moment ~15 dlls for one pound.

product_title: Melissa's Fresh Lychees, (2 lb)
review_headline: if you haven't eaten fresh lychee, you are missing one of life's greatest pleasures.
review_body:
Eating Lychee is a spectacular pleasurable experience. If you've gone your whole life long without tasting lychee, you've missed one of the pure joys of eating. The glistening, luscious fruit lies within a thin scaly "skin." An ambrosial nectar spurts if you are too rough so be gentle to peel then quick to pop the whole interior into your mouth. Don't bite hard. Inside the fragile comestible is an inedible seed. Your mouth will know what to do to scrape off what is edible while your fingers find the next. So easy to remove the cleaned seed with one hand and pop in another peeled fruit to repeat the process.

The ONLY flaw with the fruit is its short "ripe" season. If you miss this year's harvest you MUST mark your calendar for April in the northern hemisphere. When lychee is out-of-season, I pine. No other fruit approaches the lychee for sheer pleasure. From sometime in April until the end of May/first week or so in June is all you can count on. When picked too green, the lychee are bitter. Picked to late...inedible. Picked and not handled properly, you don't want to know. You have to find a grower you can trust. I've found mine.

There are a lot of claims made for lychee in terms of medicinal use. I won't bore you with the claims "eating lychee cures all." I can attest to "eating lychee makes you leave your troubles behind."

http://www.fruitsinfo.com/fruit-facts/2012/02/health-medicinal-benefits-of-lychee/

The small withered seeds (as opposed to the normal fat seeds) are called "chicken tongue" seeds - not a particularly romantic name but those with tiny seeds yield the most flesh. (I've also seen it spelled litchi)

This year, I threw caution to the wind. I placed the order for 6 pounds of lychee determined to use the Amazon "satisfied customer" option. If I didn't like them I was sending them back with a nastygram. I received the box within24 hours of placing the order, a day earlier than expected. When I opened the box, clouds parted and I could hear triumphant music. Six pounds this season was 175 lychee. Of those marvelous morsels, only one was leaking and I ate it anyway as I figured the box cutter probably nicked it since it was "fresh" juice.

If you haven't eaten lychee before, do be tender with the seed. The seeds are said to be astringent and bitter. No point in ruining a sublime experience.

Bon appetit!!!

review_headline: It is not safe to surf the internet on an empty stomach.
review_body:
It is not safe to surf the internet on an empty stomach. I read of Lion on a list of best English candy bars and was intrigued to try it. This is not sold in stores in Canada, but I knew that Amazon would come through to provide easy access to unique and wonderful items from all over the globe! I placed my order for an assortment of different chocolate bars with Spellbound From England because their prices were good and they offered free shipping to Canada. One week later, my order arrived bubble wrapped and nicely packaged in a sturdy box. I was delighted to see that the chocolate was fresh and had six months to go before the expiration date. Five stars and a high five for the seller!

However, in this review I am rating the chocolate bar itself and since taste is very much a subjective preference, I would rate Lion three stars. It is a solid chocolate bar but did not make my toes curl in delight. I love chocolate bars with wafers and rice crisps in them. Unfortunately, the caramel made this chewier than I prefer, and it stuck to my teeth. The bar had a homogenous sweet, mild caramel flavour. I could not discern the taste of the individual wafer and crisp elements—they mostly added texture, not flavour. Lion reminds me of Mr. Big that we have in Canada, except that in the latter I could taste the individual wafer, crisps, peanuts and chocolate elements. I will stick with Mr. Big in the future, but I was glad to have tried Lion and my curiosity (and hunger) are now satisfied.

review_body:
I love drinking Matcha green tea because it has high amount of antioxidants. It also taste good specially the good quality one. I don't consider myself an expert in matcha green tea but I tried a lot of brands so far. You need to know its not always easy to find the best Matcha and comparing brands side by side will give you better idea. some tips you need to know 1- the origin, grades and which part of plants matcha comes from, color, taste and finally how to prepare each grade matcha.
There Isn’t any formal or universal grading system for matcha but will list the most common two grades I found.
- Ceremonial grade: Made from shade-grown green tea leaves harvested and then stone-ground to a very fine powder. Good for drinking straight and taste good.
- Ingredient/ culinary/ kitchen grade matcha which is best when used in recipes for matcha lattes, smoothies, shakes, ice cream, baking, etc. the taste is more strong and maybe bitter to maintain its aroma and flavor when mixed with other ingredients. You can also consume as a brewed drink with more bitterness than the ceremonial grade matcha if you don't mind that.
now for this brand "New! Authentic Japanese Matcha Green Tea Powder By Jade Leaf Organics" . Here what I found:
- The color of this Matcha green tea is brighter green compared to other culinary grades I have tried.
- The taste is less bitter compare to others. I tried drinking straight and the taste actually not bad! although I prefer the Ceremonial grade for cup of matcha.
- Powder: fine green powder.
- I tried it for lattes, smoothies, shakes, ice cream and baking and the results are great
this one stays on top of my culinary grade brands and really recommend it as kitchen grade matcha

review_headline: Does a good job of lowering blood pressure
review_body: This tea has quite a tart flavor, since it is simply hibiscus, nothing else added.  I started drinking it just over a week ago and was amazed by the results in lowering blood pressure, particularly how quickly this has worked. Within a day of starting with two cups per day, I noticed a drop of about 10 points systolic and 5 points diastolic.  After a few more days I would say systolic is down about 15 points and diastolic down about 10 points, which is exactly what I wanted.  I did attempt to drink it three times day to see if more would mean even lower numbers, however it's quite hard to fit three extra drinks into my day - given that I like to drink black tea two or three times as well, in addition to water!  As well as the bp lowering effects, I do find it quite a calming drink (which maybe has a bearing on its bp lowering quality).  I was making a hot cup of tea with one bag per 12 oz of water, but with the weather turning very hot today I tried something different.  I made the equivalent of two cups (24 oz water and two tea bags) this morning, drank one 12 oz cup of tea, then let the remainder cool down and put it in the fridge for the afternoon.  Then I poured that over ice for a refreshing drink later.  Although the flavor of this tea is rather tart, it is well worth the bp lowering effects so I shall continue to drink it.

product_title: Orbit Sugarfree Gum, Mint Variety Box, 12 packs -
review_headline: 2 Unique & Wonderful Flavors + Soft, Long-Lasting Flavor = Out-of-This-World Gum!
review_body:
So, you usually buy Trident or Dentyne, and you are wondering what's so special about this Orbit gum? Yeah, I used to be like you. It's just gum, right? And mint even. What could be so special about mint?

Well, let me tell you, this gum far exceeded my expectations on several fronts:

+ 2 Unique & Wonderful Flavors: In addition to 3 packs of Peppermint and 3 packs of Spearmint, you will be blown away by 3 packs of Wintermint and 3 packs of Sweet Mint. Both of these flavors are now favorites of mine.

+ Soft, Long-Lasting Flavor: Softer out of the wrapper than other gums, it stays softer as you chew it, and the flavor doesn't disappear in just minutes, like other gums.

+ Big Pieces: With other mint gums, I'm often tempted to eat two pieces at once, because they are such small pieces. Not here. These are generously sized pieces, and I never once thought of eating two at once.

+ Cool Reclosable Packaging: Each pack comes in a neatly designed, wallet-like paperboard package--perfect for your pocket or purse (or "murse" if you are a man). These folks know that you don't put a great product in cheap packaging. Kudos to them.

I still love my Altoids, but they have met their match now! Try it, and you will see. All gums are not created equal.

review_body:
Flahavans is a super creamy oatmeal with a great unique taste. Flahavan’s has been milling oats at the family mill in Kilmacthomas, Co. Waterford for over 200 years
There has been an oats mill at Kilmacthomas since the late 1700's. The power for the mill came from the nearby River Mahon which at one time also powered four other mills. In those days, the mill was used for the contract milling of oats for local farm growers and oat growers. This is where the farmer’s oats were then milled and the milled oatmeal was returned to him. He was charged for this service. At this time, the oatmeal was a heavier type than the Flahavan's "flaked" oatmeal we know today. In 1935 it was decided to expand the mill and to put in an oatflaking facility. Oatflaking produced a finer flake, which is faster to cook. By 1959, Flahavan’s completed the construction of its current mill building. The first family connection to the Flahavan’s name can be traced back to about 1785 when Thomas Dunn took over the mill. Dunn was the great-great-great-grandfather of John Flahavan who is the Managing Director of the company today. Flahavan's 100% Wholegrain Organic Rolled Porridge Oats are a standard oat used for oatmeal. Use these jumbo oats to help make the perfect oatmeal.
I found them very easy to prepare on the stove, but most of the time it's microwave.

review_headline: Great Coffee also Great Company for the cause of goodness
review_body:
Shuffle Bean Medium Roast Ground Coffee was provided by Shuffle Bean.
Shuffle Bean Coffee is a special blend of Arabica beans shade-grown in the fertile Tarrazu Region of Costa Rica. These rare beans, nourished on rich volcanic soil, are among the world’s most flavorful and aromatic. Shuffle Bean Coffee is from Rainforest Alliance Certified farms, helping protect the environment and ensure sustainable livelihoods for coffee-growing communities. Shuffle Bean is regarded as a superbly balanced coffee with flavors of tropical fruits and chocolate. Our medium roast has a heavy body, high acidity, and a sweet finish with no presence of an aftertaste. RAINFOREST ALLIANCE CERTIFIED
Shuffle Bean Coffee is from Rainforest Alliance Certified farms, helping protect the environment and ensure sustainable livelihoods for coffee-growing communities.
The small vents on bags allow for carbon dioxide to escape from the freshly roasted batches. The valve is one-way and does not allow oxygen, moisture, or other containments to stale the coffee. Without the vent, the coffee would react to oxygen exposure, which would cause the coffee to sour and change the flavor. Shuffle Bean is a new company, and committed to selling coffees that have a positive impact on the people who grow them, and on their environment. Not all coffees have much of an aroma, other than smelling of coffee how ever the aroma was unique a sweet and caramel surprise for the taste buds. Shuffle Bean is bold and strong. Very little bitterness, compared to other coffee and with a nice blend of that caramel sweetness and a hint of citrus. I have really enjoyed coffee again. I am going to try and make a cold drink from this coffee and hope I don't take from the great flavor of the coffee. I received this product for review and this is my honest option of this product

product_title: SweeTARTS Soft and Chewy Ropes Formerly Kazoozles
review_body:
I took this giant box of Ropes into a classroom and gave it out to 20 high schoolers to get their response. About half the group had tried Kazoozles in the past and they felt this new version with a new name was much better.

But, they still admitted that they only "liked" the Ropes, and couldn't see going out and getting them, versus buying Twizzlers or other plain red licorice. The SweeTarts middle of these hollow red Ropes is probably supposed to be the flavor boost that makes them unique. It's not very strong (sweet or tart) so it didn't make them much more exciting. Overall, the teens said these were only Okay.

Myself, and the other adults who tried these, found them a bit too sweet and artificial tasting...which is ironic, since the packaging emphasizes that they are naturally flavored and colored. Perhaps they are a slightly better candy treat than others which are made with a plethora of chemicals, but they certainly aren't health food and don't have an improved natural taste in my opinion.

For the SweeTart lover...there is not really enough of that tangy taste. And, for the red licorice lover, there is tastier red licorice out there. Not sure this combination is a winner.

product_title: PS Seasoning & Spices French Fry Seasoning Variety Pack 5.5 Ounces Each (5 Flavors); Steak Fry, Chili Cheese, Parmesan & Garlic, Buffalo Wing, & Sweet Potato - Gluten Free -No MSG - Add Great Flavor to Your Meals Without Adding Calories!
review_headline: Chili Cheese and Sweet Potato were good
review_body:
So when I got these, I HAD to try them all at once. Not together of course. I made a batch of fries and divvied them up so that we could try each flavor. Steak Fry, Chili Cheese and Sweet Potato were good. They were better than okay, but they were exactly what I expected when I saw them in the list of seasonings that were coming in this set. Chili Cheese speaks for itself. It simply tastes like Chili and Cheese is on your fries without all that added fat. Sweet Potato and Steak fry are both salty, and savory, and give added flavor to those plain ol fries. I was most excited to try the Parmesan Garlic and Buffalo Wing. I am obsessed with these flavors, and order them almost anywhere we go. Buffalo Wing did not disappoint. Do not go overboard with this, unless you like a lot of spice on your food. I started with a generous amount, and added more until it suited my 'heat' level. Very very good. You can have the wings without the wings so to speak. The Parmesan Garlic though, it will be my favorite. I will be ordering more of this when I run out! That's for sure! It's the perfect blend of Parm and Garlic, without being overly garlic as well. I've been putting this on everything. From french fries to chicken to popcorn. The flavor makes me crave more when I am done eating it! I highly recommend these seasonings for anyone who loves to cook.

I received these deeply discounted for the purpose of an honest review. All opinions are my own and are not influenced in any way!

product_title: Amy's Rice Macaroni and Cheeze, 8 Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_headline: who still remembers what real mac and cheese tastes like: First
review_body:
A review from a (recently) converted vegan, who still remembers what real mac and cheese tastes like:

First, I want to point out that bought this from a local store. I was shocked (and excited) that my local Kroger had expanded their vegan selection. I picked up quite a few things. This was one of them.

To be fair, I should also probably state I'm not the biggest fan of "imitations". Especially Daiya. Had I realized before hand that this was made from Daiya, I probably wouldn't have bought it. Alas, I have really been craving mac and cheese so I thought it was worth a try. It was around 4$ at my store so note a huge loss.

Upon opening the box, I was pleased to see that it looked a lot like the mac & cheese I remember! When it was cooked - it looked sort've like it too. Texture wise, it seemed to be about right. Maybe a bit too "cheesy", ironically. I had to add a bit of almond milk and (vegan) butter to make it actually creamy. It melted good, and was a cheese like texture. As far as the taste, I do think it tasted a bit like cheese. In honesty, I can't really put my hand on what was off. But something was. Maybe it was actually the rice macaroni, as I am not gluten free and usually just eat normal pasta. Whatever it was, it had a weird aftertaste. I put hot sauce on it (like I often did with real mac and cheese). With this, I was able to get through a few bites. But then it just got to be too much.

I feel as though if I already didn't hate imitations as much as I did, or if it had been a bit longer since I had real cheese, I would've probably eaten more of this. However, I ended up just giving it to my dogs. They seemed to love it! I think a lot was in my head, and if you're okay with other meat/cheese alternatives (especially daiya because that's what this uses), then I'd definitely give it a try. I would just suggest adding a little soy/almond/etc milk to make it creamier.

review_headline: One of the only honest sugar-free chocolates on the market.
review_body:
Got these for Mother's day for my weight conscious mother.

Unlike other chocolates which are "sugar free" and contain maltitol these achieve their mouth-feel with erythritol. That doesn't sound like a big deal to a lot of people, they're both sugar alcohols right? Wrong. Maltitol might as well just be regular sugar. It's got a huge glycemic impact and has 3/4rths the calories of regular sugar. Erythritol on the other hand is almost inert with around 5/100ths the calories of sugar and virtually 0 glycemic impact.

So it should be obvious that everyone would be using Erythritol right? Unfortunately all the big name sugar free candy makers instead use Maltitol so they can proclaim their candy sugar free. I think it's horrible they're basically fooling their customers who are relying on them for weight control.

ChocoPerfection took the high road and didn't do this. That is why they're one of the few sugar-free candies I can recommend to people struggling with glycemic control. The only downside is the price, but let's be honest you shouldn't be eating treats every day. I see myself buying these whenever a holiday comes around.

review_body:

review_body:
I use Figaro Hickory Liquid Smoke at home when I'm in a pinch, like when I'm unexpectedly out of wood, or cooking in the kitchen. It works well enough, although it has a salty-vinegary over-taste if you use a lot.

When I need just a dash, this works well, but any recipe needs less salt accordingly. Because it is liquid, compensate by reducing other liquids when possible. The liquid is mostly water and can leave your burgers sloppy.

Your best choice is real hickory wood. Figure out the timing and quantity for whatever dish, and go that route. If you are cooking inside, this is a good, but imperfect choice.

As for buying four 1 gallon bottles, this is great for church BBQs and small restaurants which don't specialize in smoking their meats, but want an extra boost.

anthonytrendl.com

You find out that one person doesn't eat red meat, another doesn't eat anything that once had a face, and another one is vegan that doesn't eat any animal or anything produced by an animal. One easy answer I found to this dinner dilemma is the Taco.

Verify for yourself, but I learned from a vegan hippy (hippy vegan?) friend that there are lots of store bought products that are \\"accidentally vegan.\\" That's why when I buy, instead of fry, taco shells, I buy Old El Paso's. Old El Paso's Taco Seasoning is on her vegan list too, as are the taco sauce and fat-free re-fried beans. She uses Old El Paso's meat seasoning to season the beans and something called \\"vegan ground meat.\\"

I like that this kit has both the corn and flour tortilla options. If any vegan friends had been over, the corn was available. As it was, everyone at the table this particular night had no limitations and could eat any and all of the El Paso kit items. I thought the shells were a tad smaller than those in the regular boxes of Old El Paso shells, but I was the only one.

A couple subjective improvement opportunities exist regarding the amount of spice. At our table, we all agreed that we'd have liked the option of upping the spice level and the heat in the meat seasoning mix. The taco sauce too seemed to be significantly toned downed and, for us, there wasn't enough. It could help to offer the kits in different \\"heat\\" levels.

Not a complaint, but more of a mystery of the universe, how is it that I've never bought a box of any brand of hard shells without finding at least one broken? It's as if each box must sacrifice one of its own for the others to live. Maybe Old El Paso could be the first to pack an extra shell to sacrifice itself. Or, the first to deliver 100% unbroken shells.

This kit is great to have in the pantry for a last minute dinner or a late night after party kitchen raid. I'd pick up Old El Paso's fat free re-fries and taco sauce too to be ready for any unknown vegan converts.minute dinner or a late night after party kitchen raid. Black Rice or Wild Rice blends work well when blended about 3:1. I first tried this Red Rice alone. It requires less water than most rice varieties (about one third less water) and it cooks more quickly. I use a RICE COOKER and it works very well. (If you're buying a rice cooker look for one with a Stainless Steel inner container - avoid non-stick "coatings" and aluminum). The flavor and texture of Bhutanese Red Rice are wonderful. I would ( no I WILL ) recommend this Bhutanese Red Rice to other people, mainly by serving it when I cook for them. A lot of folks it turns out think all rice is like that dead white stuff that comes from a box of Uncle Ben's Perverted Instant Rice. They're missing out... This red stuff is da kine!

review_body:
I live in Florida but I'm from CA and I really miss that San Francisco Sourdough bread. I was a little worried about this product being shipped in the heat but that didn't seem to affect it negatively at all. I got it started and it really took off! I fed it for 3 days and then I couldn't wait any longer... so I made some bread. I used a no-knead recipe and let it rise for 15 hours overnight. I've done this before with other starters and they have usually take 18 hours but this one was ready to be turned out at about 15 hours... in fact it was probably ready at 14.

After turning out, I let rise a 2nd time and again... it doubled in size quickly! Baked it up and it came out perfect! The taste is fantastic and I know it will be even more sour the longer I age my starter. I've got 2 jars of it in the fridge now. product_title: Soylent Powder 1 day (1 bag) (7 Bags / 1 white box)
review_headline: Tastes Like Exactly What It Is
review_body: I've been looking forward to trying this for a very long time and was really excited to receive it in the mail. I ordered the one-day pack on Amazon from the manufacturer (Rosa Labs) and received version 1.4. It was really thick for me, so i thinned it out with additional water. I know most people found the taste to be neutral, but for me it had the very strong distinct flavor that should be expected of a fortified soy beverage (i.e.: it smells and tastes almost exactly like baby formula). For me, that made it pretty unpleasant. So if you're one of the handful of people who think tofu has a strong taste and smell, keep in mind that this will have a similar background flavor. However, most people won't even notice and will find it perfectly neutral. At the end of the day, I could probably get used to it over time, but a 2000 calorie serving is far too much for a woman my size. Think i'll try one of the recipes online to make my own non-gmo, non-soy version.

product_title: Russell Stover Sugar Free Strawberry Cream, 3-Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_headline: TASTY BUT BEWARE OF ADVERSE EFFECTS
review_body: My favorite piece of the Russell Stover boxed candies is the one with the strawberry fluff. Russell Stover also makes this same variety at Valentines Day in the shape of a heart and Easter in the shape of an egg. I love this stuff! So when I found these in sugar free I was excited to try them. My expectations weren't off-the-charts because it's very difficult replicate candy in a sugar-free version. I had the box sent to my work so the chocolate didn't melt on my doorstep waiting for me to arrive home. I immediately opened the bag. To my disappointment the strawberry fluff was more like a soft strawberry taffy. It wasn't what I expected but still good. I ate three (bite size) pieces between 9 and 11 a.m. I went to lunch at noon, came back, and had a sudden attack of diarrhea. I thought it was odd since I hadn't eaten anything that would give me diarrhea - so I thought. I no sooner got back to my desk when I had to turn around and practically sprint back to the bathroom for round 2. I'd heard several years ago that sugar-free candy can give you diarrhea but had never experienced it nor have I ever eaten 3 pieces of sugar free candy in one sitting. After round 3 I got on the internet and sure enough it's the Alcohol Sugars that cause the explosive diarrhea for SOME people. It's now 2:15 and my gut is still racing. I'm certain round 4 is eminent. I bought TWELVE bags of these little tasty "laxatives". Too bad I don't have a colonoscopy scheduled!

product_title: CedarHouse Ultra-Premium Liquid Smoke: All Natural Hickory Liquid Smoke - 4 FL OZ
review_headline: Love it! Love it! Love it!
review_body:
Love it! Love it! Love it!

I'm so glad I bought this. The main reason I chose to try this brand over others was not only the reviews here at Amazon, but it’s been recommended by numerous chefs, and even doctors trying to get people to eat healthy (no meat). It took me several days of reading reviews and researching the safety of "smoke" in a bottle, but I pulled the trigger and I'm glad I did.

The smell and taste is perfect - just like bacon or baked ham hock. And a few drops goes a long way (making it well worth the $12 price). Plus it's sodium free, 100% natural and safe (just natural wood smoke flavor that absorbs into water). No additives, no artificial flavors, no artificial colors or preservatives, No MSG, and made in the U.S.A.

I've used it several times to make mock ham & bean soup (no ham, but tastes like it has ham, see photo). It allows me to make healthy soup, hearty and full flavored, without the fat from ham. This also makes it perfect for vegetarians and vegans who miss the flavor of smoked meats but don't want to actually eat meat. If you want my recipe for mock ham & bean soup, feel free to ask.

Next I'll try making my own mock hot dogs and bacon (from carrots). When I do I'll be sure to post photos and offer my recipes.

review_headline: Great rice flour but some problems
review_body: I used this flour for over a year and thought it was great. It does bake great cakes, pies, pastries, etc  and you don't even need to use starches with many recipes just straight rice flour. Then one day I purchased some from a local asian store and I found bugs in my bag of rice flour even though it did not expire for at least 5 months. I figured it was just the asian store that maybe didn't store them properly. I really like this flour so I decided to order from reputable online asian grocer and again they had a expiration date that was beyond a year and the first few bags seemed fine but then one day after opening a bag and sifting through the flour I found a worm in the bag. I decided to stop using this and just buy the Authentic foods or stick to Bob red mills and I have not had any more bug problems.  Again this flour is great but beware to check your flour or maybe I just got a few bad batches last year I don't know. I did recently buy this brand of sweet rice flour because I could not find any other sweet rice flour and so far my bag has been good and now I store it in my freezer.

product_title: Carolina Gold Nuggets Microwave Pork Puffies Bake-N-Puffs, Original, 16 Ounce
review_headline: Health, Taste, Quality.  Pick any Two.
review_body:
They're really just OK. Nothing special.

You do need a stronger microwave, or cook them for a longer time, otherwise you're going to have many unpopped pork rinds.

They certainly _taste_ healthier than your typical pork rind! Much less fat, much less oily, much less salty. Unfortunately, also much less taste. I read one reviewer write that this had an abundance of porky flavor. I found quite the opposite. The pork flavor is slightly muted. On the other hand, if you're on a keto diet, you're probably going to die of a heart attack at 65 anyhow. Might as well use these as your go-to snack and die at 70 instead (hey -- no disrespect... I'm going to die right with ya!)

As with all microwave pork rinds, no need to add oil. You literally put them on a paper towel and nuke them. I nuke them for 2-2.5 minutes, but that number will definitely depend on your microwave.

I've found that scattering them on the paper towel is helpful in getting them to pop. If you space them out far enough, you tend to get a much higher pop rate.

I've also tried the bag method of cooking these, and it was less than satisfactory. It sounded like a good idea, but like 99% of all good ideas, it simply doesn't work.

They lose their heat quite fast. This is because a) you pop them "out in the open" instead of in an enclosed bag, like you do with most other pork rinds, and b) they're not drenched with oils with high heat capacity that pork rinds usually have. They'll become room temperature within 30 seconds.

However, this isn't necessarily a bad thing. Another thing I don't like about this pork rind is that it's not really crispy. Oh, yeah, sure, it's a little crispy. But compare it to any other pork rind, and it's almost mushy in comparison. If you wait until they've cooled down to room temperature, you'll get a much crispier / crunchier rind. Hot or crispy. Choose one.

product_title: Domaine des Vignes 52001 7 oz. Whole Grain Mustard, Pack of 6
review_headline: Excellent hot mustard with a creamy mouth feel
review_body:
This excellent mustard was contained in a Paris Box sent to me by trytheworld.com. Amazon apparently does not offer this company's ware -- boxes of fine foods from different locations around the world. Based on the Paris and the Morocco boxes, this is an excellent source of interesting foods, and something of a cultural travelogue to boot -- highly recommended.

trytheworld: "The origin of mustard production in France dates back to the Roman Empire who exported the mustard seeds to Gaul, centuries BC. Vineyard Domaine des Vignes uses vinegar produced from its grapes as a base for the mustard. Enjoy this mustard with charcuterie, with roasted meat, or as a dip.

The mustard is on the hot side, quite smooth mouth feel, with the whole grains of mustard made very soft by the addition of the hulls. Delicious in egg drop soup and on a Romaine and bacon sandwich. I believe these are Whole Grain, with mustard seed hulls folded in enhancing the tender crunch. The mustard comes from Dijon; Dijon is famous for Dijon mustard which originated in 1856, when Jean Naigeon of Dijon substituted verjuice, the acidic "green" juice of not-quite-ripe grapes, for vinegar in the traditional mustard recipe.

Robert C. Ross
April 2015

product_title: Sticky Fingers Scone Mix (Pack of 2) 15 Ounce Bags – All Natural Scone Baking Mix
review_body:
I was looking for something a bit different to serve with tea for a small group book study I was hosting. I saw these (and knowing the group usually loved to purchase scones in restaurants when available) and decided to give them a try. I was quite pleased. They were easy to whip up - only add water - and they baked up quickly. I used the method of just dropping them on the cookie sheet. I didn't butter the sheet as recommended, but used a silicone baking mat which made clean up quick. The scones turned out beautifully and were very light. I offered lime curd and tangerine marmalade to put on them. They were so good, the group asked to see the bag so they could purchase it themselves.

I am not a cook, nor do I have much interest in spending loads of time in the kitchen, and these were great with little effort on my part. Will definitely be purchasing again.

Note: If you are not familiar with scones, they are not a very sweet item, so don't expect something along the lines of banana breads or blueberry muffins which are much, much sweeter.

They're delicious, which is something that is commonly lost in protein bars, however you should know what you're buying. When things seem too good to be true they often are. While they taste great, there is a decent amount of sugar (and 190 calories) and not a ton of protein for something that's marketed as a protein bar.

If you don't need that much protein but are looking to work more into your diet, this is a fine product. If you are exercising moderately or heavily, or are very active and need to work a lot more protein into your diet I would look for an alternative. Otherwise, an overall great product.

review_body:
[[VIDEOID:e696e011066d4189ea00f698e41debda]] ...it's CONTROL, more on that later.

Kosher salt has become a beloved staple in most kitchens, and with good reason.
Many sea salts have a briny taste that is desirable in many dishes. Sea salts come in a near endless array of subtleties and flake size, as well as color.
Kosher salt has a fresh clean taste without the 'sea' element. It is consistent and contains nothing to add or detract except pure salt taste.
It's also a huge plus in terms of health. The crystals are larger than table salt, and that means you get the feeling of the food being salty, you get all the satisfaction, but you are actually ingesting less sodium.
When making bread, right before it goes into the oven, my breads get an egg wash and a sprinkle of salt (and sometimes a mix of seeds like poppy and sesame) on top. Kosher and sea salt is excellent because it looks beautiful and won't disappear on the bread. For meat rubs and roasted vegetables, Kosher is King.

Now why this particular Diamond Crystal salt?
In my opinion, in many cases (not all) it is superior to the familiar blue boxed brand.
Because of CONTROL.
First, the consumer friendly container has a perfectly designed pour spout. There is a small 'lip' that makes for precise pouring. It is as easy to have precision with this container as it is to dip your fingers in your salt cellar, and this packaging is a lot more sanitary.

Second, the size of the crystals. Small enough to be more targeted than the blue brand, yet large enough to still have the qualities you buy Kosher salt for, that is the ability to not melt down and disappear, and offer a pure salt taste. If the video isn't showing on your device, feel free to leave a comment and I'll give you the YouTube link.

Why else choose this one? The blue box salt contains yellow prussiate of soda, an anti-caking agent. Diamond Crystal doesn't contain any additives.

product_title: Glico Pocky Parent2
review_body:
I've long heard of Pocky, but somehow I just got around to trying it. After my experience I'd describe them as ultra thin cookies dipped in strawberry coating. My boyfriend aptly observed that the coating reminded him of the strawberry coating on ice cream bars and it's a great description. It's a creamy, melt in your mouth coating with an artificial, but still pleasant, strawberry flavor. I like that these are only lightly sweet as I find most American packaged cookies to be cloying. However, for people who like a sweeter dessert I could see these not being sweet enough. I found that because these are less sweet it is easier to eat a lot of them than most conventional packaged desserts, which can be a blessing or a curse. I also appreciated that these arrived with minimal, if any, broken pieces.

As far as the size of the individual boxes go, these reminded me a bit of the size of movie theater candy. The boxes are bigger than what I would normally consider a single serving, but too small to be family sized. It's more than I would put in a child or even grownup's lunchbox, but perfect for sharing or coming back to on a couple different occasions. The only downside is that the box didn't seem to have any noticeable tab to close the box after opening it.

Overall as someone who likes desserts that aren't overly sweet I found these hit the spot and definitely would seek out other Pocky flavors to try.

The molasses is thick and while pouring it comes out of the bottle slowly.  In order for the company to efficiently package the product, molasses is added to the plastic container while hot.  Placing hot molasses into plastic is a haven for leaching.  Whether plastic is BPA free or not, all plastics leach.  I am concerned how healthy the product is with chemicals from the plastic leached into the molasses.  How much leaching, who knows?  Why take the chance?  Until Wholesome Sweeteners places their molasses into lead-free glass containers, I will be purchasing a different brand.

product_title: Healthworks Chia Seeds 3lb 6lb Parent
review_headline: Awesome deal for this little superfood!
review_body:
I've been eating chia seeds for about 2 years now; mainly in chia pudding, but also in chia jam (using the chia gel in place of pectin), in smoothies, or in my low-carb version of oatmeal, or, as I like to call it, "Fauxtmeal". I used to only be able to find chia seeds at stores like Whole Foods, where I had no choice but to pay the Whole Foods price. Recently, chia seeds are EVERYWHERE, from Walgreens to Wal-Mart.

Even stores like Wal-Mart can't beat HealthWorks price. I've bought the cacao powder from HealthWorks before and been completely satisfied, and the same is true for the chia seeds. I like that they are pesticide/chemical-free, and the price is impossible to beat, even when buying chia seeds from the bulk bins at local natural shops.

The resealable package is nice, but I keep my chia seeds in a wide-mouth quart mason jar with a plastic screw lid. That being said, the seal on the bag is nice and strong, and the plastic material thick, so don't be afraid of spills.

Pro tip: If you ever spill chia pudding/gel all over your clothes, scrape as much off as possible before tossing everything in the washer/dryer. These little buggers get EVERYWHERE and are a colossal pain to fish out of the dryer trap.

review_headline: Freeze-dried Instant Coffee that is OK
review_body:
This is a review of Cafe Tastle Freeze Dried Instant Coffee, 3.5oz jar. I was provided with a free sample for review.

I'm a coffee lover and can't think of too many reasons why I'd drink instant coffee instead of freshly brewed coffee. But there are a few instances where instant coffee can come in handy. I'll take some when going on my backcountry canoe trips and it is also useful in some cooking or smoothie recipes that call for coffee.

This coffee tastes to me like so many other freeze dried instant coffees that I've had over the years. Nothing particularly jumps out at me as making this any better than, let's say Nestle's Freeze Dried or Starbucks Via (my favorite instant coffee).

Nothing is particularly terrible about this freeze-dried coffee as it compares to other brands and nothing jumps out to make it clearly superior to others in any way that I can perceive. It's just a typical freeze-dried coffee as far as I am concerned. I do like that the 3.5oz jar was glass rather than plastic.

If instant coffee is your thing, this should probably please you. It'll do when I can't make freshly brewed coffee.

***UPDATE (8/01/15)***
I initially gave this coffee 5-stars. The first bag of beans I received was just outstanding. When I reordered, the next batch was unpalatable. review_body: This was my first time trying Fog Chaser.  After reading so many positive reviews, I must say I had higher expectations.  It's not a bad taste, but it's not as bold and complex as I prefer.  Fog Chaser is a dark roast, but not a particularly strong one.  It doesn't have much depth or complexity, and is more of a singular note.  Even using the smallest cup setting on my Keurig, it doesn't take much creamer to lighten it, which tells you that it's not a very strong brew.  However, this company is a wonderful company that really "thinks" and cares for it's consumers.  The coffee came packaged well in non-frustration packaging.  Within the box, you get 8 separate sealed pouches of coffee pods (each pouch contains 10 pods), which allows you to open one pouch at a time to preserve the coffee's aroma.  The company also includes a plastic cup with a lid so you can store a single pouch of pods to retain freshness.  How brilliant to give us a storage container; sure comes in handy.  In the box, you will also receive an adapter for use with the Keurig 2.0, should you happen to have that model.  So while the coffee's taste did not meet my taste expectations 100%, I will continue to drink it for awhile based on it's value, and the caring and environmentally conscious company that manufactures it.

product_title: Bell Plantation PB2 Powdered Peanut Butter
review_body:
I LOVE THIS STUFF!!!! I originally discovered this stuff in my local Safeway. Unfortunately, I had only been able to find it in a 6.5 ounce size for $5.99. The smaller size went fast and the cost a bit pricey. ENTER the 1LB size I bought on Amazon and WHAT a deal.

The great thing about this stuff will become apparent to you if you compare the number of calories from fat in regular peanut butter versus this powdered peanut butter. The difference is astounding. I love peanut butter, but before this product I really had to make regular peanut butter a very occasional treat because there is just so many calories from fat in regular peanut butter.

Here's a helpful hint for anyone out there that loves peanut butter BUT gets some gas-distension after eating it: If you have this problem (like I do) you don't have to give up peanut butter. Before you eat it,,, chew on some Beano tablets first,,, wash it down and then consume the peanut butter - no problem for me after using the Beano first. What made me think of trying the latter was after reading that a so-called 'peanut' is NOT a nut at all, but a member of the legume family (beans, etc). When you think about the peanut, it makes sense that it is really like a hard shelled bean with the pods inside the casing. Anyway, try the Beano thing if you are a peanut lover (butter or just the peanuts themselves) but have the gas-distension problem when consuming peanuts,, and you can eat away! :)

review_body:
I know little about Ayurveda, "the 5,000-year-old wisdom of healthy living," so I am reviewing this simply as a dinner choice.

The spices are pleasant. I would buy again. The packet makes a surprisingly large amount.

However, I quibble with the cooking instructions, which start with "2-1/2 -- 3 cups water." That kind of imprecision will not do for Americans. In my absence, the first packet was prepared by a household member, and came out mushy.

Here's my method: Bring three cups of water to a rolling boil on the stove. Add product. Bring to a boil again, cover pot. Turn burner OFF and remove pot. After 15 minutes, remove lid and stir. If too wet, cover again.

For those who like to know, I have copied out the ingredients: Basmati rice, split mung beans, mustard seed powder, cumin seed powder, coriander seed powder, sesame seed powder, sea salt, succanat (raw sugar), asfoetida, and turmeric.

Which are all good things.

product_title: Kabrita Goat Milk Toddler Formula
review_body:
I breastfeed my son until six months old. At that time, he was diagnosed with a dairy intolerance. I was asked to change my diet to accommodate his needs. I made the appropriate changes so that he would be happy. I found it extremely hard to eliminate dairy completely from my diet due to the fact that milk is in everything! I did not want to give up breastfeeding completely, but I wanted to supplement with something that was organic, gmo free, and the first ingredient wasn't corn syrup.

Before I found Kabrita, I went through every formula trying to find one that my son would take with ease. This was no easy task and it wasn't a cheap task at all. After tons of trials and hundreds dollars down the toilet, I started to research goat milk formulas. Kabrita met my requirements and it also was the closest formula to breast milk on the market.

My son was on Nutramigen as a supplement until he was ten months old per the allergists recommendation. Nutramigen stinks (literally), it tastes disgusting, and it stains everything. On top of that, it's the furthest thing from breast milk you can find on the market. It made me sad to think that this was my only option.

I would like to tell you that Kabrita is an outstanding product for children with a dairy intolerance. It contains lactose, so it would not work for children with lactose intolerance. I weaned my son at 10 1/2 months and started him completely on Kabrita. He loves it. It's the only formula that he will take with ease. I know that the package states that it is for toddlers 12 -24 months, but when your options are limited you need to compromise on something. I chose not to compromise on quality of ingredients.

Thank you to Amazon for selling this item. Thank you to Kabrita for making a product that has been so successful with my child. My only issue is that I wish the formulas for younger babies were sold in the USA. Kabrita needs work on opening the market to other countriesoutside of Europe. I sincerely hope that this review help parents to takes the steps required to help their allergy journey to be successful.
