review_headline: Great flavor, with a medium level of heat
review_body:
This turns out to be a nice way to add a little heat to your food.

A few notes, to help you figure out if this is right for you...

* The heat is not overpowering (no need to reach for a glass of water to cool your mouth), but is noticeable. I enjoy it on hard-boiled eggs, but it takes a couple bites before I begin to notice the heat.

* The taste is recognizable as jalapeno (jalapeno is the second ingredient). So, if that is the particular flavor you are after, you might like this.

* This is a seasoned salt. If you are looking for the taste and heat of jalapeno, but don't want the sodium, you would want to look somewhere else.

product_title: Dryden And Palmer Old fashioned Rock Candy Amber Sugar Crystals, 5lbs Box
review_body:
I purchased Dryden and Palmer Old-fashioned Rock Candy Amber Sugar Crystals in the 5lb box as per a review on this item page that compared it to [[ASIN:B001L048WO Teavana Perfectea Rock Sugar (1 lb)]] that I have enjoyed for many years. Perhaps there is a similarity to the size and shape of this product as one of the other reviewers points out. However, the color is significantly different and the taste doesn't compare favorably at all.

The Dryden and Palmer product does not replicate the taste of the Perfectea Rock Sugar by Teavana. I have sampled the same tea sweetened by both products and there is a marked difference. The Dryden and Palmer product simply isn't as good. It does not bring out the flavor of the tea as the German rock sugar does, it changes the taste to sugar water. Ugh! In a contest between beet sugar and cane sugar--beet sugar wins.

In addition, upon receiving this product, I was appalled to see that the box did not contain a plastic sealed bag holding the product in check for deliver. Instead, the sugar had leaked all over the delivery box as the product packaging is merely tied with a white bakery string. While I might make a concession and purchase a product in this way from a bin and a salesclerk, receiving such a helter-skelter mess in the mail put me off immediately. I question the packaging from a sanitary standpoint--who handled it, etc. Not thrilled.

Bottom line? I doubt I will use the Dryden and Palmer sugar crystals at all; I am angry with myself for trusting a reviewer's opinion. This product does not compare at all with Teavana's exemplary product. Not recommended.
Diana Faillace Von Behren
\\"Buzzard's Eye View\\"

product_title: San Francisco Bay One Cup
review_headline: Wish these were even more eco friendly.
review_body:
My husband likes these, but says he prefers Donut Shop coffee... However, they're good enough that he says he will start drinking these instead to be more environmentally friendly.

The box came with a special attachment for a 2.0 Keurig machine so these will work in it (Keurig apparently built the 2.0 so you can't use other brands). We have a Cuisinart machine and the machine worked fine without it.

I do wish these were more environmentally friendly. There's a plastic rim, and I'm not sure what the top is made of. As such, I'm sure most of these will decompose better in a landfill than a normal k cup but I want to compost these so I think it'd be better if there was a pull tab on the top to peel the top off... Or a pull tab to pull the plastic ring off. Directions to compost these would be great to have on the box. To compost I used a cutting board, placed my cup on it sideways and cut off the bottom portion which should all be compostable (see picture). Coffee is good for my garden so I'm happy. I feel like the plastic ring makes these less that 97% biodegradable. I'd say 75%.

Also, in the box they include a big plastic cup to place all of your used cups in. I think they should take that out and recommend people upcycle a used plastic (or better, glass) container in their home. It's not an attractive cup and it's not necessary so it makes no sense why it's included in an Eco friendly product.

Please make a chai latte version of these.

Update: Just noticed the plastic container says it's 100% compostable. I wasn't aware that plastic could be compostable.. I'm not editing my post because I probably wouldn't put it in my compost/garden.

Stale as a 7 month old Cheese ball you'd find behind you're oven and tasted nothing like a pure Shew. That is not the frightening part or the reason for this well deserved rating. The next 2 months that followed these 2 handfuls of human eradication "things-in-a-bag" were unbearable to some. I crapped constantly and had itchy butt syndrome so bad I might as well have wiped my bum with poison oak, and had a feather lightly rub it for hours. No amount of scratching, wipes, powders, or even pleas for help were an answer. And Charmin's got a review on their Ultra Soft is coming, because it wasn't soft enough. Nothing was. Beware and Ignore.

Rapsblumen, or rape flower, is also known as canola, a marketing term to overcome the unpleasant English name. This honey is sweet, as is all honey, but not sugary like most honey. It has a mild sweetness and a strong savory element. It is a creamy honey, not a clear honey, so don't expect the typical translucent liquid...it is far more opaque.

product_title: Orville Redenbacher's Popcorn
review_headline: Solving the coating process, one bag at a time
review_body: The microwave caramel popcorn is messy, challenging to mix well, and MY WEAKNESS. Deliscious treat! The box instructs you to pre-pop the corn in the bag, open it, lay the slab of caramel on top, put it back into the microwave, and cook some more. THIS IS DIFFICULT, as the caramel makes the bag top-heavy and it's CARAMEL which means when that bag flops over (and it will), you have a mess. Two methods of cooking I have tried that work: (1) rest your upright bag of cooked popcorn in a microwave-safe dish capable of preventing your bag from falling over, or (2) cook the caramel slab in a mug and pour over your cooked popcorn, stiring quickly if it's in a bowl, or close the bag and shake it around while it's hot. This ensures a more even coating, fewer clumps.

review_headline: wonderful base for a vegetarian broth, other good Better Than Bouillon flavors available
review_body: I use the Better Than Bouillon options to flavor soups, rices, and other dishes (pot pies, vegetables, etc.).  I often use the no-chicken, no-beef, and the vegetable bases.  My favorite option by this brand is the no-chicken base, but the vegetable base is a good substitute for the no-chicken.  The Better Than Bouillon is a soft mixture - spreadable if you insisted on it being so - that can be mixed with water to create large amounts of broth.  However, I do not always mix the substance with water.  When cooking rice, I often just mix a couple of teaspoons into the rice to add some flavor.  It is very much possible to get this product at a more economical price.  Many Giant Eagles sell it, but also online stores like Iherb.  Use code LEK375 at Iherb for a discount.

product_title: CalNaturale Svelte Organic Gluten Free Protein Drink
review_body: These are just amazing for me. I'm one of those people who doesn't like to *eat* anything for the first couple hours I'm awake (anything other than liquid unsettles my stomach) and I'm also really busy, but I know I need something especially since I often workout before lunch. These shakes have really helped me so much. I keep 12 of them in the fridge and grab one as I'm out the door in the morning for work to drink on the way...they keep me full until around 2pm (I drink them between 9:30-10:30). Also, they are delicious...I've made protein shakes before, and these are, thus far, my favorite shakes and BONUS I don't have to make them. They *are* a little sweet, but I don't mind that as I'm usually following it up with black coffee; they are also very creamy...like drinking whole milk or even half and half. One of my favorite things is no aftertaste. Mouth tastes a little sweet for a couple minutes after finishing it, but then there isn't that grossness that settles (like with other drinks) that you breathe on people. I've struggled with eating disorders my whole life and this really helps me regulate to make sure I'm getting the nutrition I need...and the little phrases on the front are a nice little bit of positive reinforcement...really thoughtful.

product_title: Udi's Gluten Free Large Tortillas (Case of 10)
review_body: My husband and I love Udi's gluten free tortillas! Purchasing by the case through Amazon is less expensive than buying in a store, at least where we live. Immediately store them in the freezer, pull one package out at a time and store in refrigerator. NOTE: These are NOT good eaten "as is". They must be heated. I usually throw them in the oven at 375º for a few minutes to soften them and then make burritos or quesadillas, put back in the oven bake for 15 min. If you have a gas stove, they are also really good if you heat them on a gas burner, being careful to flip regularly so that they don't catch fire. I'm sure they would also be excellent heated on a BBQ, but we live in a condo building in a big city where that is not an option for us. Anyway, a large complaint seems to be the gummy texture--by heating as mentioned, you will find the gummy texture not nearly as noticeable and that these are by far the closest thing out there to a "traditional" flour tortilla.

product_title: Homebrew Lemon-Lime Soda Pop Concentrated Extract, 2-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 3)
review_headline: I find that this makes a good substitute for the sodastream diet lemon lime syrup
review_body:
I use this, homebrew lemon lime concentrate, all the time with my sodastream. Using an empty sodastream syrup bottle, I put in 1 tablespoon of the lemon lime home brew concentrate and, for diet lemon lime soda pop, 1 1/2 teaspoons of either liquid stevia or liquid nutrasweet sweetener, then fill rest of the bottle with water. I believe that other reviewers might have used the guidelines for mixing included in the homebrew box , which results in a bitter and much too strong mix. I sometimes also add 1 1/3 teaspoon of citric acid to my homemade diet soda mixture. I find that this makes a good substitute for the sodastream diet lemon lime syrup, which has become very expensive, and, where I live at least, difficult to find in the stores, and which is almost always very expensive when bought through Amazon.

As an aside, I have used other homebrew flavors, and find that the root beer recipe included in the concentrate box is pretty much on the mark for taste. It seems that it is only the lemon lime flavor that is much too strong when using their instructions...a good thing from my perspective, since it means that I get three or more batches from one bottle of the lemon lime flavoring.

review_body: I love this ghee!!  Is a bit granular in texture, but as a previous reviewer stated, it smooths out when it melts and is considered a sign of good quality ghee. I use it in cooking, and since it is clarified, meaning containing no milk solids, it does extremely well at high heat. I also use it in baking, and it does beautifully.  Over hot popcorn... fantastic and really, I've never found anything that it CAN'T be used for.  I know there are questions about it being from grass-fed cows, and in a perfect world, all cows would be 100% grass fed and we would all have access to these products.  However, the cost of 100% grass fed is prohibitive for a large segment of the population, so this product fills that gap beautifully. It is definitely more economical than making my own, which gives you only about a 75% return on a pound of butter when you make ghee. As to stability, I always keep it in a cupboard, lid tight and with no exposure to light. It keeps its freshness from the time I open it to the last bit scraped from the jar. I am very grateful to Nanak for producing this ghee and for Amazon for offering it at a good price.

product_title: Giant Reese’s Milk Chocolate Peanut Butter Cups Candy Bar Valentines
review_headline: An experience you'll want to take back
review_body:
Forget a snack - eating this is a complete journey. Just not a good one.

Imagine, if you will, trudging through a shell of chocolate thick enough to crush a man's skull. If you are strong enough and love chocolate enough to get through that, you have miles and miles of salty peanut butter to get through. Due to the sheer size of the product, you seem to get everything alone, in high definition. For the first time, you can experience the peanut butter as dried out wet cat food (in texture, appearance, and smell) and the chocolate as just plain regular Hershey's chocolate, and not the elevated experience you get in the normal cup, where every bite contains both. You know those commercials "you got your chocolate in my peanut butter! you got your peanut butter in my chocolate!" This is like you play that commercial backwards, find them completely separate, and expect the same result.

On top of that, how do you even eat it? The cup is the size of a small personal pie, and I attempted to try a knife and fork, only to meet with failure. Eating it with your hands causes the chocolate to melt. Pick your poison.

I'd give it a one star, but I'm sure that someone somewhere is the type who likes to eat the chocolate and peanut butter separately. If so, this is the product for you. Happy diabetes.

product_title: Y.S. Eco Bee Farms Raw Honey - 22 oz
review_body:
Mostly, I try to buy honey from small producers who are located in pristine areas. I much prefer that the honey be from wildflowers located far away from where any agriculture is, because I feel like it must be the case that the chemicals in conventional agriculture will make their way into the honey.

I do think that raw honey is preferable to honey that has been heated, because of the preservation of the nutrients. But to my understanding, if honey has not gotten to temperatures below about 55 degrees, it will remain liquid. All things being equal, I prefer to buy items in class jars, though I will accept plastic if necessary.

This honey does not say where it was producer or what kind of flowers the bees had access to. It just states "Harvested by healthy bees from eco friendly diverse regions." The honey is totally solid in the container, which means that it has not been kept warm. And it is in a plastic jar.

It tastes fine. Not as clean and pleasant as some honey I've had, but certainly edible. I finished the whole jar without finding it objectionable.

The price ($10 for 22 ounces) is pretty reasonable compared to what I consider to be good honey.

I'm not sorry I bought this honey. Probably of what is available on Amazon, this is one of the better choices.

There are two kinds of Soy Sauces out there. What is normally referred to as Soy Sauce is "Shoyu". This is Tamari.

The difference? The ingredients.
- Shoyu is made from Soy and Wheat.
- Tamari is made from Soy.

Tamari ends up being a little less salty but has a more complex flavor. It is more ideal for dipping and using as a condiment, where as Shoyu, while still great as a condiment, is often less expensive and is better suited for the cooking process in my opinion.

Anyway... getting off point. This is delicious. After scouring the local Asian groceries for soy sauces, I've found one that I can be happy with!

review_body:
The product comes with a recipe book when you order it through Amazon which is awesome since you can find ways to incorporate the powder into a variety of recipes. I personally made the green tea latte and the cupcake icing from the recipes in the book.

Ok, so the powder tastes very much like green tea but it slightly stronger in flavor. I enjoyed the increased flavor since green tea can sometimes be very subtle in flavor and this worked to turn the flavor up a notch. The latte that I made was very nice and calming and did provide me with some energy. I wouldn't say that the green tea powder helped with weight loss but that was expected since losing weight is a dynamic process that involves multiple factors. However, the tea was more \\"filling\\" than some other flavored rinks that I have had.

The cupcake icing recipe wound up tasting pretty good. There was not a strong green tea flavor and it wound up tasting more like cheesecake than icing. It was still yummy though. I also added some of the powder to regular vanilla cupcakes to amp up the flavor a notch. Also I topped the cupcake with almonds and chia seeds for some extra flavor. Overall, I am very happy with the product and plan on enjoying this tea when I need that extra energy after a long day. Disclaimer: I did receive this product for free for purposes of reviewing.

review_body: This Marmite is more powerful, more flavourful, and more Marmite than should be exported from the UK.  As an American I've fallen in love with regular Marmite, however XO has proven to be a radically different experience. As i finished the sandwich, and the deafening cacophony of God Save the Queen was met with a quiet nod.  I stroked my handlebar moustache and wondered what if anything was missing from the evening.  From the sitting room a woman exclaimed, "you shant meet the train in time if you tarry any further darling.  Now make haste! the lads are surely waiting at the cockleberry pub with a tall lager."  I'm now a 40 year old Ackley Eustice Pilkington thanks to Marmite XO. Splendid.

product_title: Stash Tea Decaf Premium Green Tea, 10 Count Tea Bags in Foil (Pack of 12)
review_headline: Premium Green w/o the Premium Cost
review_body:
Standard for all my reviews: When reviewing products, I always remain objective and honest about the product or service. I always review with information that I feel others would like to know about the product as I always assume what I'm writing will influence for or against the purchase. I always try to go above and beyond surface characteristics and input into quality, value and application. Most importantly, I will always end the review with an answer as to whether I'd purchase the product again which I believe is the most critical question pertaining to the item. To manufacturers: Want me to review your items, just let me know!

I have a few Amazon items on subscription, where they are sent on a schedule such that I don't have to worry about running out of the product or remembering to reorder. This Stash Decaf Tea is one of those items.

I drink a LOT of green tea and about a year ago set out to find a good balance between flavor, style and cost. After trying many premium teas, some that came in silk sachets and some teas that were private label, I have settled on the Stash. Cost is reduced if you subscribe and it's even less when considering that the tea packets themselves come loosely packed in a small box .. without a lot of packaging or marketing that would raise the price. When it comes down to it, it's about $0.17 per cup of tea which is extremely reasonable if you've priced out standard teas. The best part is that I find the Stash tea to be a great balance of flavor, not overly bitter and not requiring as much sweetener.

During my research I had actually cut open the tea bags before and after drinking allowing them to dry so I could see what was really in them. Stash does have some upper end tea bags that are very nice and this particular product is on par with what you'd find on most store shelves. The subscription option and lower price will keep me coming back.

product_title: Plum Kids Organic Fruit Shredz, 5-Count (Pack of 8)
review_body:
I thought these might be healthy, but I should have looked at the details first. These are 80% sugar: 14g sugar in an 18g serving. From the research I've read, when fruit sugar is removed from fruit it is very similar to table sugar (http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2013/06/29/fruit-sugar-versus-white-sugar_n_3497795.html). This product seems like a bagful of extracted sugar to me. It is simply dried fruit juice concentrate and fruit puree, with a tiny bit of vegetable juice thrown in to make it sound healthier. Maybe there are some residual nutrients in the dried fruit juice and puree? Only 1g of fiber.

Most desserts have a lower % of calories from sugar. Even candy like Tootsie Pops are lower at 10g of sugar per 17g lollipop. I will classify this product as candy in my book, high-end candy. However, because it is dried fruit juice I'd rather give this candy to my kids than a tootsie pop.

product_title: Vermont Smoke & Cure Smoked Pepperoni (Pack of 2) 7 oz Sticks
review_body:
BridgeFord: 2/5
- Highly flavored, so much so that it seems like they are trying to hide some other flavor. But it does have the classic pepperoni flavor
- A bit on the spicy side, this has to do with the amount of flavoring in the stick but has a clear pepper flavor to it.
- Extremely oily. There is so much oil in this stick that it is just messy and nasty
- The casing is difficult to remove and tears easily like paper.
- Consistency of the meat isn’t good, and it is clear low quality meats are used in its preparation

Fortuna: 2/5
- Flavor is relatively mild, with a slight spice to it.
- Casing appears to be a slim plastic case of some sort and again not easily removed
- Meat quality again doesn’t appear to be great
- Several spots of mold on the casing
- This is certainly a serviceable pepperoni but not something I would consider great.

Battistoni: 3/5
- Flavor is slightly more than mild, with a good spice to it. Not enough to be a problem, but enough to add some flavor. It has a slight breakfast sausage flavor hidden behind the classic pepperoni flavor as well.
- Casing again appears to be some sort of slim plastic
- Meat is a slightly better consistency than the Bridgeford and Fortuna
- Another extremely oily stick, on par with the Bridgeford in how much oil is in it again making it messy to work with.
- The stick is a tad on the softer side compared to some of the others making it a tad easier to cut
- Overall again a reasonable pepperoni, but the breakfast sausage flavor underneath kinda throws me for a little bit of a loop. Not necessarily a bad thing as I enjoy breakfast sausage, but unexpected in a pepperoni.

Vermont: 4/5
- The flavor is a nicely balanced and well-rounded flavor with a little smokiness to it. There is not a lot of spice to it, just a hint so if you are looking for a spicy pepperoni this is probably not the one for you. However, the overall flavor is still very nice.
- The casing appears to be a natural casing, it is a smooth casing (not wrinkled like most of the others), it removes cleanly from the meat, and relatively easily.
- The meat has a nice consistency and appears to use higher quality meats than found in some of the other sticks.
- This stick is a little wider than some of the others
- This stick is pretty oily, not quite as bad as the Bridgeford and Battistoni, but not much better either.
- For some reason I found this stick slightly harder to cut than the others. I am not certain why that is.
- Overall a very solid pepperoni choice, an optional spicy version could be useful, and cleaning up some of the oil would be nice. This is a pepperoni I would recommend for those looking for a nice flavor with hints of smoke in it.

Boar’s Head: 4/5
- Flavor is a pretty classic pepperoni flavor with a little heat working its way in at the end. The heat appears to come on gradually and gets fairly strong near the end.
- The meat consistency is pretty good, similar to the Vermont in that regard.
- This still has a bit of oil to it (as all pepperoni likely do), but it is not nearly as bad as the Bridgeford and Battistoni.
- The casing is again round and smooth making it easier to remove than some of the dried wrinkled sticks. Though it tears like paper similar to what was seen with the Bridgeford casing.
- Overall another very solid pepperoni choice, particularly if you like a little heat in your pepperoni.

Margherita: 5/5
- Flavor is a very nice pepperoni flavor with depth to it. There is a little heat at the end, slightly less than in the Boar’s Head but it had a similar build-up near the end.
- The casing is similar to what was seen in the Bridgeford and Boar’s head where it tears similar to paper.
- This is again a round (not wrinkled) pepperoni stick so the casing comes off fairly easy.
- This is the least greasy of the brands I tried which I found to be a very nice change of pace.
- The meat is fairly consistent, one of the best brands for consistency if not THE best.
- This was one of the easiest pepperoni to cut into consistently sized slices.
- In my opinion this is the best of the pepperoni brands I tasted. It hit all of the right notes, was easy to work with, and not overly oily like many of the others. The flavor profile was very clearly pepperoni, but with a depth of flavor that most of the others missed, with a nice heat at the end that was not overpowering, but helped add to the flavor.

#1 – Margherita is a well-rounded Pepperoni that hits all of the right notes.
#2 – Vermont is another great choice, particularly if you are looking for a slightly smokey flavor.
#3 – Boar’s Head is a great alternate choice. It is similar to the Margherita, but I simply felt that the Margherita was a little better quality over all.

I would suggest staying away from the Bridgeford and the Fortuna’s as those were the worst of the bunch..

product_title: ENU Meal Replacement Shakes for Weight Gain, 23g Protein / 450 Calories (Assorted Flavors, 12-Pack)
review_body: My young, healthy husband was diagnosed with an aggressive leukemia in July 2014.  During four rounds of chemo and a stem cell transplant, he often didn't feel like eating and was losing a lot of weight.  We tried many mainstream meal replacement drinks, but found that they contained high fructose corn syrup and carrageenan.  This is basically garbage that we try to avoid when we are healthy, let alone when we are fighting cancer.  We asked dietitians for help finding higher quality options that were still safe while he was neutropenic, but they were of little help.  Then, one of our oncologists told us about ENU.  He said it was developed in part by oncologists for exactly what we were going through.  We have since purchased and consumed multiple cases of it.  At times, my husband wound drink three of these a day when nothing else sounded appetizing.  My husband prefers the chocolate to vanilla.  I actually tasted one, and I think the chocolate ENU tastes a lot like chocolate soy milk!  This drink is very nutrient dense, actually tastes good, and doesn't have the junk that a lot of national brands contain.  We believe ENU is the higher quality meal replacement drink and cannot recommend it enough.

product_title: Powell & Mahoney Margarita Vintage Original Cocktail Mixer - 750 ml
review_headline: Fresh, Natural Mixer for the Perfect Margarita
review_body:
Do you love margaritas? They are among the most popular adult beverages in America and many people rank them as their favorite alcoholic beverage of all. The right tequila can make a noticeable difference when mixing up a margarita, but the right mixer is important as well. And one of the best mixers available is Power & Mahoney Margarita.

I just got to know Powell & Mahoney recently and I have been singing its praises ever since. This mix is every bit as delicious as the others in the Powell & Mahoney lineup thanks in no small part to the all- natural ingredients used in the process. Have you taken a good look at the ingredients used in other mixers? They're enough to make even the most tolerant person cringe. Even a really good tequila often cannot mask the taste of a bad mixer and I can think of many mixed drinks that I could barely finish due to a less-than-pleasant mixer base.

With Powell & Mahnoey Margarita mixer, you get the great, natural taste you desire with a good balance between the sweet and the sour. Pour a little into a glass and taste it all by itself. You will notice flavors of lime and a little bit of orange with an overall taste that leans toward the sour side but one that seems just right to match with a fine tequila. The taste is even good enough that some people might enjoy this mixer served with non- alcoholic combinations like soda water and even on the rocks with nothing added.

Margaritas are popular drinks but even your favorite drink can lose its appeal if it contains a weak ingredient. With Powell & Mahoney Margarita mixer, you get the great, natural, fresh citrus flavor that makes for the perfect mixed drink. Buy a bottle from this Vermont- based company and fall in love with your margarita, all over again.

product_title: Amazing Grass Green Superfood
review_headline: Does have caffeine (green tea) but can't tell how much from the label.  VERY energizing, but I'm assuming its not much caffeine
review_body:
I can't believe how addictive I'm finding this stuff - I want to eat it far more often than I should. I keep it simple and blend it up (using my single serve size cup for my awesome ninja blender) with about a cup of blueberries or raspberries, frozen. I tend to put 3-4 scoops of the green stuff in. The annoying grittiness is disguised by the berries. The result is a creamy, smooth, delicious treat. I add in stevia if I want it a bit sweeter (did that at first, don't bother now) and 2-3 tablespoons of cocoa powder plus a lot of stevia, or some blackstrap molasses, if I'm looking for a dessert drink to feed my chocolate cravings. I adore it in all these forms, but find that more than 6-7 scoops a day CLEANS ME OUT. Probably not a bad thing. But ummm. Yeah. Loving it so far.

ANd yes, I'm NOT missing coffee (coincidentally decided to make February my Coffee-fast month) and without any caffeine in my system, I DO feel energized. Its hard to believe that could just be from vitamins - maybe its the maca root?? But I'm a lot less hungry and more full feeling all the time, and with 3 scoops of greens and 1 cup of blueberries, each shake is about 150 calories, so I'm loving that.

product_title: 2 Pack 10 Rolls Fujifilm Neopan Acros 100
review_headline: Neopan Acros is hands down my favorite black and white film
review_body:
Neopan Acros is hands down my favorite black and white film. High contrast, has a lot of punch. Orthopanchromatic, so it does respond to the entire visible spectrum, although less so in the reds. Obviously depends on your developer, but overall has some of the finest grain of any film, excellent if you want to blow up some big prints. Maintains reasonable contrast and grain even when push processed.

An interesting trait of this film is that it is very resistant to reciprocity failure - long exposures stay uniform for up to half an hour. As an astrophotographer, all these features make it my go to black and white film.

product_title: Braswell Seafood Select Balsamic Cherry Grilling Sauce for Swordfish
review_headline: Awesome Sauce!!! May seem a bit pricy but WELL WORTH THE COST!
review_body:
Awesome Sauce!!!!! May seem a bit pricy but WELL WORTH THE COST!

I mix Braswell's Select Cherry Balsamic Grilling Sauce for Swordfish with Fairway Grilling Sauce (pretty much a Bar-B-Q sauce but I like this flavor for this mix) & a little Lea & Perrins Worcestershire Sauce for a terrific combination on chicken & pork for grilling. I sear it 1st right after I brush & burn off the grill grates then use a low heat setting or higher rack & slow cook it so it does not burn & the meat stays juicy. I sometimes stick a small piece of cherry wood (just a branch if I have it) on top of the burner under the grate & infuse everything with the cherry smoke…what a flavour! Sometimes I add a little Knudson Just Cranberry Juice to the mix if I want it a little more tart & sometimes a little honey if I want a sweeter taste…depends on the mood, the sides & what I have available. Sorry but I just “eyeball” my ingredients but maybe ½ & ½ of the Fairway grilling sauce/ Braswell’s cherry sauce with a couple dashes of the Worcestershire Sauce…you don’t need much, enough to coat the meat & a little leftover sauce in the bowl to drizzle over the meat after searing when grilling so a 12oz bottle goes a long way.

I also use the above mix & coat the meat (as you would with an egg) then roll in Italian bread crumbs & cook on medium heat in a stainless pan in lots of butter on the stovetop. I like to try to crisp it but as I’m using thick bottom stainless or LeCreuset ceramic over cast iron pans anything that sticks to the bottom I put water in the pan & make a thick sauce I serve over/alongside the meat. You have the meat juice/a little fat & this sauce for a wonderful but not overpowering flavour & great aftertastes. Try it & be creative!!!

FYI, I never used it on fish though as I prefer just lemon & butter.

product_title: Paleo Bread -Almond (1 Net Carb)
review_body: OMG!!!! And they call this bread??? More so like aged old wet, nasty, smelly, mildewed slices of putrefied sponge material that hasn't had any air in thousands of years is what I call it!!!     After leaving my Dietician's office, I was advised to try different gluten and soy free breads. This is one of the breads that was on the list. I had not read any reviews about it before buying. I just decided I would go on a shopping spree and buy 4 different alternative breads, but hold on to dear life to my receipt so I could return the product that didn't work for me. Well out of the 4 I tried, this was absolutely the most horrible, disgusting, gross overpriced \\"so called\\" health food product I ever tasted in my life. I so wanted to like this product because I am a low carber and it had the lowest net carb of all the others that I bought, but it just got more disgusting with each attempt to silence the nasty rancid taste. I tried it frozen, toasted, grilled, unthawed and the foul nature of it just wouldn't let up. The only reedeming thing about this bread is that I am so grateful that I could return it for a full refund, which is very important to me when I am trying new products that I have no experience with. I work hard for my money and I can't stand to see not even one penny of it go to waste.     Anyhow, on yesterday, as I sat in my car in Whole Foods' parking lot, I just wanted to give this bread one more chance before returning it because the low carb profile of it just calls my spirit to want to like it. For some strange reason, I thought it might be better since it had been sitting in my car for several hours which was  about room temperature around this time of year. I open the bag and before the horrific smell could hit my nose and signal a warning to my brain, I put another piece in my mouth and Oh my God! What the heck did I do that for?!!!! It seemed as though I bit into a pile of FUNKY mold and mildew and I couldn't gag this crap out of my mouth fast enough! I rushed into Whole Foods to get my refund. In a state of trama, I explained to the cashier my horrific experience of eating the bread as I began to feel sick on my stomach and very nauseous. After being horrified herself from my reaction to the bread, she chunked the bread into the trash and asked me was I alright and did I need her to call for help. I told her I would be fine although I felt nauseous and sick to my stomach for a couple of hours after eating the bread. Apparently, this mess (i meant \\"bread\\") cannot stay at room temperature not just because it may compromise \\"taste\\" (for lack of a better term), but because it could make a person very ill due to the fact that this bread seems to be a breeding ground for mold and mildew which seems to love this bread more than humans do. Please do not buy this bread unless you can return it if you don't like it. Its an expensive nasty lesson if you can't get yourself a refund. As you see majority of the people here on Amazon do not like the bread and they are not exaggerating the nastiness and funkiness of this bread.    I understand how challenging it might be for a company to step outside the box to cater to finicky eaters or health food junkies like us (i.e. the people that have chosen to eat this type of food) so I usually won't write a review unless the product is good/exceptional or notoriously bad (like this one). If this product was just not up to par for my specific taste buds, just average, nothing to rave about or simply somewhere in between, I wouldn't continue to patronize the company, but I'd reframe from writing a review and wish the company well with the customers that like their products because I know being in business in this type of market isn't easy. But this product was so traumatizing to me that I felt it appropriate to come to Amazon to share my experience in the hopes that Julian Bakery reads this and do something about rectifying this God awful product before someone gets sick and sue the pants off of them. Thank goodness I'm well now, but I would not feed my worst enemy this bread.     I will digress a bit for those curious about my bread taste test by sharing that of all the breads I tried, this was the worst one by far. The other ones were just not to my liking and shall remained unnamed. But to the contrary, Three Bakers rye bread  was so good and yummy! It was like finding bread nirvana for me! As a low carb eater, the bread is dangerously good! It is the closest thing to the taste of regular bread (it actually tastes a bit better to me). Although Three Bakers bread taste damn good and it does not contain soy, dairy, or gluten, my issue with it is that it's too many carbs for me (2 slices which are smaller than reg size bread. They're the size of a big craker = 28 net carbs) and it does not say that the ingredients are organic nor does it say that they are NON-GMO. For the price of the Three Bakers Bread (i.e. $6.89 for about 12-14 slices) I am very disappointed about these issuess, so once I devour the loaf (which I've almost done in 3 days) I'm sad to say I would only buy it a couple of times of year when I just want to splurge on bread.

product_title: Keurig B155 Commercial OfficePRO Premier Brewing System
review_headline: Disposable, don't last, can't be fixed
review_body:
Keurig machines are disposable junk. The only thing that keeps them selling is our common desire for quick quality coffee.

Got a B70 in Dec 2012, it didn't make it 2 years.

When it fails after warranty, all they offer is "discount" on a new one -- basically a "Black Friday" price, 1/3 off retail. Wow!

Check out the 1-star reviews on the new 2.0 machines: They are "improved"...to increase Keurig profits. A scanner now makes sure manufacturers have paid license fees. This "feature" has ZERO benefit to the customer, makes the "My K-Cup" accessory useless, and your existing stock of K-cups won't work. Basically, it's "Welcome to the world of DRM for coffee"!

They don't last, cannot be repaired, have enough defects to make eventual failure nearly certain. There is a whopping 1-whole-year warranty, after which the company refuses to service the machine AT ALL.

There is no parts list or repair manual. There is no service center. The machine seems designed for quick assembly by cheap labor -- there is no way to remove the case and get at the insides.

Search YouTube for "Keurig repair"; it's an eye-opener. People use hacksaws and Dremel tools, just to get the case off, to attempt a fix. I have electric tools which cost far less, yet come with a manual and can be disassembled for maintenance/repair.

I've owned Mr. Coffee and Black & Decker coffee-makers that cost far less and lasted much longer. When I donated them, they still worked!

Buy at your own risk. It will become landfill, though if you are lucky, later rather than sooner

It's the sort of coffee you might have on a late Saturday morning in autumn, after you've woken up from sleeping in and wander to the kitchen in cozy socks to pour yourself a cup, wrapping your hands around the warm mug.

Personally, I'm a fan of the packaging. I love that when you tear open an individually wrapped packet, the fresh aroma of ground coffee greets you. review_body:

I definitely recommend trying lime sparkling water with this. Sparkling water is already a great alternative to soda, but if you miss the sweetness as well, just pop one of these suckers in and you'll be good to go!

An hour into the "experiment", I was beginning to get concerned that the effects wouldn't wear off, but apparently it will last anywhere from 15 minutes to two hours. No need to worry. My taste buds have reverted to their normal state.

product_title: Dechunxian China Top Ten Famous Teas
review_body:
This silver needle (Baihao Yinzhen or 白 毫 銀 針) tea is a very lightly oxidized white tea from the Fuding region of Fujian province in China. It is made from only the tips of the Da Bai variety of tea plant, picked early in the season. The leaves have a furry appearance when closely examined. It is a less common tea and is highly regarded.

The leaves should be brewed with water that has not yet boiled and only for a few minutes. Once the tea has been drunk, the leaves then can be brewed again, several times in succession.

The result is a beautiful pale golden beverage with a lightly fresh herbaceous and floral aroma. The flavor is complex, with the fresher herbaceous elements giving way to richer and slightly sweet notes and a very lightly astringent finish.

Make a point of enjoying the brewing and drinking of this tea, rather than gulping it while distracted.

The tea is packaged in an airtight bag in a reusable metal canister.

DeChunXian provided tea for evaluation and review.

review_headline: Amoretti Caramel syrup does not disappoint!

I use this and other Amoretti syrups mainly to enhance the flavor of my bland meal-replacement shakes - but this caramel syrup is quite versatile - it also goes very well in my coffee.  I constantly try out different flavors of Amoretti syrups whenever I see one marked down in price, but I confess there is always a bottle of this caramel syrup to be found in my growing collection of syrups on my lazy susan in my kitchen (currently holding 8 open bottles).  The quality of Amoretti syrups and the virtually infinite possibility of flavor combinations (caramel + expresso syrup - yum!) are only surpassed by Amoretti's superior customer service team. review_body:
In one word: Nectar.

product_title: Buff Bake – Nut Butters Variety Pack Snickerdoodle Almond Butter, Chocolate Chip Peanut Butter, Cinnamon Raisin Peanut Butter, and Cranberry Coconut Peanut Butter)
review_body:
I've tried numerous high protein nut butters, including ones from P28 and Nuts N' More, and these just don't do it for me. They're not bad, but they're not good; according to the 3 star rating \\"It's okay.\\" Won't be buying again, but I'll finish these jars.

First, it's more expensive than other high protein nut butters. The nut butters from P28 and Nuts N' More come in 16oz containers, whereas this one comes in a 12oz container. The prices are comparable between high protein nut butters, so you're getting less nut butter for your dollar.

Second, the protein/Calorie ratio is not as good. This product has only 13g/200 Calories. One of my favorites, [[ASIN:B00HRH9J4M Nuts N More Peanut Butter Crunch, Toffee, 16 Ounce]], has 14g/188 Calories. Another, [[ASIN:B00B99OJ26 P28 Foods Formulated High Protein Spread, White Chocolate, 16 Ounce]], has 14g/200 Calories.

Third, these nut butters are really liquid, almost a soup-like consistency. I tried placing them in the refrigerator after stirring, but all of them except the almond butter became rock hard. I do find sticking the almond butter in the refrigerator makes it an ideal consistency.

Fourth, if you're more interested in the taste than the 1g or 12 Calorie difference, then you'll still be let down by the taste. Full disclosure, I like strong flavors. I love the taste of peanut butter, but if it's flavored, I want to be able to tell. With this product, I barely get the flavors:

-I thought Chocolate Chip would be my favorite, but it was my biggest letdown. Not a strong chocolate flavor at all.
-Cinnamon Raisin was the biggest surprise. Normally not a huge fan of cinnamon raisin peanut butters, but it was pretty good. One of the stronger flavors, which is probably why I like it.
-Cranberry Coconut I've already reviewed separately, but I didn't really get cranberry or coconut from it. A fine peanut butter, but a lackluster flavored peanut butter.
-I like snickerdoodle cookies, but the Snickerdoodle Almond Butter tasted just like a cinnamon raisin almond butter. Not saying that's bad. It may be my favorite of the bunch because it refrigerates well and spreads better than the others.

TL;DR - I'd go with P28 or Nuts N' More over these nut butters, but they weren't bad. I'll finish the jars, but I won't order again.

review_headline: New Packaging, Not the Same Flavor
review_body:
So disappointed with this shipment. I've been ordering the Southeastern Mills Brown Gravy Mix in bulk about every 6 months (or whenever I ran out!) for a few years now, as I loved the rich flavor and texture; it went well with many dinner dishes and was like no other brown gravy I could find.

Now the gravy pouches have a new look--they still say Southeastern Mills but also tout a new name for the flavor, "Classic" Brown Gravy Mix. Also, each pouch does not contain the same 2.75 oz. (77g) of gravy mix as before; now it has only 1.76 oz. (50g). I also noticed that the ingredients have slightly changed, but I didn't think much of it until I actually made and tasted the gravy. That was when the real disappointment set in.

The gravy is a bit darker and the flavor is completely different. It now tastes a lot like the common beef gravies you can get from the supermarket. If some people like that kind of flavor, then that's fine, but the reason I ordered this gravy, aside from not being able to find it in local stores, was because it stood out from all the rest, being deliciously different and closer to homemade. I wish Southeastern Mills didn't have to ruin what was an already great-tasting product. This may very well be the last case of their gravy I will use.

When you're cooking something in a pressure cooker or a long wet cooking method like soups stews crockpots, then this should be added either in the bowl when you serve it or right before you serve it, Because the smokiness does fade if you're using a long wet cooking method. product_title: Go Lo Almond Butter
review_headline: Taste is Tops; Price and Low-Fat Value Less So
review_body:
\\"Go-Lo\\" almond butter certainly is tasty enough to love. I ate some by itself and then spread a generous amount on toasted homemade bread. Both ways showcase a product that has a complex, toasty/nutty flavor. And that flavor is almond and not peanuts or hazelnuts. The next big thing is that Go-Lo claims the product rates zero on the glycemic index, making it fine for people who have issues about sugars. Fine so far.

Reading the product label, the serving size is set at 2 TBs/32 g and there are about 10 servings in a jar. Eleven ounces of product costs almost 15.00 plus shipping on Amazon. Well, nuts and specialty nut butters are expensive. Still, similar products Amazon suggests on the same page cost much less or even less than much less.

Looking further, each serving contains 170 calories of which 130 calories come from fat. Much of that fat comes from palm oil--a highly saturated fat. Palm oil is listed second on the ingredient label, after almonds. As for protein, at 8 g. per 32 g. of product, this seems to be fairly high-protein, assuming it is a complete protein or you eat it on something and drink a glass of milk. Some of that protein comes from non-nut sources: hemp and pea protein. I wonder how 'processed' those two products are? Whatever, they do add to the complex flavor of the product, and the oil balance provides an agreeable texture to the product.

Love this. I'm very picky about my decaf (if I'm not getting the caffeine boost, I at least want it to taste good), and this one is great. It's less bold than Dark Magic decaf (my other favorite), and more grounded. It's the sort of coffee you might have on a late Saturday morning in autumn, after you've woken up from sleeping in and wander to the kitchen in cozy socks to pour yourself a cup, wrapping your hands around the warm mug.

The packaging is also nice. Each k-cup is individually wrapped, and the coffee is enclosed in a soft filter cup rather than the typical plastic k-cup. When you tear open an individually wrapped packet, the fresh aroma of ground coffee bursts forth to greet you. Since I've started using my Keurig, I don't get that fresh smell of coffee anymore and didn't realize how much I missed it. product_title: Russell Stover Limited Edition Chocolate Gift Box -- Cake Flavors
review_headline: Yummy, if you like the taste of shoe polish mixed with gasoline.
review_body:
Eww, eww, eww!! I wasn't even able to finish one truffle, and my expectations were extremely low. I love truffles and enjoy all kinds (Lindt, Ghirardelli, Godiva), but I'm well aware that Russell Stover is the Dr. Thunder of chocolate. I'm pretty sure the last time I had Russell Stover was as a kid, until today. I was perusing the after-Christmas candy sales and decided to buy this since it was so cheap.

I first bit into the red velvet truffle. I was actually surprised that the chocolate wasn't too bad. It pretty much tasted like the cheap semisweet chocolate chips I buy for making cookies. But then I started tasted the filling, and my taste buds screamed out in horror and immediately demanded that I spit the nastiness out. There was something so wrong about this truffle. I can barely describe it. The best word for it is \\"chemical.\\" I may as well have licked shoe polish. Actually, if I could go back in time and had a choice, I would definitely pick the shoe polish. At least that would meet my expectations. I did NOT expect this to taste like chemicals.

My husband saw my reaction and asked our 6-year-old daughter if she wanted to finish it (he certainly wasn't going to try it), and she gladly took it (she wasn't in the room for my screams of terror). She quite enjoyed it and didn't see anything wrong with it, and she and her brother finished off the box. I honestly don't consider myself a chocolate snob, and my kids have tasted really awesome truffles before, so it's not as though they're ignorant of good, quality chocolate. My husband took a bite out of the chocolate cake truffle, and he wasn't grossed out by it. It's a shame he didn't try the red velvet to see if I'm completely insane. It's possible that something horrible happened at the factory with the red velvet mixture and that that's the only inedible one here, but I wouldn't want to find out. I vow never to buy another Russell Stover chocolate, no matter how cheap it is.

Have you ever seen the movie Elf? You know that scene where he sprays the perfume in his mouth? My reaction was much like his.Elf? You know that scene where he sprays the perfume in his mouth? My reaction was much like his.

I never use the microwave and always tip the contents into a saucepan and heat at a low-medium temperature until you start seeing bubbles.

It goes very well with a wide range of desserts such as tarts, crumbles, Xmas puddings, pies and my favourite rolly polly. Although the product can be stored at room temperature prior to being opened, once opened it must be kept in the fridge and consumed within 3 days.

product_title: Halfpops Curiously Crunchy Popcorn, Butter and Pure Ocean Sea Salt, 6 Ounce
review_body:
If you make popcorn the old fashioned way ie on the stove top, throw in some melted butter and shake some salt on the bowl of popped corn, you'll find those unpopped "old maids" in the bottom of the bowl, well salted and drenched in butter, when you work your way down to the bottom. This snack kind of reminds me of those kernels, though split open so you don't crack your teeth on them.

The sea salt and butter taste are good and not artificial tasting and the corn kernels are split so you get a lot of fiber taste when crunching your way through them. Keep your drink handy though as you'll be using it to wash down the hard kernel pieces from under your tongue. It's kind of like eating roasted pumpkin seeds-lots of crunch with lots of fiber souped up with butter and salt notes.

If you're a Smart Food popcorn kind of person, this is definitely not your next go to.

In the past I have bought large bags of almonds from Costco. And one bag takes forever to complete, because it is a huge bag, like most things at Costco. But I have never eaten an almond out of their bag and stopped to think for even one second that there was any issue with what I was eating.

I can't say the same for this product. Obviously, I am disappointed. I will still eat them to finish up the box, because I am sure I am not going to get sick from them, but I won't be ordering them again.

I gave two stars because they were individually wrapped, they did arrive on time, and maybe just maybe I got a bad batch.

product_title: Brookside Dark Choc Pomegranate, 32 oz
review_body:
Got these for Christmas. Like other reviewers mentioned, there's only a minimal amount of pomegranate juice in these, and they definitely don't taste like real pomegranate.
They're just chocolate covered gummies. The gummy alone was tart but if I had tasted it without know it was supposed to be pomegranate, I wouldn't have guessed it had any pomegranate at all.
The chocolate is standard Hershey's dark chocolate covered with "resinous glaze" (whatever that is) to make them look shiny and not clump together.
People who think these have any health benefits are kidding themselves. They're candy, after all. They're still loaded with sugars and the little bit of fruit juice in them is negligible.
They're edible if you like chocolate, but by no means extraordinary when it comes to chocolates.
My 2 star rating is because the package leads you to believe these are real fruit. I ate 3 or 4 of these and tossed the rest in the garbage, so I would not buy them for myself.

review_headline: Great for alkaline ph readings, and tastes real.
review_body:
I have a problem with being too acidic, and when I'm acidic I lose energy pretty fast, as seen per urine ph strips. Green smoothies, chlorella and citrus fruits helped some, including bottled lemon juice. Those things helped, but not as much as I needed, often. Baking soda and sodium ascorbate always got me alkaline, but they also caused a concerning ache in a kidney and studies show too much b. soda can cause kidney problems.

I have been putting a tbsp. of True Lemon and about 2 tbsp. of frozen orange juice in a quart jar to sip on throughout the day. (I also add some celery seed as that helps with blood pressure, though it didn't seem to increase alkalinity.) Even with some pretty strongly acidic meats I am able to stay alkaline. And I much prefer the taste of True Lemon to the bottled lemon juice. And btw, I take my drink through a straw to protect my teeth from too much acid.

product_title: Comvita Manuka Honey UMF 15+ 250 Gr/8.8 Oz - Set of Two Jars - Free U.S. Shipping by Priority Mail
review_headline: But I know 15+ UMF is a good medicinal standard
review_body: The brand I was searching for was out of stock. So I chose this Comvita. I researched their verification and they are the real deal. This is 15+ UMF and I did want a higher UMF for medicinal/health purposes. The higher UMF is really hard to find, when you do find it, its out of stock. But I know 15+ UMF is a good medicinal standard. Its not as if we're critical care patients. We really wanted preventive and to assist with some health issues that arise. It arrived promptly, two jars. The consistency was firm and the color is a light brown. The taste is sweet, of course its honey and I do love the taste of it. But this is not overly sweet. Now, my older son has digestion issues. He cannot absolutely tolerate dairy and processed cheeses. But oh how he loves them both. He will actually throw up within 2 hours of eating dairy and have heartburn if he lays down, he's known of these dairy issues for several years. Well, the very day this arrived, he had consumed some pizza with cheese on it. Not a lot, just a slice and he thought it was worth it. He so craved that pizza! Now he is not a baby and I can't follow him around insisting he adhere to his health regime. But sure enough, later that night as he was sleeping, he immediately jumped up and ran for the bathroom to throw up that pizza. I jumped up and ran for this honey. After all, this is why I bought it. I didn't think it would help immediately but it did. After he finished his business, he usually suffers the heartburn so he must sit upright. I gave him 1 level teaspoon that evening. He sat up on the sofa, when I came to check on him later I saw he had stretched out and laid down straight. Oh no! But He looked to peaceful to wake. I went back to lay down myself, but not one time did I hear him wake up. (with the heartburn) He told me the next morning, he never did wake up during the night. That has never happened before he always had the following heartburn with dairy. He's seen digestive specialist and allergist whotell him to just keep the offending food away and you'll be fine. But a 17 year old is going to crave to eat pizza! If just sometimes. I've tried to make them myself without cheese, now that's awful. Each night, this honey is now part of his regime even without consuming the dairy. I think its a great digestive aid, I take it myself each night but only 1/2 teaspoon.

product_title: Viva Labs Organic Coconut Flour
review_headline: Four-Pound Bag is a Money Saver
review_body:
I've been using one particular brand of coconut flour over the past year, so it is always interesting to compare brands. Quite honestly, the Viva Labs coconut flour is so identical to the brand I've been using that I can't tell a difference. Both are not bleached, GMO-free, and contain no additives or fillers.

The flour tastes like coconut and has a mild sweetness. It also has the grainy texture that I expect of coconut flour. It comes in a resealable bag, making it easy to store after use.

Price Point

With the Viva Labs one-pound bag of coconut flour at $9.99, the brand I'm buying is a steal at $5.99 a pound. However, you can also purchase Viva Labs coconut flour in a four-pound bag for $14.99, so it's clear where the best deal is. If you use coconut flour regularly, the four-pound bag is definitely the way to go and the way I'll be buying my coconut flour in the future.

review_headline: If you like chips, most would say that you can't go ...

Each chip is covered with a pleasing amount of chocolate to any chocolate lovers' palate. It's not over abundant, but it's thick enough to get a true and satisfying taste of the chocolate along with the chip. They're so gratifying, that you really don't need to eat the whole 5 oz. bag in one sitting--unless of course, you like to over-indulge like me. The point is, this will totally fulfill any sweet, with a little bit of salty, craving. In fact, it just might exceed your expectations. Really, they're that Good!

product_title: Bulk Save Popcorners Kettle Popped Corn Chips 12 to 48 packs each 5 Oz
review_body:
Sometimes you want sweet, sometimes you want salty. Sometimes you want a chip and sometimes popcorn sounds tasty. This Popcorners Kettle Popped Corn Chips combine all four wants into one light chip with great texture. The texture is kind of a bubbly, quilted texture which enhances the chips' appeal.

The kettle flavor is just the right amount of sweetness to me so it's not overpowering, yet you can taste a bit of saltiness, too. And the chips are fairly healthy, as they are lowfat, low sugar and low salt.

Ingredients listed on bag: enriched Yellow Corn {Yellow Corn, Niacin, Iron, Thiamine Mononitrate, Riboflavin, Folic Acid}, Sunflower Oil, Sugar, Sea Salt. The oil used is a healthy oil and like the use of sea salt instead of regular salt.

These are air popped with real corn. One bag has 140 calories and is low sodium (110 mg or 5% DV) and low sugar (3g), so they are relatively guilt-free. There are no artificial additives or preservatives and they are gluten free. This kettle is one of my favorite flavors and the only sweet flavor they make. I like the sea salt, too which tastes like salted popcorn.

Great to serve at a party for something a little different.

review_headline: Ramp up the nutritive value of baked goods & cooked cereal.
review_body:
Sprouted ground flax is more nutritious than flax seed or even ground flax seed. Sprouting gives it a fresh smell that is not overpowering. I add anywhere from a teaspoon to a tablespoon or more per cup of flour, commercial baking mix, or cooked cereal mix.

Like all whole foods, this is a perishable item. Though it doesn't spoil easily, keeping it in the refrigerator will keep it fresh even longer. It substitutes well for wheat germ in the Cornell Triple Rich formula--you can google that for more info--which adds small amounts of soy flour, dry milk and wheat germ to the bottom of each cup of flour. This greatly increases the nutritive value of all flour-based carbs.

product_title: Hint Fizz, 12-Ounce Bottles (Pack of 12)
review_headline: Comes in a GLASS bottle with a metal lid that requires an opener
review_body:
I've been buying regular Hint water for our kids' lunches for a year or two now, and we love that they're unsweetened and yet tasty. I thought I'd buy Hint Fizz just to add a little variety, and the picture plainly shows a plastic bottle with a screw top cap.

They arrived this week with my Subscribe & Save order, and I was perturbed to see GLASS bottles with metal lids that need an opener. There's no way I'll send a glass bottle in their lunch, and I can only imagine how quickly they'd lose a bottle opener. So I'll be drinking these at home. I know the glass bottle is considered safer than plastic as far as plastic contaminating foods, but they should list them that way.

As far as the product goes, they're really good. Carbonated water and a touch of fruit flavoring with no added sweeteners, coloring or preservatives. 5 stars for the contents. 2 stars for the misleading picture of the product, and the lack of safe portability and difficulty in opening.

review_headline: Tasty Sardines You Can Work Into Your Diet
review_body:
Sardines are Healthy!
==================
Due to the healthy nature of fish in general, and the fact that small fish like sardines have much less exposure to mecury toxicity, I started trying to incorporate them into my diet. Although I wouldn't consider myself a huge fan of fish, reading the label was enough motivation for me to give it a try. 21 grams of protein, 10 grams of total fat and some omega-3 fatty acids to boot? I was excited to get sardines into my diet. Until, I tried them! I tried various brands and many different variations and flavors. I had a really hard time with the skin and the toughness of the fins, and also the crunchiness of the bones. I had a really hard time stomaching sardines.

And These Sardines Are Also Palatable
================================
And then I discovered Crown Prince Skinless & Boneless Sardines in Olive Oil!!! I can't tell you how much better skinless and boneless sardines are! They are delicious and I'm confident with these little gems, I'll be able to work these into my diet. I use these as a nice healthy snack when my day gets crazy and I'm not able to prepare my normal protein and healthy fat go-to foods. Healthy, tasty, and convenient. So glad to have these around when I need them.

product_title: Mrs. Mays Fruit and Nut Toppers, 4 Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_body:
Mrs. May took almonds, cranberries, rice malt, sesame seeds, and sugar and salt -- in that order, so the result is neither sweet nor salty -- and created delicious squareish chunks that look at first glance a lot like granola.

They're square, though, with no flakes. They make a nice snack, chewy rather than crunchy, and tasting a lot like slightly sweet almonds. My first thought was to sprinkle them on salads, where they take the place of croutons and add a nice touch of flavor and texture.

Mix them into muffins or cereal or yogurt for breakfast. You can also include them in the crumb topping of a holiday pie or cobbler, using them in place of nuts or oats. The bag suggests putting them on ice cream, too, and I expect they know what they're talking about.

They're also good just as they are, right from the bag, for a snack. A 50 calorie serving gives you 1 gram each of fiber and sugar and 2 grams of protein, so it's a healthy choice.

product_title: Fairy Dish Washing Liquid (500ml)
review_body:
If you've never used Fairy Liquid, then you are really missing out. I was introduced to this wonderful stuff while living in the UK about 15 years ago. Since then, there are many more types and the bottle has been redesigned, but the fact remains that this product is far superior to anything we have in the US, and worth ordering it off Amazon. Why Proctor & Gamble don't sell this in the US (even by another name, I have a hard time believing that average American's would purchase anything called "Fairy Liquid") is a mystery to me. Perhaps it's some sort of conspiracy to keep us buying washing up liquid that is weak and useless!

I tell you, it's a real conversation starter when a guest finds it in my kitchen, and you really can't go wrong with a product that is gentle on your hands, smells nice, yet does a great job on grease, not to mention the fact that you can pre-treat laundry stains, use a drop or two in a bucket of water to wash windows, or even remove a pesky stain from the carpet.

product_title: Hain, Sea Salt, 26 oz
review_headline: Best Product I've found for a Flavorful Sea Salt But need the iodized for a Healthier Thyroid
review_body:
I prefer the texture and flavor of sea salt and have been using it in place of regular table salt for years. There are many misconceptions involving the health benefits of sea salt vs table salt. I too fell for the 'natural is healthier' thought process for sea salt.
Salt is salt and no matter if its table or sea, it still has sodium which needs to be used in moderation for numerous health reasons.
It actually took a visit to an Endocrinologist appointment with my Dad to realize the error of my ways.
Most sea salt is not Iodized!
Iodine is an essential mineral and is needed for the normal metabolism of cells. Metabolism is the process of converting food into energy. We need iodine for normal thyroid function, and for the production of thyroid hormones.
I had switched to a Non-Iodized Sea salt many years ago for better health and ignorantly was depriving my body of an essential mineral.
I was diagnosed in Feb of 2012 with Hypothyroidism, or underactive thyroid. I now take Levothyroxine daily and feel much better. After the first year I am pleased to report that my thyroid hasn't worsened. I don't know that I can ever correct the damage from the lack of Iodine for so many years, however I'm no longer causing this deficiency in my body.
[[ASIN:B000MDACSK Hain Pure Foods Sea Salt Iodized -- 26 oz]]is the best product I've found and will continue to use this daily for my health and for my family.

review_body: This is admittedly my first experience with any Matcha product, but I was pleasantly surprised by it. I have also dabbled with it as part of a meal replacement smoothie.  Since I am a Young Living distributor, it seemed a natural fit to try some of it in their meal replacement shake.  It created a nice, unique flavor with the hint of vanilla that was left from the YL mix.  I also used it in a gluten-free banana nut muffin and it kicked that up quite a bit too.  The flavor enhanced the muffin and actually seemed to give it a little more moisture. For me, early results with Matcha Green Tea Powder has been very good and I would have no trouble recommending it.

product_title: PowerBar PowerGel, 1.44 Ounce  (Pack of 24)
review_headline: This product is a pretty decent product for what I'm using it for and ...
review_body:
This product is a pretty decent product for what I'm using it for and that's for hypoglycemic attacks and when I'm crashing from fatigue at work. As a diabetic I've been striving to find a small sugar source that is more compact than the bottles of apple juice I've been constantly carrying around in my work bag. I can store 4 of these @ 27g per in the space my 35g per apple juice was. That's a gain of 73g. Now, I don't usually need 35g of sugar when I'm hypoglycemic, I tend to need around 25g. So this was a big plus. Also, the added caffeine is a plus since it helps to cut out the fatigue I get after an attack. The caffeine "rush" is equivalent to about what my job's 6oz coffee provides.

As for the taste, it's okay, nothing special. I'm use to black, crude coffee and dense protein bars so this isn't a huge step off for me. It tastes okay and does what I need. If the taste were a bit improved I'd certainly give it a final star.

product_title: TORNADO ENERGY 16 Ounce (Pack of 24)
review_body:
I purchased both the Ice and Original from BigLots for $.50 each for a 16 oz. bottle. I figured that at $.50 a bottle what's do I have to lose. Well let me tell you what I had to lose. My entire purchase of 2 bottles.

The original at 1st tasted like the brand RipIt energy drink to me or at least reminded me of that drink. I couldn't really pick out any kind of certain flavor to this drink as with other energy drinks you can. I wasn't unpleasant but it didn't shine thru either. This also applies to the Ice flavor as well. As I was finishing off my bottle I decided to look at the contents of the bottle. Carbonated Water was and usually the very 1st thing and yet it didn't seem to have next to any Carbonation at all, perhaps it lost the fizz. I can't really say that this energy drink really gave me a kick of energy or if I would even buy it again even though it was only $.50 per 16 oz. bottle. What I would say is that if you really want to try it find either a BigLots or some place else 1st then pay the amount there asking for a case. I could buy a case cheaper than even with the Amazon Visa card but I wouldn't even want to spend another $.50 on this brand. Also according to the back of the bottle of the Original flavor each bottle has 142mg of Caffeine in it.

As far as the rest of the reviews it's my thought that these are people that are the sellers or the company that made the drink that made the other reviews of this drink.

Also this is from my experience with my tastebuds that this review is based on. It's very possible that you might enjoy this more then I do but I would strongly suggest you find them at a cheap price before spending the amount they want to charge here.

product_title: Stash Tea Company Decaf Chai Spice Tea, 18 Count Tea Bags
review_body:
The Stash Tea Company was founded in 1972, in Tigard, Oregon, a suburb of Portland, and was originally operated out of a Victorian-style house. But, right from the beginning the company focused on making only premium teas. That commitment to quality has propelled Stash Tea to the position of one of America's largest tea companies.

Among Stash Tea's wonderful infusions is Chai Spice Black Tea. \\"Chai\\" comes from the Hindi word for tea, but in the West it is interpreted as Masala Chai, Indian spiced tea. Well, in fact this tea is a wonderful version of Indian spiced tea, based on a mix of Indian black teas, spiced with ginger, cinnamon, allspice, nutmeg and cloves.

Now, as you might expect from that description, this is a spicy tea. When I first opened the package, the smell of cinnamon wafted up to me and I thought, \\"Oh no, cinnamon tea?\\" Well, the flavor is much more complex than that - spicy, but not in an overpowering way. In fact the flavor is exotic and refreshing, and a real joy to drink.

review_body: This is — at least on this site — a deceptively marketed product. Here the product is described as "100% biodegradeable oil". Upon arrival the box read "97% biodegradeable by weight". In practical terms that means that the lid must be carefully peeled off and put in the trash. Also the filter must be removed from the ring that fits into the coffee maker, and it clings stubbornly to the ring. When that's done (and it takes some time) you have only the ring and the coffee grounds which are biodegradable — not much better than the usual K cups that are environmentally really problematic. While "by weight" this may be only 3% of the cup, that's a lot of trash per cup. The coffee inside is OK, nothing special, but this does not offer a realistic option for those who wish to limit the environmental consequences of single-serve coffee.  The Eco-Fill brand of fill-it-yourself cups represents a FAR better approach to using K cups without filling up the landfills.

review_headline: Great product if you use them correctly!
review_body: The Brew and Save Refillable Single-cup Keurig K-Cup Brewers work very well, but you must follow a few simple guidelines IMHO.  Do not use too fine a grind.  I've had great results with the pre ground coffees, but if you grind your own, use maybe one notch coarser grind than you normally would.  Do not overfill or pack the coffee into the Brew and Save, it wont work well at all.  Fill to the line and gently tap on counter to settle the coffee.  Wash the Brew and Save immediately after use and rinse the screen from the BACK not into the top, then tap the Brew and Save lightly, upside down, to remove the excess water.  That's all there is to it.  I'm very happy with the Brew and Save and recommend them without reservation.

product_title: Green Giant Veggie Blend-Ins 100% Vegetable Puree, 36 Ounces (9 Pouches)
review_headline: 100% real vegetables, ready to add wherever you like!
review_body: I'm writing to provide some perspective that seems to be missing (IMHO) from other reviews. The notion of Jessica Seinfeld's cookbook, Deceptively Delicious, which produced this partnership with Green Giant is pretty simple. If you really struggle with getting your kids to eat vegetables, adding puréed vegetables into a variety of recipes- especially those that would not contain vegetable otherwise- can be a way to increase the nutritional value of their food on the whole. Her cookbook contains recipes on how to purée and freeze vegetables on your own, but there are plenty of people who don't have the time or kitchen comfort level for the process. So, here you have these pouches ready to go and they come with recipes from Jessica's cookbook so you can immediately put them to use. As with so much of prepared food, you pay for convenience. However, unlike most prepared foods, please look at the ingredient list of these before you comment. There is one ingredient and that is it. They are 100% puréed vegetables. No additives, no fillers. If you are cost conscious, making puréed cauliflower or squash or spinach is quite simple. But if not, these are high quality and ready to go.    A thought for the, ahem, I'm sure wiser than his years 27 year old (childless?) reviewer who spelled out rather articulately how this is fooling parents into thinking they're feeding their kids healthy food, because the amount of puréed 100% vegetable being added to their, I dunno, brownies, is too small to equal a real portion... Allow me to say:    This is a valid criticism in theory only, not in practice. There are plenty of parents who understand this is not replacing vegetables, nor is it a full serving, but rather this is a 1/4 cup here and a tablespoon there of vegetables where there would otherwise be none, such as in chicken nuggets, or brownies. Yes, we STILL feed our kids vegetables, this doesn't mean we are liars (are you serious?) It means we are parents. We have a Plan A, Plan B and usually a Plan C for anything that matters. And getting the little people to consume veggies matters, so wise 27 year old reviewer... It does not have to be a cure all miracle silver bullet solution to be a worthy addition. And, btw, I know you prob don't have any little people of your own, but depending on how small they are... Sometimes a tablespoon or two IS a serving of vegetables. Just sayin. Ahem, will step down from soap box now...    So, parents and anyone who is health conscious but perhaps time squeezed and looking for a handy ways to add 100% vegetable matter to your diet or anyone for whom you prepare food, knock yourselves out. This oughta do it.

product_title: MOCAFE Thai Tea Drink Mix, 3-Pound Bag
review_headline: San Diego/ LA style Thai tea! I LOVE IT!!!
review_body:
Bring a military wife, being able to travel around the world, and use to manage a Tea shop, this product has been the closest tasting Thai tea I have learned to love. Yes, Thai tea leaves are better, when you know how to really make it right (brewing time, the right temp and ingredients). However, not many people know the real secret to making a delightful taste of Thai tea. Using a Thai tea powder, such as this one, is the shortcut to making it. The powder gives you a stronger taste. No this Thai tea doesn't taste flowery, like they make it in most places in Maryland, this powder Thai tea comes close to tasting like the one you would buy from Tapioca Express (San Diego or LA, CA) style taste. However, this product has to be mix in with the right ingredient, mixing water is not good enough. Here is how I make it for the same tasting Thai tea you'll buy/find in SD/LA:

step 1: boil water and add black tea bag ( black tea is the best kind to use)
step 2: when done boiling and the tea taste strong (tea color should be dark), let it sit and cool.
Step 3: when the tea become room temperature, add the amount of Thai tea powder(make sure the powder is fully dissolve and dark orange color)
step 4: add half and half or coffee mate original favor(this is what i use, and it gives it a creamy taste that i like best)
step 5: add ice or put it in the fridge.
step 6: if you want to make Thai tea slushy/smoothy: Follow step 1-5 and add vanilla ice cream into a blender and mix. ENJOY!!!

BTW, Im living in Spain now and for the next 3 years, I glad I was able to fine and get this powder ship over here. It super nice to be able to enjoy this drink away from home.

product_title: Sweet White Rice Flour, 1 lb.
review_headline: Sweet Rice Flour--you need this in your Gluten free Recipes ( :
review_body:
If you are new to Gluten free baking, you might have had a few disappointments, but Sweet White Rice flour replaces some of the sticky quality that you lose when you eliminate wheat.

Sweet rice flour tends to be more difficult to find even in stores that carry other specialized flours. I had to look online to find it and was very pleased to find Barry Farm's offerings.

I follow Jeanne's gluten free flour mix from her blog the Art of Gluten Free baking.

1 1/4 cup brown rice flour, 1 1/4 cup white rice flour, 1 cup tapioca flour, 1 cup sweet rice flour (that's the Barry farm brand), 2 scant teaspoons (just a teensy bit under each spoon) of xanthum gum (the rest of the sticky quality)

So far I've successfully made carrot cake, and oatmeal applesauce cookies. Granted these are wetter desserts, but give it a try.
