review_body:
My daughter and I have enjoyed the different flavors throughout the summer. However, these drinks are so delicious, they are Great for anytime. My favorite is the Summer Peach, and my daughter's favorite is the Black Cherry, but we do enjoy a variety of flavors that are available, and so easy to make a cold and delicious drink.

What I like about these little squeeze bottles is that you can carry them around anywhere, and you only need a cold bottle of water. In addition, I like the idea that you can make it the way you would enjoy it the most, either strong, or light. When we make the Summer Peach, we use 3 drops, and love the taste. Also, we love that we no longer have to add sugar, and the sweet honey in the tea is satisfying.

Another plus factor is that we do not get thirsty after drinking one glass or bottle, as we did with soda, and this drink is much more healthy than soda. 10 Calories per fl.oz is another Bonus, and it contains a good source of vitamin C. The price for a pack of 4 is very reasonable, and we now want to stock up on it, especially for the extreme heat in the summer of AZ. Highly recommended!

product_title: Honest Tea Mango Acai White Tea 16 Oz. Glass Bottles 12 Pack
review_headline: Very Good, But Would Be Even Better Without The Added Sugar.
review_body:
Honest Tea Mango Acai White Tea 16 Oz. (473 mL) Glass Bottles 12 Pack, by Honest Tea.
This Honest Tea Mango Acai White Tea, is as the label says, just a tad sweet at 18 grams of sugar per 16 ounce bottle. I do not know why they had to add cane sugar, as the sweet mango provides its own sugar. Processed foods in general, contain too much sugar and salt. Thankfully, this brand of tea only contains 10mg of salt per bottle.
Anyway, the tea tastes very good. If it did not contain the cane sugar and did not come in a breakable glass bottle, I would give it a rating of 5 stars, but with the added sugar and the glass bottle, I can only give it four stars. As a pre-diabetic, I have to avoid sugar. Even a 16.9 ounce bottle of Coca-Cola at 55g of sugar (from Honest Tea's parent company), will raise my blood sugar enough to leave me feeling very tired.

According to the Honest Tea label on the bottle:
\\"After 4,700 years, there's a new fashion in tea. Introducing white tea - grown from the same plant as green and black tea, but picked at a 'youthful' stage. White tea has less caffeine than other teas, but is still loaded with healthy antioxidants. And instead of accessorizing with high fructose corn syrup (so last century), we add a pinch of organic cane sugar, mangos and the superfruit acai. It's white, and it's OK to drink after Labor Day. This season, white is the new black and green. Honestly yours, Seth and Barry
p.s. Sambazon(R) acai (pronounced 'ah-sigh-ee') is a sustainably harvested fruit from the Amazon rainforest. In addition to being high in antioxidants, acai also has omegas, the good-for-you fatty acids. To learn more about acai, visit our friends at www.sambazon.com.\\"

product_title: Kellogg's Special K Pastry Crisp, 4.4 Ounce
review_headline: My favorite flavor out of all of them!
review_body:
Special K Pastry Crisps are my go-to snack bars. At only 100 calories and a decadent, sweet taste, they've taken reign to satisfy my standard granola bar fix on pretty much a daily basis. I've tried all the flavors—even the limited edition ones that I could only find on Amazon!—and this Cookies and Crème flavor is by far, my favorite. They taste like a flat, healthy version of an Oreo cookie! YUM!

I am not blind to the criticism about this product line not being completely natural, using artificial sweeteners, etc etc etc. I do consider myself a healthy eater, and while I acknowledge these bars are not 100% clean, at just 100 calories and the prepackaged convenience, they're hardly anything to complain about either. I'm sure I could whip up a healthier snack bar if I had the time and ingredients, but unfortunately, I am a full-time student AND I have a job, so that isn't going to happen. I am perfectly fine with having processed snacks in moderation; they are a good pick-me-up during a long day when I don't have the time or energy to sit down for a full meal, and these definitely lie on the healthier end of the snack-food spectrum too.

I consider Pastry Crisps the healthier, tastier version of Poptarts. I always liked Poptarts but not how they made me feel sick afterwards. They're not exactly the most diet-friendly food either. Thankfully, Special K came out with a thinnified version of them, and they're freakin' delicious! I always stock up on these, but will definitely be buying this flavor again in the future.

product_title: Golden State DeLite Monthly Fruit Club - 12 Month Club
review_body: The concept of this product is so amazing, and for the first few months we were really happy. But then the quality of the fruit just went away. I found myself calculating how much each piece of fruit cost and how I could get similar quality around the corner at a quarter the price. From my point of view, if you charge a premium price and market your product as an expensive gift, you need to bring the value. I'm actually embarrassed that I gave this as a gift to my wife. She still smiles as she bites into the mushy, prematurely-picked peaches and just-off mangos, but she's clearly giving me the it's-the-thought-that-counts benefit. My recommendation is to keep shopping. Golden State is a huge disappointment in the most important area; the quality of the fruit itself. I really wanted this one to be good...

product_title: Typhoo Tea 80ct Tea Bags 8.82 ounces 250g
review_headline: My go-to tea (for now, maybe for good)
review_body:
I live in the U.S. so my tea options are more or less limited. I'd began with Lipton, as most do, then tried P.G. Tips some years ago. It's fine, but for some reason I switched to Tetley's a few years back. It held up well, great flavor and aroma, until I bought a new box last month to find the flavor was totally different than before. Uninspiring. I have no idea what changed but have seen comments across the net from those who have made the same sad observation. Yorkshire Gold was as strong as often reputed but just didn't appeal to me. Then someone suggested I try Red Rose, but it was not impressive; almost identical to the current Tetley's.

So today I found Ty-phoo at Big Lots...figured for 4.50 a box it was worth the experiment.

The red box full of three sealed foil bags was a nice discovery. The fragrance was nice...a bit more pronounced than I recall any other being, no doubt due to the foil bags.

My first cup was excellent. I take my tea unsweetened with a small shot of cream or milk and it was very, very good. I soaked the second cup's bag a bit long and like other reviewers noticed a profound bitterness that overwhelmed the flavor and left a strong aftertaste that lingers for the better part of an hour. Lesson learned -- do not oversoak this tea. However, it will now be my go-to for the foreseeable future. I'm interested in trying Barry's if I ever come across some but for now, it'll be Ty-Phoo.

product_title: Milka Naps Mix, Singles 147g new pack
review_body:
The Milka Naps Mix Gift Box is a fun, unique gift for those tired of Whitman's and the usual American brands. Nothing wrong with Whitman's, but sometimes a change of look and flavor is nice.

As a sampler, it provides only a few of the Milka options. Four flavors are here: noisette, hazelnuts, alpine milk and strawberry. All are delicious, though I don't like strawberry/chocolate (in any candy) personally, and give those away to eager friends. The Naps box are perfect for coffee tables and as a standalone dish at work.

Milka and its famous purple cow, is owned by Kraft, is an eastern European chocolate originally produced in Switzerland and is available in Germany, Austria, Hungary and other nearby countries.

Distribution is still weak in the United States, but can be found increasingly in larger cities. Usually, then, it is found only in international grocery stores, though it pops up in eclectic grocers from time to time. It has been around 100 years. Whether or not Kraft will change the recipe has yet to be seen. For now, the texture and taste are better than Hershey's and Nestle. It is a smoother, creamier basic chocolate.

I fully recommend the Milka Naps Mix Gift Box.

Anthony Trendl
HungarianBookstore.com

product_title: Cento Skinless & Boneless Sardines in Olive Oil, 4.375-Ounce Tins (Pack of 25)
review_body:
Sometimes there are fewer sardines in the can and more olive oil. I guess this wouldn't be entirely bad, except I can't think of what to do with the sardine tasting olive oil and I throw it out. A little higher quality control would make this a better product and would have earned it five stars.

I wonder which costs the manufacturer more, sardines or olive oil? I can understand there being fewer sardines in the can if the fish costs more than the olive oil. Or, if the olive oil costs more than the fish, then it would be costing the manufacturer more to put fewer sardines in the can. In this case we must conclude that the sardines and the olive oil must cost the same amount. But, maybe there is a third expense like the cost of maintaining a high standard of quality control. In this case we must conclude that the cost of higher quality control exceeds the cost differential between sardines and olive oil. From macroeconomics we can assume a 2% annual gain in global manufacturing efficiency. With this in mind we can conclude that the relative increasing cost of labor in time would make quality control relatively more expensive, and that the quality of this product would eventually go down to three stars. On the other hand, if there would be a way to automate the quality control to guarantee the number of sardines in the can in time this could increase the number of stars that this product would receive. If these two functions were plotted on the same graph an average could be made to determine the overall trend...

This is the kind of pondering that happens from me writing these reviews at 3:45am...!

review_headline: Coffee Without the Actual Coffee Flavor; but Plenty of Caffeine(!!)
review_body:
This doesn't taste like coffee as we commonly expect today. It's more like ground coffee you can buy in a supermarket or even tea that's been brewed for quite a long time. Think Folger's or Maxwell House--or the stuff you get at Denny's.

Here's a VERY telling statistic: As of June 2014, this \\"coffee\\" ranks #79 at Amazon under Grocery & Gourmet Food > Beverages > Coffee > Coffee SUBSTITUTES. I'm not making this up; apparently the majority of Amazon customers see this as a \\"coffee substitute.\\"

If you're going to drink \\"weak\\" coffee without a lot of strong coffee flavor, you might as well save yourself quite a bit of money by buying non-$tarbucks. Buy whatever's cheap in a can at the supermarket, and you'll probably be just as happy.

Also note, the lighter the roast, the higher the caffeine content. (I think that is why lighter roast coffees are popular with some folks.)

I mean it... I've tried them all, whatever town I'm in, wherever I am I go for my espresso fix. And I am a Purist..... Straight up, no sweeteners, no creamy gunk, no fluffy foam -- just pure ORGANIC dark espresso coffee.

The convenience of my Keurig machine, the fact I can use my own (non-tap) water and the fact there's no lines, and no cross-contamination of flavors -- which occasionally happens even in the best coffee places -- is just perfect.

It is now my go-to coffee so I purchase it in bulk to be certain it's available. The proliferation of Keurig and other machines like it, their small size, makes it practical to own more than one, so you can take it to work, your second home or, when visiting family take it with you! If you think that's a crazy idea and any coffee will do, then you might not know just how good, great, superb the perfect cup of coffee can make the day feel!

We have also tried their Fog Lifter blend, and it is bolder and also delicious. I recommend this brand to all my friends who have Keurigs.

product_title: Knorr MiniCubes Cilantro Seasoning, 2.8-Ounce
review_headline: Great product; misleading quantity description, and overpriced
review_body:
Buyers can be quick to get angry and yell "false advertising" or "bait and switch." I don't think either are true here; I'm sure the sellers intended to post their product accurately.

Here's the problem: the listing says "Knorr Minicubes Cilantro Seasoning 2.8-Ounce Boxes - (Pack of 24)" directly under the in-stock and sold-by indicators at the top of the page. Since each box contains 20 cubes (not 24), you assume you're getting 24 boxes of 20 cubes for $5.17, which would have been a terrific on-line price. You actually get one box of 20 for $5.17, which is a terrible price. I've bought them at bricks-and-mortar stores for $.99 per box of 20 cubes.

That said, the cubes themselves are wonderful. The give a great flavor to home-made salsa and other dishes, and I've always loved using them. I'll be watching to see if the sellers amend their description to correct the error, which -- again -- I'm sure was an honest mistake with no deception intended.

Usually I open one end enough to remove the flavor packet then squeeze it closed and use the other hand to crumble the noodles into smaller size easily scooped by a spoon. That was not possible with this product. It was so hard that even when grasped by both hands I was unable to "snap" the noodles in half or crunch them into pieces.

I spent 20+ years in the military and while overseas would purchase this same brand many times and would occasionally run across long stored items that were a bit stale. None however were bricks! Don't know how this occurred, don't care. All I do know is that they tasted as stale as they were before cooking and will not be eating the remainder.

Returning is a pain in the ass so I'll be "eating" the cost of this purchase and pray that the other batch of chicken noodles I purchased at the same time were better stored than these pork ones. Haven't tried them yet because I'm still trying to get the taste out of my mouth of this batch.

product_title: KASHI BAR CHEWY CHOC ALMND SEAS, 7.4 OZ
review_body:
A nutritionist recommended Kashi chocolate and almond granola bars to me. I used to think you shouldn't eat chocolate when you're dieting or trying to eat healthy. Not true! Research shows a bit of dark chocolate everyday is good for your heart. It's hard to believe these delicious bars are that good for you! They taste a tad sinful, but are only 140 calories. When you are craving chocolate or something sweet (like a dessert), these are a great alternative. You don't need to feel deprived when you are dieting with these bars. Desserts taste good, but often have you feeling like you ate something not good for you. You feel heavy afterwards. These bars won't leave your stomach feeling that way.

They have 6g of protein, 160mg ALA Omega-3, are 16% of your fiber, fairly low in sugar at 7g - the nutritionist said try to stay under 8g for cereal- and low in sodium at 5% of your DV, They are also low in fat at 6% DV. It's amazing something so tasty is this healthy. They are naturally sweetened with rich dark chocolate, wildflower honey with NO high fructose corn syrup. They have 7 whole grains and chia. The 6g of protein come from whole almonds and crispy soy grahams. They have a touch of sea salt.

These are my favorite kashi bars. I love to put a couple in my purse when running errands or going to a meeting. They are a healthy and surprising delicious snack during the day. You can really taste the big squares of dark chocolate, the almonds and the touch of sea salt - a mouth-watering mix. Congratulations to Kashi for creating something this delicious which is so healthy.

I've only had them about 3 weeks so I can't comment on how long they will last. One word of advice, though: don't jam them onto your hands by putting your fingers between each other and pulling down. The seam between the fingers was starting to look strained when I did that. Instead, pull down each finger on alternating sides until it's mostly on. Then interlace your fingers to finish.

product_title: Dandy Blend - Instant Dandelion Beverage Single Servings
review_body:

I still use a couple teaspoons, but with other brands I was using 3 heaped teaspoons as a comparison. (I like strong coffee, so need a similar flavour punch). It tastes great with cow milk, almond milk or soy milk, and is also drinkable black. I like how when you pour boiling water on it, before you add any milk, it has a nice thick crema on top. Does it taste the same as coffee? No. I can certainly taste the difference. You won't fool a confirmed coffee drinker, but it's got a good depth and richness to the flavour that other coffee substitutes lack.

I drink this because if I drink coffee, tea or cocoa in the afternoon/ evening, it messes up my sleep routine. But I still like to have a hot drink at that time of day and the Dandy blend is perfect for this. Also, dandelion is a known liver/digestive tonic and that's a good thing to have regularly!

product_title: Dave's Gourmet Sauce, 5 Ounce
review_headline: It's hot. But it's not the hottest (or even close).
review_body:
Since reviews for several different hot sauces seem to be lumped together here, my review is for Dave's Ghost Pepper Naga Jolokia Hot Sauce.

This stuff is hot. But for a seasoned hot sauce aficionado this is not the ultimate in heat or pain. If you have conquered Dave's Original Insanity Hot Sauce then this is not going to impress you. This is disappointing because the whole point of buying ghost pepper hot sauce is for extreme heat.

Do not be fooled though, this stuff IS hot. And if you aren't seasoned this is plenty hot to put you in serious pain. But since this is ghost pepper sauce I was expecting something hotter than original Insanity Sauce and this is not it. It's a step below on the heat scale. Not a big step below but still below. With Insanity Sauce I have to be more careful about how much I put into my dish. But with this ghost pepper version I find myself erring on the side of putting in too much rather than not enough. This one is more forgiving. Also, while the original insanity sauce is thick like lava, this is runny like regular Tabasco Sauce. Whether that is better or not is a a matter of personal preference.

That being said, this one is still good for those times when I don't want to go all out so it's not without its merits. But if you're looking for ultimate in heat, this is not it.

product_title: Lorann Hard Candy Flavoring Oils YOU Pick the Flavors 12 Pack + One Dram Dropper by LorAnn Oils
review_body:
I ordered these as I am beginning to foray into candymaking. Last night I made a double batch of meringues and divided it into 7 bowls so I could test the flavors. I made about 1/2-3/4 of a cup worth of each flavor - here are my thoughts on the flavors so far:

Raspberry - tasted great, but gave a slight pink tinge that I didn't care for.

Champagne - I guess I'm not sure what I was expecting this to taste like. It's really hard to describe, maybe because I've never had a really fancy bottle of champagne. I never would've been able to guess that it was supposed to be champagne if I didn't know. Very subtle taste - needed about 15 drops to taste.

Cheesecake - smelled great, but tasted really artificial. Definitely tasted like cheesecake, just really fake cheesecake. Needed about 15 drops to adequately flavor.

Mango - I was the most excited for this one, and it was the one that disappointed me the most. It tastes really medicinal to me.

Peach - loved this, tastes just like peach.

Pear - loved this, it tastes a little like Absolut pear vodka more than just pear, but I still really liked it. Required about 10 drops to flavor.

Pomegranate - loved this, tasted great but it also gave a bit of a pink tinge.

I ordered almond, amaretto, bavarian cream, marshmallow, and vanilla butternut as well, but I haven't had a chance to test them yet. I really liked these, however, so I do plan to purchase more.

product_title: DaVinci SUGAR FREE Banana Syrup w/ Splenda 750 mL
review_headline: A wonderful flavor to help diabetics make a good tasting treat or snack!
review_body:
If you are a diabetic and have ever attended a nutrition class for diabetics you probably have heard of this product. We have a whole collection of the different flavors and I have posted a photo of some of the ones we use the most. This is an ideal additive to diabetic cooking, baking of foods or the mixing of drinks. It is sugar free and calorie free and extremely low in sodium.

These mixes are ideal for use in coffee, tea drinks, Italian sodas, cocktails, pancakes, waffles, diabetic cakes and muffins. You can find a lot of diabetic recipes and substitute these flavorings for ingredients that have more sugar and calories. The result is surprisingly good and it will help reduce your sugar and calorie intake while helping you add more flavor to your food.

We miss shakes and ice cream and this is a good flavor to use to make such a treat. Peel and freeze a banana in 3 to 4 pieces in a zip lock bag. Put it into a blender with 6 to 8 ounces of skim milk, a couple of tablespoons of vanilla or banana instant sugar free pudding, one to two table spoons of this flavoring and ¾ cup of crushed ice. Blend this until smooth and you have a good tasting dietetic fruit smoothie that makes a good snack. You can even freeze this and have a sort of banana ice cream treat. We also used to add in a vanilla protein mix that we would add into one of these to make a light meal.

Flavorings like these are nice to spice up your low calorie drinks and food and the Da Vinci Gourmet brand is the best we have found. They are internationally recognized as the highest quality flavoring made and one tablespoon = a free food exchange for a diabetic.

I strongly recommend this to you as a great product!

product_title: Organic Raw Cacao Powder - Best Dark Chocolate Taste - Pure Natural Unsweetened Cocoa 1lb/ 16oz
review_headline: Very impressed by this healthy Cocoa Power that is good for me and tastes great!
review_body:
UPDATED REVIEW 4.14.16

First I will say that I grew up in a household that always used Hershey's Cocoa for everything: Baking, Making Cocoa, Making Shakes etc. And our family bought every Hershey cookbook we could find and so the tradition continued over time....

Fast forward to this present day: So I opened up the Pure Raw Organic Cacoa (Cocoa) Powder. It is the real deal! This is how I tested it over the other brand and my results:

TASTE TESTS OF EACH COCOA DRIED in TEASPOON:

1) Placed a small amount in a teaspoon of this the Pure Raw Organic Cacoa Powder.
2) From the Hershey Cocoa tin, I placed the same amount of Cocoa in another teaspoon.
3) Tasted the Hershey Cocoa first. Tasted fine, texture smooth, semi dark and smooth taste.
4) Rinsed my mouth with pure water to be fair to tasting the Pure Raw Cacao.
5) Tasted the Pure Raw Cacao Powder in another teaspoon (the same amount). Noticed that the taste is just a bit slightly bitter and stronger, yet it tastes fresher than the Hersheys.

TASTE TESTS IN MY COCOA:
1) Found my Mother's old timey HOMEMADE COCOA RECIPE but I changed it to add per cup: 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon.
And NO SUGAR, I added Raw Brown Sugar instead for this recipe and the Raw Organic one...(I used to use Splenda, however I discovered that it is not as healthy as other sweeteners...so I began using Raw Brown Sugar in March 2016 and add it to my tea, smoothies and when I use this Cacao Powder).

2) Tested each cup of Cocoa - With the same amount of Raw Brown Sugar added, I had to add 1/2 more teaspoon of Raw Brown Sugar to the recipe with the Pure Raw Sugar and a tad less Cocoa using the Pure One. Note that I found that Raw Brown Sugar is very sweet so you may want to use less.
Results doing it this way? The Pure Raw Cacao tasted RICHER and FRESHED more like one would expect from a dark chocolate.
****Keep in mind with this: You will need less of it then regular Cocoa because it is stronger. For me taste, I used about 15 percent less.

TEST ON CHOCOLATE SHAKES:

1) I did FIRST my old Hershey Shake and used my regular Blue Bell Vanilla Ice Cream and NO SWEETENER as I did not need it.

2) Then I tested the Pure Raw Organic Cacao and added about a teaspoon of Raw Brown Sugar.Both were great, however, the Pure Raw Organic Cacao had a RICHER TASTE in Cocoa and my Chocolate Shakes. Put it this way, all was gone!!!

I totally love these mushrooms!! I remember these from when i worked as head chef of an asian restaurant.... Such a interesting flavor! honestly one of the the most flavorful ingredients in the kitchen...

The stems, like NEVER soften up. Ive had stems soaking for about 2 weaks in water, and they were still not tender. Cut around the stems if you want to cook these. You can cook the stems in steaming water/ boiling water/ sautee them in oil for along time, and eventually they will soften.

DO NOT throw away the water you use to soak these mushrooms. I do rinse the mushrooms for about 1 second, and let go a brownish liquid.... but you dont have to. if you let these mushrooms soak, the water is an extract of all the mushroom flavors... It is high in components that will increase the umami flavor of any dish u add it to, and it will increase the flavor with a complexity of its smokiness as well. I usually use a little bit of "shitaki water" as water when i add a little bit of chicken bullionm, then i add it to stirfrys, or fried rice.

product_title: Melitta Coffee Maker, Single Cup Pour-Over Brewer with Travel Mug (Pack of 2)
review_body:
This is the the least expensive complete family-sized pour-over coffee brewer on the market. Melitta is known for their inexpensive pour-over coffee brewers. This version makes about 30 oz, or six 5-oz "cups" of coffee. It is easy to use and, if you are used to an automatic brewer this allows you to control various elements that the "machine" does not. Here are some instructions for using your Melitta Coffee maker.

The short version is this:
1) Heat the water
2) Dose your coffee in the filter in the brew basket
3) Pour-over
4) Enjoy

The long version is this

1) Measure out your water
I use a cheap electric kettle and put only as much water in it as I intend to pour. This prevents any over-pouring. You can add 2-4 oz if you intend to do the pre-soaking (step #4)

2) Heat the water
It should be a little below boiling. I let my kettle heat to boiling, then immediately take it off the heating element and give it 10 secs or so to cool down and stop "gurgling" (boiling). It's important to preserve good heat, so don't lollygag with the next few steps or else you'll lose so much heat that the extraction doesn't work well. The heat matters because coffee is largely an oil, and as you know about water and oil, they don't mix. It is the heat that chemically effects the coffee grinds so they give off the maximum flavor. This is also why cold-brew systems take so long, not much heat. Of course, if there's too much heat you can scald the grinds and it will taste burnt.

3) Apply the filter
I do this while the water stops boiling. Also, This pour-over takes a #4 sized flat-bottom filter. These are easily found at the grocery store whether Melitta Brand or an off-brand. These are not "basket shaped" or cone-shaped. They have a tapered shape with seam-like line across the bottom that makes it a bit like the cone and the basket at the same time.

4) Pre-soak the filter
You can use a separate (preferably glass) measuring cup to measure out the extra water (2-4ozs) and then pour this over the empty filter. Let it drain completely through before proceeding to the next step. This is to wash away any added flavors that the paper might add to your coffee. Most people skip this step. I myself skip it a lot too.

5) Add coffee
1-2 tbsp per 5-8oz cup. I usually use about 8 level tbsps of medium grind coffee. That is the "typical" grind that pre-ground coffees are in. But if you use your own grinder, this would be right about the middle in-between french press and espresso grind. To be honest, there's not a lot of difference between the flavor from different grinds but understand that the finer the grind, the more the water will be exposed to the coffee (i.e., more surface area to expose) and the slower it will pour. This can also slow down the drip speed, meaning it takes longer and the coffee has cooled down a little more. If, however, you use a coarser grind (French Press) then it will be a faster pour, with less exposure, meaning less extraction. The resultant cup will be quicker, weaker, and hotter.

6) Wet the grinds
This means pour just enough of the hot water to soak all the grinds, and then stop. The grinds will saturate or "blossom" at this point. This step is crucial for extracting maximum flavor.

7) Wait 30-45 secs as the grinds blossom

8) Pour the rest of the hot water in a smooth, slow, circular motion trying to evenly expose all the beans yet avoiding the paper--no sense trying to extract more paper flavor right! If you live in australia, you should swirl it counter-clockwise (jk).

[Super secret step #8.5--when it looks like all the water has drained through fold the edges of the filter down on top of the grinds, covering them entirely, then press gently to extract a few more droplets of extra-strong coffee.]
---
9) Clean-up
Dump the filter and grinds; rinse the brew-basket and carafe. While a warm water rinse is fine most of the time, you should use a dishwasher or soap and water occasionally to prevent staining, and keep the oils out so they don't effect the flavor and make all your new cups of coffee taste like old cups of coffee.

Points to Ponder
* The finished product will not have any of the crema one might expect from an espresso, and it won't be as strong as a French press or an Aeropress.
* Instead, it will produce a smooth, quick, cup of American-style coffee.
* The easy-cleanup is a major reason for preferring paper-filters over reusable filters. Also, the reusable filters tend to retain some of the old coffee-flavor over time and are not as "reusable" as one might hope.
* This makes 30oz of coffee if you use enough water to reach the metal band of the carafe. It says "1,2,3,4 cups" on the side, but it really has room for 10 more ounces, beyond those markings.
* One advantage over smaller brewers is you can always make less than 30ozs of coffee in a larger pot--just use less coffee and less water--but with a smaller brewer you cannot safely make much more than the recommended amounts. The 6-cup brewer also supports size #1 and #2 filters as well, for 1-3 cups of coffee. Or you can use the standard #4 filter, and just use less grinds and water.
* This is cheaper than automatic coffee-makers, and produces as good or a better results.
* The carafe is decent and multi-purpose. As long as you rinse the coffee smell out, it works just fine with any other drinks. Plus, it has a third-piece, a lid, that can be used to keep the heat in if you aren't ready to pour yet.
* The brew-basket fits on all sorts of other glasses or jugs with a medium to small opening. I use this brew-basket to brew directly into a thermos jug, or into a tall kitchen glass for a "fancy" coffee drink like an iced coffee or milk-coffee.
* The lid can be used as a drip catcher/stand for the brew basket when you need to set it down so as to pour the carafe.
* The brew basket has a protrusion at the bottom that is not visible in the cover-art. This makes it impossible to just set down on the counter. I set the brew basket in the lid, or just toss it in the sink or dishwasher.
* All parts are dishwasher safe, but I generally don't use a dishwasher since I'm never sure how tough the glass is.

Happy Brewin!

product_title: Natural Value Coconut Milk, 13.5-Ounce Containers
review_headline: This is NOT authentic coconut milk
review_body:
The ingredients are listed as "coconut extract and water." That's a manufactured food, as far as I'm concerned. Coconut milk is "Coconut milk is the liquid that comes from the grated meat of a brown coconut," according to Wikipedia. what the heck is "coconut extract" anyway? Google that and you'll come up with listings for little 1 or 2 oz. bottles of flavoring, primarily for baking. Wikipedia doesn't have a listing for it.

Nor does this stuff look and behave like the authentic coconut milk I used to buy before it became so darned popular (and food manufacturers figured out they could soak the public). I am keenly disappointed. I gave it 2 stars instead of 1 only because it doesn't have the BPA cans or guar gum, and one presumes it is organic.. I'll never buy this again.

review_headline: French Roast Too Dark For Most, But I Liked It.
review_body:
I ordered a 5lb bag of French Roast. When I opened the bag the beans were practically sweating oil. I used it in my drip coffee maker, a french press, and an aeropress. Ground it with a burr mill grinder (nothing fancy). I thought it tasted pretty good. It has a strong flavor, not sweet, mildly bitter. But I usually go for dark roasts. My roommates and friends seemed to think it was too dark.

For the price these 5lb bags are a great deal. That being said I live in a house with 4 coffee drinkers. A 5lb bag seems to last us about a month. I usually break the bag into smaller vacuum sealed bags which I keep in the freezer. Flavor doesn't really seemt to diminish with the vacuum bags. Also the bags never seem to lose vacuum or bulge which suggests to me that the beans are not releasing much gas by the time they get to me, which I read could be a problem.

The main reason I bought this coffee was price. And compared to any other coffee I've tried in stores or online, it's a real bargain.

We've since moved onto the Papua New Guinea City Roast which everyone (including me) seems to enjoy.

product_title: Tinkyada Brown Rice Pasta, Lasagne, 10-Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_headline: whole grain, gluten-free, and they're good!
review_body:
I recently had the idea to take a ravioli recipe and make it into lasagna instead (ravioli is quite a pain to prepare from scratch). I went looking for the whole wheat Hodgson Mill lasagna noodles I usually buy and my supermarket was all out of them. I prefer whole grain pastas and I saw these from Tinkyada, so I bought them instead. I've had good luck with Tinkyada pastas in the past, so I figured I would be happy with these.

These are pretty good lasagna noodles. They're the kind you have to cook (by boiling) on the stovetop first, but I prefer that kind. (Some of the no-boil ones get too crunchy for my taste.) They didn't stick together during cooking; the water from cooking was slightly discolored, but that seems common to Tinkyada pastas and doesn't affect the taste at all.

I followed the directions on the box and boiled these for slightly less than the stated cooking time, since I planned to put them in the oven afterwards. If I had it to do over again, I would probably boil them for a minute or two longer, as they were a little tough. (Also, I know that other Tinkyada brown rice pastas stand up well to overcooking.) However, despite the toughness, I was pleased with the result. I thought the taste was very good, as well, and they were not too \\"rustic\\" as whole grain pastas tend to be. The lasagna made with them has also been very good as leftovers.

A few of these did rip apart just a little after cooking. This was about the same as what I've experienced with other brands of lasagna noodles, though.

If you're going to use these in lasagna, make sure the top is covered with cheese and sauce, or the top layer of noodles will dry out a little bit.

Overall, I'm pleased with these and would definitely consider buying them again. (If you are making a huge, family-sized lasagna, you may want two boxes.) If you need to eat food that's gluten-free, these will also work for you!

product_title: Lea & Perrins The Original Worcestershire Sauce, 128-Ounce Bottles (Pack of 3)
review_headline: This is the Original Worcestershire Sauce and, by far,  the Best. But what will you do with 3 gallons?
review_body:
I've tried other so-called Worcestershire sauces and none have come close to the original Lee and Perrins.

At $47.00 including shipping for 3 gallons it was a great buy. Three of us split this order.

I use this sauce in Bloody Marys and on steaks, hamburgers or any other type of beef. It is also wonderful in french onion soup. Unlike other reviewers, I don't marinate my steaks in it. Rather I douse it liberally over steaks, a number of times, as they cook on the grill.

But the question remains, what will you do with 3 gallons? You could split it up with friends as I did. That is 384 ounces! First consider the price advantage. 10 to 15 ounces of this sauce costs about $11.00 on Amazon. Update (August 2014) - now $5.44 ($0.54 / oz) & FREE Shipping on orders over $35. So there is/was a huge price advantage even if you threw two gallons away. .

Taste: a Bloody Mary would never be complete without a dash of this sauce. However you'll never need very much of this sauce for that purpose. But on steaks, hamburgers, etc using a heavy dose several times per side as they cook (I don't marinate) --- you can use up quite a bit of sauce. What I've found is this keeps the steaks very juicy and imparts a very subtle flavor that you'll miss when it is absent.

Highly recommended for steaks/beef, french onion soup, and Bloody Marys

Update (August 2014): Since smaller bottles are more fairly priced think twice about ordering 3 gallons

The first place I looked? Amazon, of course. They shipped from the UK and took a month to be delivered. They arrived today.

I think these are one of those “acquired taste” type of snacks. I was expecting them to taste like Funjuns, but they are far, far away from Funjun-land. I like pickles, but these are a punch in the mouth of sour pickle flavor. They get better as you eat them and dissolve into an oniony flavor, but they are not something you’d want to eat before kissing someone. Ever.

product_title: Kellogg's Special K Coffee House Breakfast Shake, Vanilla Cappuccino, 10 Ounce, 4 count, (Pack of 6)
review_body:
Now I have to be honest and say that I'm not a huge fan of cappuccino or Vanilla, so with that being said, I gave it to my husband to try who is. After he drank the free one, he had me go back to the store to buy more. He LOVED IT ! He said that it absolutely doesn't taste like something that is "good for you". You can taste the vanilla AND the cappuccino and has a rich and creamy taste.

The good points are:
We've never tried any other breakfast shakes, so we couldn't compare this to any other, but with less then 200 calories and 10g of protein...it's definitely going to be his "go to" breakfast when he's in a hurry to leave for work and this is ONE breakfast he can have while driving and not have to worry about consuming and driving. :)

The down sides we found was the amount of sodium in this. At 230 mgs...that seems quite high to us for just one protein drink, so he won't be able to drink this every single day, but overall, still a great option for him.

The other down side is the price....at $6.99/4 pack...while we don't know what the average protein drink goes for, we felt like that's a bit pricey, however, I did find it on sale at our local grocery store for $5.99 and then I was able to use my $1.50 off coupon, so for THAT price, it's DEFINITELY worth it. But my husband likes it so much, that he'll make me buy it regardless.

For the very last tip, my husband told me to make SURE I told everyone that they MUST drink them cold for the best taste. He drank one that was room temperature and wasn't as thrilled as the ones that came out of the fridge the next day.

product_title: XS Energy Drink Cranberry Grape Blast Twelve 12 Oz. Cans
review_headline: Great effects, but the taste is a little weird
review_body:
My brother used to be an IBO for Amway, but I never really gave XS a chance until now. I read reviews saying that this is the best flavor, so I gave it a try. I don't know what those people were talking about, because I think this flavor tastes like cough syrup (probably because it has no sugar). I would not recommend this flavor to anyone, unless you like the way cough syrup tastes, which I don't. But don't get me wrong; the effects of this drink were amazing. I've never felt so awake and alert from just drinking one energy drink before. After you get past the taste, the effects are definitely worth it. This is why I gave it a 5 star review despite the taste. I'll never buy this flavor again, but I also happened to order a variety case, and I must say that the "Wild Berry Blast" "Peach Tea Blast" and "Electric Lemon Blast" are the best flavors overall. The "Electric Lemon" flavor tastes just like a carbonated light lemonade, but the "Wild Berry" flavor was a little harder to describe. But trust me, it tastes really good, especially when compared to the "Cranberry Grape" Flavor. The "Peach Tea" flavor is great because it tastes just like unsweetened peach tea, but it has the effects of an energy drink. It's hard to rank these flavors, but here's my top 3:

1) Electric Lemon Blast (because I love lemonade)
2) Peach Tea Blast (because I love iced tea), and
3) Wild Berry Blast.

review_body: Some people don't know honey is flavored differently depending on the flowers/pollen that is gathered to make the honey.  This flavor of honey is my all time favorite.  If you like the scent and taste of oranges, this is worth a try.

product_title: Frontier Anise Seed Whole, 16 Ounce Bags (Pack of 2)
review_body: This Anise Seed is great quality and has a nice full flavor when used as a tea. It is awesome to serve after dinner and my guests always love it.

product_title: Stonewall Kitchen Aged Cheddar Beer Crackers, 5 Ounce
review_body: These crackers are called "Aged Cheddar & Beer" on the box but would be more accurately labeled "Tasteless & The End of Your Hopes and Dreams." They are what disappointment would be if someone decided to bake disappointment into little squares that crumbled at the slightest touch. product_title: Spicy World Golden Raisins, Premium, 2 Pound
review_body: I have been getting my raisins from the grocery store.  No more of that for me.  From now on, it is Golden Raisins from Spicy World.  They are plump and juicy.  Taste very fresh and delicious.

product_title: Kauai Coffee Medium Roast Single Serve Cups, Garden Isle, 20 Count
review_body:
This is a very nice, relatively light coffee. The flavor is a bit rich without any bitterness. If you're looking for a strong, dark roast, you won't find it here. But if you want something on the mild side but still flavorful, you've got it.

Note that most of the poor reviews of this seem to be for a different product, as they refer to some kind of dark-roast whole-bean package. Some kind of technical mixup, I guess.

product_title: Blue Diamond Gluten Free Almonds, Whole Natural, 1.5 Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_body: I love almonds. However, I am one of those people who will eat out of the container until the container is empty. So I realized that I needed to work on portion control. These little bags of wonderful almonds is a great solution! If you like almonds and need to watch the amount you eat, try these 100 calorie almond bags. Great idea!

review_body: They are her favorite snack, she would eat a whole container if I let her. I like them too actually and they are healthier than the big bag of cheese curls, thats what these remind me of except much smaller.

review_body: I buy this product all the time. So refreshing and the best coconut water out there. Not as sweet as the others, which i prefer. I've ordered twice on amazon and both times packages have been damaged. So I just have to drive a little further to buy it. Worth it though.

product_title: Lavazza Crema e Aroma - Coffee Beans, 2.2-Pound Bag
review_body: I love that coffee and my DeLonghi Coffee machine loves it too.  The taste is great and the beans are good for a self grinding coffee machine.

product_title: Dulce Bean Organic Wheat and Gluten Free Dark Chocolate Chip Macaroons / Cookies

review_headline: The best and for the money, economical muesli product out there.
review_body: The best of all the organic muesli goes. I add the non sweetened almond milk, and chia seeds, plus 1 scoop of optimum nutrition whey isolate protein plus 1 scoop of Amazing Grass Chocolate Drink Powder, Green Superfood. I let it sit overnight and have a delicious-nutritious and filling breakfast. I've tried just about  every other muesli product and this by far is the best out there. product_title: Mild Nacheez
review_body:
Not too hot, not too boring. Our child at 9 yrs (year ago) was told she could not have gluten and lactose. She missed nacho cheese dip. She tried it after a few month ago but no she finally accepted no more cheese; then, I ran across this in another search.

review_headline: SATISFIED YOUR SWEET TOOTH AND HUNGER IN A HEALTHY WAY
review_body: I am always trying to eat a healthy breakfast and after eating the Quaker warm & crunchy granola I realized that healthy does not have to be bland and unappetizing. The taste is very satisfying and the crunch relaxing. The individual serving packets are easy to carry and provides a healthy crunch on the go. I have less frequent sweet hunger cravings now. My daughter is a big oats fan and she loved this so much that the packet was finished in no time. I went to my usual warehouse market buy unfortunately could not find the product there on that day. Quaker has come up with a really goods breakfast option. The portion size is small though but I add it as a crunchy element to my usual bowl of oatmeal. I cannot wait to try the other two flavors

review_body: I love tea and love to test out different kinds. In places like Starbucks or upscale coffee houses I often get Tazo Awake. product_title: G7 3-in-1 Instant Coffee, 50 Sachets
review_body: If you've ever enjoyed Vietnamese coffee in a restaurant, but wanted a good alternative on the go or at work, this is pretty much the answer. A friend from work let me try this product and I have been ordering it for myself ever since.

product_title: Lavazza Caffe Espresso Ground Coffee
review_headline: Is this really supposed to be Italian-type espresso?
review_body: I was really looking forward to this one, since the only kind of coffee I drink is espresso. Lavazza is supposed to be the true Italian espresso. Apparently this one has been adapted to the American palate. If you like your strong and toasty espresso skip this one. I guess I would recommend it to someone used to American coffee looking to do the transition. Otherwise, this is just coffee tea. I will stick with my Bustelo and Pilon ground coffee. I sort of feel bad giving it one star, since I guess it's a matter of taste. But it's definitely misleading to sell this as italian "caffe" espresso.

product_title: Junket Tablets Pack of 5
review_body: Item arrived on time. Nothing was going to happen until it got here anyway. Worked flawlessly. I used more than recipe called for since it didn't seem to be working. product_title: Barilla Pasta 16 Ounce
review_headline: Bavette pasta in Italy = Linguine pasta in the USA
review_body: During a recent long stay in Italy, with a kitchen to cook in, I bought and enjoyed a lot of Barilla \\"Bavette\\" pasta with a wide range of sauces. I had never heard of Bavette before in the USA. But, after some quick Googling I found that \\"Bavette\\" in Italy is what Americans usually call Linguine in the USA. There isn't much to say about Barilla except that it is the Death Star of dried pasta. Who knows how many zillion tons of wheat finds its way every year to the vast, planet sized Barilla factories in Italy and the US. The Barilla Linguine pasta sold here is made in the USA. But it has cooked up the same and produced the same great results as the Barilla Bavette pasta in Italy. RECOMMENDED.

I will stick to the bagged stuff from the store that is already puffed.

product_title: McVitie's Digestive Biscuits -400g 3 Pack, Original
review_headline: Great product and great deal overall
review_body:
I never buy these because of the purported claim of baking powder being good for digestion (in fact I would advise anyone to avoid the aluminum containing ingredient) but because when I was first introduced to digestives in a CARR's biscuit sample pack I started to search for them, as it is rare for anyone in the US to even encounter it. Though I have been seeing these in grocery stores more often, it doesn't necessarily stand out unless you know where to look for them, and normally they are only available in places such as Indian markets (often at around $3.99 for the smaller packages.) Some grocery chains do carry them for cheaper, though normally it's only the chocolate covered ones (which admittedly are good, though I would go with Cadbury if I were to choose despite not trying the McVities version.)

Supposedly it's a (hot) tea drinking biscuit or is intended for an after meal snack (or something. . . ) though I've never thought of doing such and tend to only drink iced tea. Admittedly if I were to buy these biscuits it's the result of staring at a computer monitor for too long and getting the munchies; upon receiving them in the mail (from Britain no less, with neat magazine clippings of various sorts that make me wish my ancestors never left from Britain over 200 years ago) I then satisfy my cravings and let out a self-loathing lardo belch.

product_title: Bart's Bakery The Best Gluten-Free Chocolate Chip Cookies in the World (3, 4.2oz Boxes)
review_headline: Not Safe, Not Gluten-Free, wheat contamination from shared kitchen.
review_body:
The "Gluten Free" cookies made by Bart's Bakery are not safe and "may contain wheat".

Their current cookie box packaging says under the ingredients "We segregate our ingredients and thoroughly clean our equipment however, we do not recommend consumption of our gluten-free cookies by those with celiac disease."

When asked directly about their cookies, the company response was this: "If gluten is a serious health issue, I would not not chance our cookies. We’d love to have you as a customer but we’d rather err on the side of caution."

Products like this are dangerous. They should not be allowed the gluten-free label.

product_title: Natural Dried Papayas (Dices, Chunks, Spears), Low Sugar, Unsulphured-Green Bulk

Recommend? Yes! With its price, and the amount you're getting, definitely. 50 cents a can is pretty decent.

review_headline: It's working as a replacement for artificial sweeteners for me...
review_body:
When I accepted a sample of yacon syrup for review, it was mainly to see if I could use it to start weaning myself from artificial sweeteners a bit. Subsequent to its arrival, I decided to go on a Paleo eating plan (for a number of reasons). I immediately checked it out to see if it was allowed (it is), so on with the trial...

The main target for me is to use this for trying to get used to drinking more tea (instead of so much diet soda). I found that a teaspoon of this syrup does a good job in sweetening up the tea to be closer to the type of sweet drink result I was looking for. After using it for a week or so a couple of times a day, I've experienced no side effects or anything that would cause me to stop using it. I wasn't ever much of a molasses person, but I can see how the comparison between this and molasses would be accurate.

Because I have a large amount of weight to lose (and since I'm changing a lot of diet variables), I can't point to this as being a specific factor in weight loss or health change in my case. All things being equal, I'd still be happy drinking diet soda and using Splenda. But I know subbing in yacon syrup is a better idea, and I'm happy with this offering from Life & Food.

product_title: Blair's Jalapeno Death Sauce with Tequila & Skull Key Chain - 5 oz
review_body:
This is quite an interesting hot sauce. I'm a huge fan of Blair's hot sauces, of which there are many types - at least a dozen. They are rank-ordered by Blairs in terms of heat level and this is the 2nd mildest sauce in their lineup.

The taste is great: a very strong Jalapeno taste with hints of garlic and some other spice(s). Unlike some (many?) hot sauces, which are all heat and little or no flavor, this one is all about the strong flavor. You can really, really taste those Jalapenos, and it goes fantastically well on things that benefit from an intense Jalapeno taste - eggs, chips, etc. This sauce is *extremely* mild, and by mild, I mean it has almost no heat. It has turned out to be the perfect sauce to offer family and friends who don't like hot foods. The heat is so mild in this sauce that it's really more of a flavoring sauce than a hot sauce. review_headline: These are a heck of a deal.
review_body:
I used to be addicted to Diet Coke, but I've been told by my doctor to eliminate anything that fizzes from my diet. Now, I'm addicted to ice tea.

I make my tea with a Mr. Coffee, which brews half a gallon of pretty good tea in ten minutes flat. I used to spend a minute or two per batch opening the little paper envelopes around the tea bags, and wishing my local grocery still carried tag-less tea bags.

The answer to this problem - a problem so small it doesn't really deserve to be called one - turned out to be Amazon's offer of these large-size bags. It would be really great if they offered bags exactly half this large, since Mr. Coffee is designed for half-gallon, rather than full-gallon lots.

I like the flavor of the tea, but tea purists should note that the tea itself is very murky, not transparent. That is, if you hold a glass up to the light of tea made from these bags, you won't see any glow at all through it. I have no idea what causes the murkiness, but it's only an aesthetic issue as far as I'm concerned. Maybe tea fanatics have strong feelings about the look of their tea, but for me quality is in the drinking.

I also plan on trying it in my oatmeal and think it would make a great addition to a refreshing cocktail in the summer. The uses are endless and it's nice to feel secure in that this is a wholesome, pure product from a family business and not a big food company using chemical ingredients. I do not like things that are overly sweet and am quite picky when it comes to sweets and desserts. A huge reason why I appreciate this raspberry sauce is that instead of pure sugar, you really taste the fresh raspberries the way they are meant to be enjoyed.

I also want to add that the customer service is wonderful and the owner of the business/maker of the items has been in touch with me every step of the way to make sure I received everything in a timely manner and that everything is to my enjoyment.

One last thing - I really appreciate that this is actually sold in a pack of 4. product_title: Kellogg's Special K Coffee House Breakfast Shake, Chocolate Mocha, 10 Ounce Bottles (Pack of 24)
review_headline: Able to Control Hunger, but Grainy Texture isn't Pleasing
review_body: I received two full-sized Special K™ Coffee House Breakfast Shakes to try and review compliments of BzzAgent. As a busy, multi-tasking mother, photographer, blogger I was happy to try a product that would not only help me save time, but provide energy nutrition as a portable breakfast. I sometimes forget to grab breakfast. We all know that's a bad idea and definitely doesn't help with productivity. One morning my stomach was desperately growling in hunger so I forced myself to run to my fridge and get out the Chocolate Mocha flavor of Special K Coffee House Breakfast Shakes. I looked over the ingredients and was pleased with the percentages of added nutrients, but concerned about the 18g of sugar, 210mg of sodium and some of the additives such as carrageenan. Yet, coffee extract and caffeine were in the bottle too and I do love the taste of chocolate mocha, so for the sake of an honest review, I opened the bottle and took a drink. Thick, sandy texture and kind of bland were my first thoughts. I could taste chocolate and mocha, but the flavor was definitely not what I'm used to when I buy chocolate mocha flavored drinks such as Starbuck's Mocha coffee drink in the bottle at most gas stations and grocery retailers. Of course, while Starbuck's Mocha may taste significantly better and feel smooth during its descent, it's also got a higher sugar content at 31g, but lower sodium and not nearly the amount of percentage of added nutrients. Yet, as much as I truly wanted to like the Special K Coffee House Breakfast Shake in Chocolate Mocha, I'd much rather have the Starbucks drink for a chocolate mocha coffee drink fix despite it not really being a healthy breakfast choice. So my taste review is definitely disappointing, but did the drink perform? Yes! I was actually satisfied and it lasted almost until lunch before hunger finally returned. I can recommend this flavor only for those mornings where you're in a rush to go and need something with the appropriate percentage of added nutrients. A tad high in sugar and sodium, but able to control hunger and provide energy via coffee extract which provides caffeine. If you're not picky about texture or additives such as carrageenan, than try it!added nutrients. Here is why I had to give it one star. When done, the outside of the loaf was a very unappealing white, even with an egg wash to help with browning. The inside was stark white with a dense & very spongy texture. The after taste was definitely corn-like, which I suppose isn't a surprise since it's made from maize. My son, 21, took one bite and said "No, thank you. Please go back to King Arthur's bread mix."

I have read some good reviews, mostly Australian, since Orgran is an Australian brand made by Roma Food Products. Many reviewers recommended using milk and eggs to replace the water and butter to replace the oil to improve flavor. I have not tried this yet, but may need to if my son tests positive for a reaction to tapioca (which is in the King Arthur bread mix). I'll update my review if that occurs. I must say though, if you cannot tolerate the various alternative flours, starches and yeast, this bread mix would be worth the effort of trying to improve the flavor because it was still better than the dry, crumbly, chalky GF breads I have found in the supermarket.

Keep reading for a word about flour made from maize vs corn flour (source: deglutenous.com)

Cornflour is a fine white powder separated from the protein and other components of maize flour, what is left is purely starch. It has no taste and it most commonly used as a thickener by first combining with a little cold water to make a paste.

good for:
thickening sauces, soups, stews and gravies - cornflour doesn’t make the dish cloudy as it would if using flour to thicken.

Beware: In Australia they have have wheaten cornflour, which uses the same process to remove the protein from wheat to leave starch (just to confuse things) so be sure when you buy cornflour that it is made from corn.

Maize flour
Maize flour is the entire corn kernel milled into flour. It contains protein and fat as well. The grind can vary from fine to coarse (at it’s most coarse you would know maize flour as polenta) and it is better for certain things depending on its grind.

Fine maize flour
good for:
making breads - such as mexican tortillas or cornbread (more dense than normal bread)) so be sure when you buy cornflour that it is made from corn.

product_title: Sprouting Seeds Broccoli and Friends 1 Pound Broccoli Seed, Crimson Clover Seed, Red Radish Seed, Alfalfa Seed
review_body:
I'm new to sprouting and haven't invested in a proper sprouter. Instead I used my individual Ninja Kitchen Pulse Blender cups as sprouters. The blender cups have lids that allow for easy draining (search the web for more info on how to use blender cups as sprouters) and I was able to grow these seeds easily.

The sprouts were ready to eat in 5 days (this includes 1 day of soaking) and it was super fun watching them grow a bit everyday (I'm easily amused)! I rinsed the sprouts 1-2 times per day and left them on my kitchen counter-top.

I don't get a lot of sun indoors because I'm in the PNW area so I love the fact that I can grow fresh vegetables even without sunlight! These sprouts will be my winter diet staple.

The sprouts are tasty and has a strong radish-flavor, as noted by other reviewers. Personally, I love that because it adds a lot of flavor to salads and soups. But if you don't like radish-like flavors, it's probably best to pick another seed blend.

1lb of seeds create a lot of sprouts. I used 1/4 cup of seeds and had to split the sprouts into 2 Ninja Blender cups so that the sprouts weren't too squished (they grow better if they have space).

I've uploaded photos of the fully-grown sprouts (they are yummy in noodle soups!) to the product photos section in case anyone is interested.

review_body:

But I have to admit I like this cooked tuna. It comes in a chunk or steak, not in bits and pieces like is often the case with canned tuna. So it's not as easy to mix with mayonnaise as some other brands. But it has a nice texture, almost like meat instead of fish.

And the odor and taste, though fishy and somewhat stronger than most canned tuna, somehow seemed to add to its appeal on the palate rather than detract. You get something with taste and texture rather than a bland blob of something tasting like mayonnaise sitting on your bread.

The can we had was white tuna packed in olive oil. The oil seemed to add to the taste, rather than mask it. I think I prefer the oil over water.

The can does seem pricey, at close to $4 per can. But you do indeed get what you pay for. It's good.

product_title: Bali's Best Assorted Coffee Candy Jar,
review_headline: Great Tasting Candies, but can be a bit Messy
review_body:
I have experience with these candies before. I think I ordered a 4-pack about a year ago. They are some of the best around. Being a "coffee hound", I have tried quite a few brands.
Here are my observations.

1. Come in 2 flavors, espresso and latte. The espresso is a bit stronger as you would expect.
2. Candies are definitely hard, which I like.
3. Good, strong coffee taste.
4. Plenty of candies in a plastic jar. I recycle the jar and use it for other food storage. It's a nice touch.
5. Sometimes the candies seem "half-melted" and rather messy to unwrap. Fingers can get sticky easily.
6. Be careful as these candies can easily stick to your teeth.
7. Not sugar-free, so don't eat too many. (It's easy to do, as I love the taste!)

Overall, these candies are delicious, and I would recommend to a coffee lover.

review_headline: Bad taste, bad texture, I'd hoped for more from a gluten-free product
review_body:
I was hoping for a healthy gluten-free treat that would help me lose weight. I suppose I could be more disappointed, but I'm not sure how. This is my first time trying health/energy bars. I usually just munch on carrots or apples and a little cheese or something like that.

With 300mg sodium and 9g fat, 3g of saturated fat and 12g sugar alcohol out of 60g total weight it doesn't seem all that healthy to me. Moreover it has no vitamins or nutritional support. It apparently just tries to fill you up.

More important it has all the tasty attraction of wild hickory nuts and cardboard. The Chocolate Fudge does have a hint of chocolate taste. But the flavor is just a hint.

The texture is fine for the first small taste, but I could not finish the bar as my mouth began to feel like I was eating Metamucil with a kind of grainy tongue coating texture. Even drinking cranberry juice could not fully clear the unpleasant sensation from my mouth. I've been told by a friend this is common to most health/energy bars. Yuck!

If all I had to eat were Think Thin bars I'd probably lose weight by not eating. I would not be very happy or very healthy if I did.

product_title: Gold Medal Prod. 2045 Flavacol Seasoning OLqrrq Popcorn Salt 35oz
review_headline: Great tasting popcorn starts with Flavacol
review_body:
This is the best popcorn seasoning out there. It really makes that batch of movie night popcorn pop. The best part about this seasoning other than taste is its designed to be used during the popping phase. Meaning every kernel gets flavored at that exact moment when the kernel explodes and soaks up oil and salt. Flavoring the kernel at this moment enhances the flavor, this in turns gives your popcorn a deeper flavor while using less flavoring. All without burning either the flavoring or heating apparatus. This isn't that butter flavored powder that's designed to be used after popping. This is super fine flavored salt thats designed to be added to the popping process. All it takes is a 1/4 of a teaspoon to season the entire batch. This product could also be used after the popping as additional salt topping, but it really should be used during instead. It's not a butter topping, its flavored salt, so anyone expecting to add Flavacol after popping for an additional butter flavor with be disappointed.

Flavacol is one off the necessary ingredients in "theater" popcorn, that's why its rated so high. There are very few substitutes that can match it, but none of them can beat Flavacol so you might as well buy this, chances are your local movie theaters do, because its that important and delicious. The recipe for great popcorn is; Popcorn kernels, oil, and Flavacol.

product_title: Whole Spice Cracked Black Pepper, 1 Pound
review_headline: What could be so special about pepper!
review_body:
For quite some time now I have known there is a difference between using ground black pepper and grinding fresh pepper yourself. Only recently have I heard of Cracked Black Pepper and was skeptical. How could it be so different? I mean, it's just pepper. Well, it is! It has such a "bigger" flavor. It is wonderful in all the soups and salads I have cooked. I have used it in meat rubs. Awesome! I grind it over salads. YUM! And if you want a great steak, rub it with cracked pepper before grilling.
Caution though, it is easy to over do it. It really does have a significantly stronger flavor than any other pepper I have used. It is easy though to learn what your taste buds prefer and make adjustments accordingly. I am not a gourmet cook but this has been a great and tasty discovery for me.

review_headline: If you're looking for great cashews, look elsewhere.
review_body:
I'm always on the lookout for great roasted nuts, cashews above all, and especially when I'm on the Atkins Diet, 'cause it's important to have treats to keep from falling off the wagon. I bought these cashews because they had lots of great reviews and few knocks.

Now I see why: the seller, Farm Fresh Nuts, sends a follow-up E-mail to every purchaser hoping that they're completely satisfied with their purchase, but asking for the opportunity to "address your concerns before leaving feedback."

Hmm. That has to skew the feedback responses. But I'd rather leave you an honest opinion than get my $38+ back (for 2 two-pound units).

These cashews aren't bad. They're somewhat above average, I'd say, but a long way from great. I admit that I'm picky (my username may give you a hint), but I've had better from several sources. I'll probably eat these once I roast them further to develop the flavor. Also, they're the smallest "jumbo cashews" I've ever seen.

I used to be able to buy fabulous cashews from a local store in Memphis, a remnant of the old chain of Planters' Peanut Shoppes, but when their ancient Planters' rotary roaster finally died, so did the taste of their product. Planters' canned cashews were excellent 30 years ago, but alas, times change.

In the last three years, I've tried every premium cashew brand I could find, especially those with Colossal in the name: Kroger Private Selection (blech!), Walgreens (okay), CVS (pretty good), and several generics and other brands that slip my mind. The very best I've found were Schnuck's Culinaria Colossal Cashews (highly recommended), but Schnuck's has left Memphis. So good luck finding a really great cashew, and be so kind as to let me know if you find some.

One final kibitz: these cashews arrive in a zip-type plastic bag. That's okay, the wonderful ones from the Peanut Shoppe came that way, but they didn't advertise a "Reuseable Storage Container" . . . that would be tacky.

product_title: Huy Fong Chili Garlic Sauce, 18-Ounce (Pack of 3)
review_body:
When I heard about the Huy Fong main processing plant being under some legal threats a while back, this is the product I hoarded. I go through three of these per month, and use Amazon's subscription delivery service for these and some other personal staples. Sriracha is nice sometimes, but it's excessively sweet, as Tabasco is overbearingly vinegary. Because this is pretty much just chili peppers (specifically ripe, red, cooked but unpickled, medium-hot California jalapeños) and garlic, but not piles of sugar, a flood vinegar, a bunch of other spices, or a lot of salt, you can use this more readily than just about any other source of spiciness, in Asian, American, Mexican, Italian and other cuisines. Anywhere you want spicy, and where garlic would not be inappropriate, violá! (If I don't want the garlic, I go for the same company's Sambal Oelek chili paste, or La Victoria's Salsa Brava; both are even more neutral in flavor profile than Huy Fong Chili Garlic.)

Huy Fong Chili Garlic has a fantastic, thick and course-ground "caribé" texture, and so is ideal as a base for making a homemade red salsa or other dipping sauce. My favorite uses for it are to mix into bland pre-packaged noodle bowls, to add to Thai or Szechuan or Mongolian take-out that's not spicy enough, to jazz up "hot" salsa that doesn't live up to its label, to make any pasta/marinara sauce (or even just tomato sauce) into an Arabbiata sauce, and as an incremental addition to stews and soups that need some kick. It's also a good marinade base, as long as you know who's going to be eating it and what their tolerance is. Another use for it is compensating for red chile powder that has a nice, roasty New Mexico flavor but too little heat; it doesn't have that "chile rojo off the ristra" taste itself, but it will add the needed kick to "repair" a disappointing batch of red chile sauce (or Tex-Mex chili for that matter).

The only occasional downside to Huy Fong's Chili Garlic I can think of is that it's not really a complete salsa/sauce by itself in most contexts, but a condiment and a recipe add-on. If you want something explicitly in a style like Tex-Mex, Cajun, Vietnamese, Santa Fe, or whatever, you need to add the appropriate spices (and know what they are and in what proportions). Because this goes so far, I can imagine this 16 ounce jar lasting for months. After doing tons of housework, I massaged it into my cuticles with excellent results. It even seemed to improve my nails, preventing the annoying chipping at the edges I've been experiencing.

product_title: Oreo Mega Stuf Chocolate Sandwich Cookies (13.2-Ounce Package)
review_headline: I guess I have to be the sensible one in these reviews.
review_body: I'm not even going to complain about the ten dollar price tag - if something is legitimately rare or special, the price is going to be higher. My problem is that the production quality of what I received isn't worth the price or of being called rare or special. First off, way more than a third of my bag was empty space. Just as there are fewer doublestufs in a bag I expected a smaller number of these; I did not expect my voice to echo in the empty caverns of a just opened bag. Because of all the unoccupied space in the bag (and despite Amazon's packing airbags) a lot of my cookies were cracked or shattered. And of the remaining few souls who survived, they look like something constructed by Helen Keller on a 3 day drunk. The tower in Piza doesn't lean this far. As far as taste goes, it's really no different than a doublestuf - I would not even say there is significantly more filling.

review_body:

There was flavor beyond simple coffee to these and the K-cups had some contents left in them after use. Not what I experienced from this purchase. I have since concluded that the ones I purchased here were fakes. Stay away and purchase from a physical store or try another buyer. You'll be disappointed from the ones you order here unless I only received a bad package.

product_title: Gerber Good Start Gentle Powder
review_body:
I was truly, deeply horrified to have to supplement with formula, but after my baby continued to lose weight at 3 weeks, I had to. I researched the hell out of formula as my husband and I both have food intolerances - pretty scary given my husband's only symptom of gluten intolerance was seizures. I was really torn between this formula and Nature's One organic. Nature's One definitely has superior ingredients all the way except that Nature's One uses a lot of casein, which many babies (and I expect mine) react poorly to. This formula uses whey exclusively, and partially hydrolyzed at that.

I HATE that the third ingredient in Good Start Gentle is corn maltodextrin - YUCK! And this stuff truly tastes and smells foul (metallic and bitter). I also hate the inclusion of DHA and ARA as they are highly processed and unlikely to work as effectively as those components in breastmilk. I highly doubt the probiotics in here are any good since the product isn't refrigerated.

I use it anyway because I think introducing casein into baby's open gut could be very, very bad. I also give her Udo's infant probiotics and about half breastmilk, all I can produce. I really wish Nature's One used whey. :(

Ingredients

1.5 cups Blanched Almond Flour
3 eggs
1 cup of water or milk(or slightly less to desired thickness)
Optional: spices like cinnamon and nutmeg, vanilla, blueberries or other flavors

Instructions

Mix all ingredients in a medium sized bowl using a hand blender or immersion blender until batter is a pourable consistency.
Make one test pancake to check for desired thickness and texture.
Cook all pancakes on a griddle or in a large pan for approximately 2-3 minutes per side until bubble form and both sides are golden brown.
Enjoy!

You can use sweet potatoes (traditional and I love them) or any potato, bulk it up with chickpeas, use chicken or beef or shrimp (shrimp doesn't need to cook as long as beef), throw in carrots or kale or green beans or...you name it. product_title: Jaipur Avenue Chai Tea Mix Masala
review_body:
This is exactly what I was looking for. I'm a full-time student of Indian background and I really love having a hot-caffeinated beverage in the morning, and coffee is just a tad too caffeinated for me. My mom used to make us hot chai in the morning, so I set out to find an instant version (just pour hot water). (THIS is IT) I read about Jaipur Avenue from a reviewer comparing another product with this, and I just scrolled down and found a reviewer for Jaipur Ave mentioning she came from a Punjabi household and that this tasted authentic. Woohoo! I knew this had to be legit. SO glad I was not disappointed. If you're looking for the best approximation of the real thing, go for this. Not that American-ized, over-sweet crap you get at Starbucks and other hipster places.
Tried the masala and the lemongrass ones -- both are fantastic. I've never heard of lemongrass chai before, but actually it's quite a pleasant twist on the concept.

product_title: Nubian Heritage Honey & Black Seed Soap 5 oz ( Pack of 2)
review_body: I have tried 3 Nubian Heritage soaps. My first experience with N.H. soap was the shea butter soap with the frankincense & myrrh. That soap is fantastic in scent, cleansing and moisturizing. My next N.H. soap was the mango butter soap. That soap is not bad. I won't purchase it again. That soap to me on a scale of 1 to 5 was a 3.  This N.H. honey and black seed soap rates up there with the shea butter frankincense & myrrh soap. The scent is extremely delightful; it lathers well, gently cleanses and softens my skin. I use  N.H soap to cleanse my body from the neck down- not my face.  I use pure black soap with shea butter for my face.  I look forward to trying the coconut & papaya soap next and I have long ago concluded that N.H. soap is the only body soap for me. Their honey and black seed soap is one of the \\"must have\\"  soaps of theirs' that I feel a strong desire to keep quite a few bars of on hand for my beauty needs. When I use it- I feel like I'm pampering my body. *I am L.C. from N.C.*

I have been looking for ways to reduce weight and get my metabolism back on track. I'm not that young guy I used to be. So, I ordered Yacon Syrup because it raises metabolism, assists in weight loss and increases fiber.

The instructions tell you to take it several times a day but you can also use it as a sweetener. So, I put it in my oatmeal because oatmeal is a natural fat burner. When it came out of the bottle, it looked like chocolate syrup. I was tempted. So, I put some on my finger and licked it. It is not chocolate, but it is delicious. I added a little more to my bowl of oatmeal.

Throughout the day, I can feel the extra energy. I'm not taking the naps like I used to, but I still take naps. It's just that now when I lie down during the day, I know that I've accomplished a lot and got in a full day. I love this stuff! It's now a part of my daily routine.

I put it in coffee for a different flavor. I eat peanut butter too as a part of my weight loss efforts and Yacon Syrup topped on peanut butter is a taste that can get addictive. But, I just discovered it as a great topping to apple slices and that was out of this world!

product_title: Worthington Choplets Vegetable & Grain Protein Patties, 20 oz. Can
review_body:
It's a treat when our family has Choplet sandwiches.
My folks used to stock up on vegetarian meats at camp-meeting,
and this Worthington brand Choplet has remained a family favorite since the 1960's.
I'm not sure if the chops contain the exact ingredients as in the 60's,
but I do know they still taste the same to me.

The patties are made from vegetable & grain protein. The texture is somewhat spongy,
with a slightly nutty flavor. Great for sandwiches or the 'meat' course of a meal.
A can contains 8 choplets, each piece is approx 3\\" dia x 1/2\\" thick, with 1/2 cups broth.
Can is said to be four servings which is 2 slices per.

If your one that enjoys deluxe sandwiches ~ Choplets are delicious when dipped in egg,
dipped in flour and fried golden brown.
Served on your favorite bread with Miracle Whip/Mayo - lettuce - tomato - pickles - onions.

INGREDIENTS ~ Choplets - Textured vegetable protein (wheat gluten, soy protein concentrate,
water for hydration), caramel color.
Broth - Water, hydrolyzed soy, corn & wheat protein, autolyzed yeast extract, salt,
dextrose, corn oil, caramel color, disodium inosinate, disodium guanylate, soybean oil.

When I bought a case (12 cans) of 20 oz cans at Apple Valley Store in Berrien Springs, Mich,
May 2013 - everyday retail price was $60.61 total, and $5.18 ec. for single can purchase.
I know the store ships, and even with S&H may be better value then a few of these prices.
