product_title: Anchor Butter New Zealand, Unsalted. Pack of 4
review_headline: Not impressed with the taste and manufacture date which is 24/01/2013
review_body:
First of all I would like to rate the delivery which was fast. The butter was well packed and insulated. When my butter arrived, it was cold and firm.
However the butter itself was manufactured on 24/01/2013. I ordered it in December 2013. So the butter that arrived is almost one year old. I am not sure if I am ok with that. I can buy organic Valley limited addition butter from grass fed cows at my local store that is made in October and November 2013.
Now I come back to the taste of the butter. I am sorry I was not impressed with the taste of the butter. After I read about the New Zeland Anchor butter, I was expecting something unbelievably delicious. Not the case. The taste of this butter was missing richness and flavor. The taste is more water like. The color of real butter should be more deep yellow or orange. The Anchor butter is light yellow. I buy Amish butter at my local farmers market that is much tastier and yellow.
I gave this product 3 stars because it came from grass fed cows and shipping was excellent. Nevertheless I am not sure if I order this again because I am not impress with the taste and manufacture date.

product_title: Villa Manodori Balsamic Vinegar
review_headline: A great introduction to quality balsamic vinegars
review_body:
Until recently I had no idea that balsamic vinegars can be more than the stuff you get at the supermarket. I saw a segment on balsamic vinegar on America's Test Kitchen and that got me interested. I started by getting a bottle of aged Monari Federzoni from the supermarket which was one of their runner-ups (winning product was not available). The Monari Federzoni was perhaps slightly better than the average supermarket balsamic, but still nothing to write home about.

I didn't want to spend upwards of $100 to get a very old balsamic. I was looking for the cheapest product that would still give me an idea of what a quality balsamic tastes like. After trying out the Villa Manodori today, I think I hit the mark. Compared to the supermarket stuff, this was much thicker and sweeter. I really enjoyed it, and I think I finally got what all the fuss is about. I'm looking forward to see what the really old ones are like.

review_headline: A dense, moist pastry that melts in your mouth!
review_body:
Several years ago my parents travelled to Racine, Wisconsin to attend my dad's annual army reunion. While they were there they got to sample a local taste sensation known as a \\"kringle\\". It was all they could talk about when they returned home. Kringles are butter-layered Danish pastries that were first introduced to Racine in the late 1800s by immigrant Danish bakers and actually date back to the 13th century. And let me tell you they just melt in your mouth. Kringles are big business in Wisconsin's fifth largest city and several bakeries ship these tasty treats to loyal fans all across America and beyond. O & H Danish Bakery has been making Kringles since way back in 1949. In this particular offer buyers get to sample a pair of O & H's most popular flavors....pecan and raspberry.

Each Kringle serves 8 to 12 people and my experience has been that they freeze quite well. Just a couple of weeks ago I sent a co-worker a Kringle to express my sincere thanks for a profound act of kindness. She loved it! Meanwhile, I showed up to Christmas dinner last year with a Raspberry Kringle under tow. Everyone enjoyed it and remarked that it was fun to sample a regional treat from another part of the country. If you are looking for a different sort of birthday, anniversary or Christmas gift then I urge you to consider one of these O & H Danish Kringles. By the way, they are also available in two packs right here on Amazon. You just might start a brand new tradition in your family. Highly recommended!ar with a Raspberry Kringle under tow. Everyone enjoyed it and remarked that it was fun to sample a regional treat from different part of the country. product_title: Nestle Stouffers Entree Macaroni and Beef, 12.75 Ounce -- 12 per case.
review_headline: Too Salty For Me, Not As Good As It Could Be.
review_body:
Stouffer's Signature Classics Macaroni & Beef, 12 7/8 oz. (365g).
This frozen meal contains 970mg of salt, about the same as two hotdogs, which are pretty salty to begin with. This meal will leave you with a salty aftertaste and is not as good as it could be. I remember the lunchroom meals of macaroni and beef (American Chop Suey) from grade school and high school, something I looked forward to. This meal is edible, but nothing to look forward to. The extra salt content will cause you to retain fluids, at least until the extra salt leaves your system. If you like extra salt, you can always add your own, but you can't remove it once it is there. For anyone with high blood pressure and on a low salt diet, this is one meal to stay away from. Processed foods in general contain far too much sugar and salt, which is not good for our individual health. The label Nutrition Facts and INGREDIENTS information is as follows:

Nutrition Facts: Serving Size 1 Package (365g), Servings Per Container 1. Calories 360 (Calories From Fat 110). Total Fat 12g (Saturated Fat 5g, Trans Fat 1g), Cholesterol 31mg, Sodium 970mg, Total Carbohydrate 45g (Dietary Fiber 4g, Sugars 15g), Protein 17g.

INGREDIENTS: TOMATOES (DICED TOMATOES, TOMATO JUICE, CITRIC ACID, CALCIUM CHLORIDE), BLANCHED MACARONI (WATER, SEMOLINA, WHEAT GLUTEN), BEEF, WATER, TOMATO PUREE (WATER, TOMATO PASTE), CHILI SAUCE (TOMATOES, HIGH FRUCTOSE CORN SYRUP, SUGAR, CORN SYRUP, VINEGAR, RED PEPPERS, SALT, DRIED ONION, DRIED GARLIC, SPICE, NATURAL FLAVOR), 2% OR LESS OF SUGAR, DEHYDRATED ONIONS, MODIFIED CORNSTARCH, SALT, SEASONING ((SOY SAUCE, (WATER, SOYBEAN, WHEAT, SALT), AUTOLYZED YEAST EXTRACT, DEXTROSE, SOYBEAN OIL)), CULTURED WHEY, YEAST EXTRACT, SPICE. CONTAINS: MILK, SOY, WHEAT INGREDIENTS. DISTRIBUTED BY: NESTLE USA, INC., SOLON, OH 44139 USA. ("Best Before" date is stamped in white lettering below the list of INGREDIENTS). review_headline: Another Stupid, Expensive and Cruel Fad for the Rich
review_body: I can't believe that people would want to drink a cup of coffee that went through the intestines of a Civet and came out in the poop of the poor creature. I have heard the expression Eat S***! but this is a case of Drink S***. How about if a human swallowed coffee beans and crapped them out? Would anyone want to drink that? So what is the difference? A Civet is a poor little feline type creature that does no harm to the Earth. Who in Hell thought up the scam to feed coffee beans to this animal, gather them and make a really crappy cup of coffee - literally? Do you in Amazonland really trust a cup of coffee to be free of the Civet crap or did a little bit remain when the beans were processed? Please just drink your coffee straight, without the additional passage through the digestive tract of a Civet or any other animal. Coffee is good for you but Kopi Luwak has to be the worst cup of coffee that anyone can drink because of the animal cruelty involved and because it's a ridiculously pricey scam and possibly dangerous to your health.

review_body:
I received an Amazon gift card for the holidays and wanted to use it for something for my wife and I to use in the kitchen. I read all of the reviews for the different salt blocks available. Most indicated that when the salt block arrived it was cracked or broken and/or 'banged up'. I went ahead and ordered one any way! Oh how naive I was. As other reviewers have experienced, the salt block is only packaged with packing peanuts in an over-sized cardboard box. The salt block is heavy and will slide around in this type of packaging. Product was delivered diagonally cracked in half with corners rounded and banged up from shipping.

My recommendation is this: If you plan to order any salt block and have it shipped to you, expect it to arrive broken. I'm not upset about it, just adjust your expectations. If you would really like a good salt block, perform a Google search and with luck there may be a specialty store in your area. Lucky for my wife and I there is such a store here in Portland. I should have gone with my gut and purchased a salt block that I was able to see and ensure was not cracked. Like most things, you get what you pay for. Lesson learned! Buyer beware.

I also have to say that I also really like the little jar, and the spoon that comes with it! I could see myself easily reusing this down the line once I run out of my supply of salt.

product_title: Traverse Bay Fruit Co. Dried Cherries, 4-Pound Bag
review_headline: Direct From Our "Cherry Capital" - Delicious, Healthy Fruit at Wholesale Price
review_body:
These dried cherries are delicious, healthy food sold on Amazon at wholesale prices. Traverse Bay, Michigan is the center of the state's largest cherry growing region. You receive the 4-pound box directly from where the fruit was both grown and processed. Their quality is first rate. The vast majority of all tart and sweet cherries produced there are processed: frozen, canned, brined, dried, or chemically preserved as bottled maraschino cherries. Michigan is by far the biggest grower of tart cherries accounting for over 70% of the nation's output.

Traverse City, MI calls itself the Cherry Capital of the World. It certainly is the national tart cherry capital. Turkey actually substantially outproduces the US in growing cherries. That is appropriate considering that Turkey is where ancient Europe found the varieties that it grows. I assume that these Traverse Bay cherries, which have been dried and moderately sweetened, are one of the tart varieties. We do not find them overly sweet but rather intensely flavored by the fruit itself. By comparison, my wife and I find most varieties of raisins to be a bit too sweet.

Many writers claim cherries have a number of important attributes that can reduce pain, especially joint pain, assist digestion and help reduce both cancer and heart disease. That is another good reason to have some daily. Their taste and convenience make them easy to use whether you eat them directly or in salads or in baking. Thankfully, Amazon makes them affordable. When you subscribe you can save up to an additional 15% more, which drops their price to half of what health food stores charge per pound. The only minor complaint I have is that although rare, it is still possible to find a partial pit or two in each box. That falls under the category of being understandable or par for the course. In all: Highly recommended.

review_headline: If you knew how kopi luwak was cultivated, you wouldn't buy it.
review_body:
Kopi luwak is made from the beans of coffee berries that have been eaten and excreted--yes, you read that right!--by the Asian palm civet. To make this coffee, the civets are typically snatched from their homes and life in the wild to be imprisoned alone in tiny, barren cages. They're deprived of everything that is natural and important to them, including freedom, exercise, space--even real food. They bite at the cage bars, turn in circles, and go insane from being imprisoned with no escape. Deprived of adequate nutrition, they begin to lose their fur. All of this cruelty is just for a novelty coffee sold by companies such as Amazon.com.

If you want feces in your coffee and if you want to support cruelty to animals, then by all means buy it. I will not support animal cruelty. Therefore, I will not buy kopi luwak.

product_title: Lipton Herbal Tea Pyramids, Peppermint 18 count (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Great after dinner tea. Keep on hand to sooth head colds
review_body:
Peppermint teas like this are wonderful to enjoy after a big meal. Peppermint teas are very soothing to the stomach and leave a refreshing flavor in your mouth. They're also nice to enjoy a cup of when you're not feeling well with a cold or flu. The aroma of the leaves when the tea is hot helps open and sooth stuffed up sinuses and help relieve painful sore throats. And enjoying a cup of peppermint tea during the holidays when it's cold outside is relaxing and comforting.

Lipton has been making an interesting selection of hot teas for a while now. At first I never gave them much thought, however after buying a box of [[ASIN:B00CHHKCL6 Lipton Black Tea, Vanilla Caramel]] (formerly called Caramel Truffle), and falling in love with the blend, I decided to start giving some of the other teas a chance. For a while I bought the [[ASIN:B003VCZQIA Lipton Black Pearl Tea]] as well, and have since then tried many other blends and found pretty much all of them to be good. I appreciate that Lipton made this peppermint to to be plain, without any added extra flavors like chocolate, as several other companies do. I like my peppermint tea to be plain, and with a great flavors. This Lipton peppermint is spot on.

product_title: Cameron's Gold
review_body:

The \\"sell by\\" date was still 9 months away so I thought it would be OK. I ground some beans and made a fresh pot of coffee the usual way I always do it... Very bitter aftertaste, not acceptable. The next day I tried a less stronger brew, still bitter. Tried again with a mixture of this and my other favorite beans, still a bitter aftertaste. No amount of sugar or creamer will mask out the bitterness. Going to give it away or toss it, or maybe throw the beans out in the backyard and hope for a beanstalk to the goose that lays golden eggs.

Update...
Another reviewer mentioned the bitter aftertaste diminished after leaving the bag open. I tried again after a week and found most of the bitterness is gone. However, this is still definitely not a premium tasting coffee, flat, not much chocolate, and no caramel taste at all. My old Costco \\"Jose's Vanilla Nut\\" whole bean coffee is way better than this.

product_title: Gevalia Single-Cup Coffee for Keurig K-Cup Brewers
review_body:
This review is based on using these with the cheapest Keurig brand machine, the $99 Keurig Mini Plus. I don't know why other people are having issues with the cup design as I have none. Putting the cup in and repeatedly lifting the lever/canister that holds the cup WILL result in coffee grounds in the cup, but I attribute that purely to user error. The simple way to solve this is to make sure the Keurig has enough water and is ready THEN put in the coffee brew cup LAST. If I have no issues doing it this way in Keurig's cheapest machine, why is everyone having issues in the much more expensive ones??

Spending almost a year trying to find a decent tasting Keurig coffee proved to be the hardest thing about having a Keurig. Part of the problem is finding a lighter coffee that still retains excellent, smooth flavor. At first I tried the Gevalia Columbia roast being one of the few single-origin Keurig coffees out there and was pretty impressed. However, I decided to give the Signature Blend a try despite being a blend as I still preferred coffee on the lighter end. The Signature Blend coffee simply is phenomenal and if you have any inclination towards lighter, smooth coffees I would say get that. If you like darker roast coffees, the Columbia roast should satisfy that as it is more rich and bold.

On a side note, these seem to be MUCH cheaper in the grocery stores at roughly $7-8 per 12 count.

This tower of chocolate provides three strong boxes of different flavors. Personally, my favorite are the dark intense chocolates (72% and 86%). They are very high quality, and one square is rich and will satisfy you. Also, this is the healthiest form of chocolate. They also offer dark chocolate with fillings, such as Caramel, Raspberry, or Mint. I found the Caramel to be excellent. Keep in mind the dark chocolate used with the fillings is 60%, so it's not that strong (whether you consider that to be a positive or negative).

While I'm not a fan of milk chocolate, the tower also contains some variants of that.

The boxes are of a high quality, and can be used for other items once the chocolate is finished.

The only reason I wouldn't give this 5 stars is because the squares can be bought in standard Ghirardelli bags. There are no flavors that are exclusive to this tower. So it doesn't feel as special as it looks. But overall, it's a nice gift for a chocolate lover.

product_title: Coffee Bean Direct Decaf Dark Whole Bean Coffee, 16 Ounce (Pack of 3)
review_body:
Caveat: Everyone has very specific personal tastes with regards to coffee. \\"One size\\" does not fit all. Period. My preferences are a \\"strong\\" or bold cup of coffee that brews well in a Keurig with self-made K-cups. I \\"should\\" drink decaf; however, I also shop for price and availability of bolder roasts. Due to budget concerns, I MUST be somewhat flexible in what constitutes a good cup o'Joe. I usually brew two k-cups at 8 oz in a large 20 oz mug. Add creamer, sweetner, and a splash of cold Alaskan water (not much warmer than a melted icecube).

I drink an avg of 5 such mugs per 24 hours. My idea of \\"day\\" hardly matches anyone else's as right now, we're light 24/7. Come winter, it will be 18 hours of dark.

Everything that comes to Alaska has a fairly significant add-on cost due shipping (this includes grocery store purchases, too). Few companies offer \\"free\\" shipping to either Alaska or Hawaii, no matter how much we purchase in a single order.

So, I've been experimenting with various offerings at Amazon as I really need the Amazon's flexible shipping pricing. Not everything is cheaper on Amazon, but by the time shipping is factored in, it's at least a break-even price point, and with Warehouse Deals can be a significant savings.

I purchased a Keurig this past Xmas and renewed my love affair with coffee. BUT, I rapidly learned that I simply cannot afford either the cost of pre-made K-cups nor am I willing to add to the landfill at the volume of coffee I make.

I've been purchasing from Coffee Bean Direct for years now, but mostly their teas, simply because I could buy acceptable coffee locally, but not budget-priced loose leaf teas. Their service and quality has always been excellent.

I really like this coffee, especially for being a Decaf. It makes a really smooth bold cup of coffee. However, since it's priced double to that of Eight O'Clock products, I'll probably only use this as a supplement to make a50/50 blend -- lower my caffeine. For those who don't know, Sumatra is the lowest acid coffee available. Sumatra Dark Roast would be about a 7 out of 10 on a \\"roast scale\\" with 2 or 3 being standard restaurant brews, and a 10 being Espresso-level.Pre-made K-cups are definitely a bolder cup than a self-made one; however, as in all things that require some balance, I recommend that anyone who isn't a purist for the boldest to give this a try -- especially those who fight stomach acid issues. There is also a non-decaf version, too.

product_title: Dr. McDougall's Right Foods Vegan Black Bean & Lime Soup, 3.4-Ounce Cups (Pack of 6)
review_body:
With 137 positive reviews, I trusted the quality. Wrong.
Flavor: none, nada, zero, until I added lime juice from my stock.
Texture: like mostly mashed beans in water--requires a LOT of stirring to unclump beans.
Overall: I normally have vegan, no salt black beans in a can and this is the same--with 1/4 cup water added.
Time (according to directions): Prep-1 minute; microwave-2 minutes; stirring (unclumping) the beans--2 minutes; letting them sit--8 minutes. Now, does it take 13 minutes to heat a cup of black beans in your micro? No; it takes about three minutes.
The packs ARE very light, so I would say the only advantage is to take them backpacking--at work or in nature. Of course, taking a can of beans to work is not the way to impress colleagues, but it would produce the same results.
If your car camping, saving weight is no big deal. If you buy beans in a can, you can also use the can as an offensive or defensive weapon, ash tray, door stop, etc. Why buy flavorless dehydrated beans and then add water, unless the weight of carrying them is an issue.
I will be giving these away as gifts!!

product_title: Matcha DNA Certified Organic Matcha Green Tea
review_body:
I have had some experiences with \\"High End\\" and \\"Lower End\\" matcha tea's (or so I was told they were), all of which I found to be bitter, sometimes astringent, and often found my stomach would be upset shortly after.

I decided to give Matcha another try after seeing this was from Chinese origin and nothing added (sugars and/or sweeteners, ect) The price is about right for clean and certified matcha, So I got some, it was not bitter, astringent, rough or unpleasant. But smooth, slightly sweet and easy to make. Nice deep color, darker then normal Japanese matcha though. It is also pretty durable, some matcha tea needs a lot of special attention in preparation, this I just threw in a glass and added warm water and it turned out pretty good!

Simple, quick, tasty, and healthy! I'd recommend it if you want an alternative to the matcha that is currently out there for sale.

Pros:
Packed with minerals and antioxidants
Great boost with little crash after
Smooth round flavor
Easy to make
Nice packaging
If your frighten of the possibility of radiation in Japanese matcha, This is from China.
This 3 oz version comes in prepackaged portions! Makes it so much easier to drink everywhere

Cons:
When not on sale might be a little pricey (but with what is out there, I would still buy it)
Doesn't come with more recipes or alternative ways to brew it (when shipped, I think online does)

Give it a try! You might be surprised too. Happy Drinking.

product_title: Nantucket Off-Shore Nantucket Rub, 1.5-Ounce Tins (Pack of 6)
review_headline: One of the best herb and spice blends for fish
review_body:
First I want to address some complaints about the quantity of these tins: they are small, but a little of this rub goes a long way. You do have to rub it into the fish - not merely sprinkle it - to get the full flavor from the smallest amount of mix. A tablespoon will more than adequately cover a one pound piece of salmon and there are three tablespoons per tin.

The herbs and spices are fresh and highly aromatic. The tin helps keep them that way, although I would recommend using up a tin within a few weeks of opening it. What I love is there is no salt. Period. Most blends include it and for those of us who have sodium restrictions this is a major plus. If you must have salt you can add it yourself. The ingredients are simple: garlic, onion, dill, tarragon, pink peppercorns, lemon peel, paprika, black pepper and fennel. It's the quality of the ingredients that I mentioned above and the skillful blend that make this a value. You could buy the herbs and spices yourself, but getting the proportions right is the hard part.

I've used this on various types of fish from salmon to flounder and it works on them all. It's my secret ingredient for most of the fish-based dishes that I serve.

Just be aware that each tin only contains three tablespoons of the mix and you will not be disappointed. Especially since you can easily flavor three pounds of fish per tin. It's the flavor that counts and this - to me - is worth every penny for how it transforms my fish into something special.

review_headline: A wonderful chili for best taco salsa!
review_body:
Really, cacabel's are my husband's & my FAV. chili to use for salsa (esp. for use on tacos). Not too hot, not too mild. Darlin' hubby wrkd in prof. kitchens for 23+ yrs. & made a real study of Mex. cooking & spent time with the \\"grandmothers\\" & got some of their secrets. Here's the salsa recipe (you won't be sorry!):

Makes about 1 cup

* * * *
4 Cascabel chilies, with only stem pulled off (don't need to clean out)
6 oz. tomato juice (½ of 12 oz. can)
1 big clove garlic, smashed & peeled (smash to remove skin easily & bring out flavor)
- - -
¼ med. to lrg. onion, minced
pinch salt
pinch Mexican oregano

Using blender, whir first 3 ingred.(tom. juice, chilies & garlic). Stir in everything else by hand. Serve immed. Will keep 3-4 days in fridge.

NOTE: This can be made ahead of time, but do NOT put onion in while chilling in fridge; stir in right before serving. (due to acid, onion will start disintegrating)

product_title: Weaver's Coffee and Tea, French Roast Organic Ground Coffee, 12-Ounce Bags (Pack of 2)
review_headline: Excellent flavor - but too fine of a grind
review_body:
Caveat: Everyone has very specific personal tastes with regards to coffee. \\"One size\\" does not fit all. Period. My preferences are a \\"strong\\" or bold cup of coffee that brews well in a Keurig with self-made K-cups. I \\"should\\" drink decaf; however, I also shop for price and availability of bolder roasts. Due to budget concerns, I MUST be somewhat flexible in what constitutes a good cup o'Joe. I usually brew two k-cups at 8 oz in a large 20 oz mug. Add creamer, sweetner, and a splash of cold Alaskan water (not much warmer than a melted icecube).

I drink an avg of 5 such mugs per 24 hours. My idea of \\"day\\" hardly matches anyone else's as right now, we're light 24/7. Come winter, it will be 18 hours of dark.

Everything that comes to Alaska has a fairly significant add-on cost due shipping (this includes grocery store purchases, too). Few companies offer \\"free\\" shipping to either Alaska or Hawaii, no matter how much we purchase in a single order.

So, I've been experimenting with various offerings at Amazon as I really need the Amazon's flexible shipping pricing. Not everything is cheaper on Amazon, but by the time shipping is factored in, it's at least a break-even price point, and with Warehouse Deals can be a significant savings.

I purchased a Keurig this past Xmas and renewed my love affair with coffee. BUT, I rapidly learned that I simply cannot afford either the cost of pre-made K-cups nor am I willing to add to the landfill at the volume of coffee I make.

****

I really liked the taste of this coffee, but the grind was too fine and really clogs up my Keurig filter. I may try it as a whole bean when it shows up on Warehouse Deals sometime. I'd recommend it for those who like french roast in a drip coffeemaker.

The good news is that the juniper is quite easy to care for, and this tree, it's landscaping, and its potting are all visually appealing. I find this to be an excellent value for it's cost.

product_title: Miracle Noodle Gluten-free Shirataki Pasta
review_body: I got my noodles today and was so excited.  I purchased the variety 6 pack so I could see which noodles I enjoyed the best.  Today I tried the fettuccine noodles.  I opened the pouch and put them into a colander and rinsed them well.  Then in a frying pan, I put in a T of olive oil, and a spoonful of chopped garlic.  Got that good and happy then threw in the noodles.  I then added some pasta Italian seasoning.  I added a splash of fat free half and half, and let that simmer together nicely.  If I had been preplanning I would have cooked up some vegetables, like onions, peppers, pea pods, anything I could find that is tasty and put that in with the noodles and I would have had an enormous platter of food for practically no calories.  But, I was in a hurry......  The results were:  I enjoyed it a lot.  For those of you who want the taste of REAL pasta, this is not for you.  What it tastes like is Asian noodles.  I have had a dish similar in Chinatown in NYC, with grilled shrimp on top.  Now there is something I shall try next time.  I will continue to keep these noodles in stock.  Great food, simple to prepare and next to nothing calories.

product_title: Melitta Cone Coffee Filters
review_body:
I use a Cuisinart 12-cup drip coffee maker with high quality coffee (fair traded, organic, whatever all that stuff means) I purchase five pounds of beans at a time from a local roaster in San Diego which I grind as needed. These filters are key part is making great coffee. I've tried supermarket brands and others, and I always feel these give the best result. The filters add nothing and subtract unpleasant flavors. As a note: if you do a quick Google search you'll find there is a compound (cafestol) in coffee which which some research has shown raises bad cholesterol (LDL) levels. Coffee filters remove that compound. This is certainly a reason to drink coffee which has been filtered.

Buying six 100-count packs at a time from Amazon is by far the most cost effective way to get Melitta filters which can otherwise be a bit pricey, plus it assures they are always on hand.

Because I like the filters I've given a pack to various friends at times to try. I wish I got a cut from the extra filters Melitta sells due to those gifts.

As another reviewer commented, there must be an artificial chemical ingredient, or it's pesticide residues or something of that nature coming through. I recommend AVOIDING this product.

review_headline: Excellent flavor that tastes like real smoked BBQ

This salt is surprisingly good! I'm a huge fan of smoked flavors, but oftentimes items that claim to be \\"smoked\\" have either a nasty aftertaste, or just taste artificial. This salt, in contrast, truly tastes like a good wood-smoked product.

I first used it as a rub on oven-roasted chicken along with some rosemary. While the smoked flavoring was not as intense as it would have been had I used my smoker, it was clearly there. It made for an excellent tasting chicken - a very nice change from the usual oven-roasted flavor.

I also used it to season some corn on the cob (just a small pinch). Again, great results. The smoke tang is there but not overpowering. Very balanced taste.

Even though it's been very humid out, there was no clumping of the salt. That's important for me since I keep my seasoning salts in a small open bowl for easy access.

If you're looking to add a bit of smokey BBQ flavor to dishes without the need to break out the smoker, this is well worth trying. Highly recommend.

product_title: Knorr Mi Arroz Rice Seasoning Mix, White, 0.19 Pound (Pack of 24)
review_headline: MSG + 3,960 mg (!) salt = headache and thirst; something worse than ramen
review_body:
I should have read the nutrition facts first. This is the worst thing for your health. And to top it all, it doesn't taste good either.

I have been cooking rice for about 2 decades now. I can make it in my sleep. I wanted to try something new and tried this mix. It was a mistake from the start. The instructions on the packet are all backwards. Why would you fry uncooked rice and then add water?

I cooked the rice as the instructions dictated without adding any other ingredients as I normally would. When I initially tasted it I noticed the very strong salt taste and that extreme lack of flavor. See, for all of the numerous ingredients that they list, it doesn't taste like anything but salt. The salt flavor is overpowering. I ate about half a cup. Then I dumped the rest of the pot. Such a waste of food. I had to drink 2 glasses of water trying to get the saltiness out of my mouth.

I then looked at the ingredients..... :0
The amount of salt in just 1 packet is over 200% of your daily value. 200%! The recommended daily value is 2,400 mg of sodium. Just one packet has 3,960 mg of salt. The crafty people that make this advertise the serving size as 1/6 of the packet. But, you need a whole packet to cook the rice. This is actually worse than ramen noodles. I never thought I would see something worse than ramen noodles.

I am very disappointed in Knorr, a brand I have used for many years, for making such a bad, unhealthy, and tasteless product.

Just add regular salt to your rice. This seasoning is completely unnecessary.

product_title: Amazing Grass Green Superfood
review_body:
I bought this stuff because I am working on losing weight on a low calorie and low fat high exercise diet. I thought I might need some sort of added nutrition.

After receiving the stuff - original flavor, I mixed up a scoop in about 16 ounces of water and looked at it. Nasty looking stuff - dark green like something you might see on a stick you poked into pond scum.

Steeling myself for the worst based on the many reviews on how bad it tastes, I drank - chugged - the entire glass. There was no bad taste that I could discern and only a bit of grittiness.

Later that day after my first dose, I felt a sort of sweetness in my stomach. I'm not sure what that was about but it was there and was not unpleasant.

Thinking that maybe 16 ounces of water was too much to chug, I started mixing the stuff in about 6 ounces of water and then chugging that with a water chaser. It is a bit thicker but still no nasty taste.

I haven't been using it long enough to tell if it is doing me any good (hence the three star rating) but maybe the diet/exercise regimen I am currently on is skewing the benefits. Too many variables to comment on the benefits so far.

Bottom line: This stuff is not a mint julep that you can sit by the pool and sip while enjoying your morning paper.

If you see any benefit from using it, mix it up in a bit of water and drink it down with a water chaser. Then make yourself that mint julep and go out by the pool and check out your paper.

product_title: Grassfed Organic Ghee - Pure Indian Foods Brand
review_headline: Superior Product from a Socially Conscious Manufacturer
review_body:
Well, I've finally joined the rest of the world in the 21st century by eliminating all the non-stick coated pans from my kitchen. I've gone back to my old favorites, the All Clad Stainless Steel pans that don't add toxins to my food (my favorite go-to pan is this one [[ASIN:B004T6J64M All Clad Stainless Steel 4-Quart Saute Pan with Lid]]). The unfortunate reality is, though, that in my non-expert hands, most foods I cook do stick to my pans. The solution: Ghee.

Because Ghee has a higher flash point than butter, it doesn't break down at all during cooking. You know what I'm talking about. You use butter to sauté but find that you have to keep adding more and more as you go because it mysteriously disappears or browns onto the pan. That doesn't happen with Ghee.

I'm not one to participate in the many common dietary trends. As someone with a bit of formal training on both nutrition and the workings of the human body, I believe that balance and moderation are the keys to excellent nutrition. My mantra is: everything in moderation. We do need some cholesterol in our diets, just not as much as we'd like. We also need carbohydrates. The great majority of us, who aren't sensitive to lactose or glutens actually should be eating these things.

That said, I am not a fan of GMOs these days. My viewpoint is not dietary in nature. I certainly don't want to get into my environmental concerns or discuss the virtues of anti-trust regulations. I'm just going to say that I appreciate the fact that this product is made from organic milk alone. The milk used in this product is harvested in the spring and fall only, when the cattle are permitted to graze exclusively on non-GMO green grass (the growth phase of the grass affects the nutrition it provides).

The fact that the cattle are restricted to a diet of green grass alone affects the flavor of their milk, which in turn affects the flavor of the Ghee.

I am an F1 Hybrid, myself. Yes, my father is 100% Persian while my mother is a typical American of mixed European heritage. As such, I learned to cook a few traditional Persian delights, many of which incorporate ghee. It is for this reason that I have experimented with many different varieties of Ghee. This brand is far superior in flavor and texture. And while my initial interest in ghee was in ethnic cooking, I've found that I use it in a broad array of dishes these days.

Further, it pleases me that this company seems committed to ethical business practices and conservation of the environment. These folks provide a truly superior product with a social conscience. product_title: Annie's Homegrown Gluten-Free Rice Pasta
review_body:
My previous review from July 2012 is below, but something has changed. Since opening our latest case, both my husband and I have become ill after eating this product on both of the two occaisions I have prepared it. Opened brand new milk and butter to make the most recent batch (eliminating suspects), and it left us sicker than the first. Noticed on package sodium phosphate is added. This is the same chemical used for bowel prep before colonoscopy. We can both attest, it's effective for that purpose based on our unfortunate experiences. Will never order again.

I, like most GF folks (I imagine) do a lot of cooking from scratch - but sometimes it's really nice to have a convenience, comfort food classic. No non GF person will mistake this for the real deal (it is rice pasta), but for those who are GF, it fills the craving and is still super-easy to pull off on those nights when more involved cooking just isn't in the cards.

product_title: The Republic Of Tea Get Clean AM Herbal Tea
review_headline: Not Strongly Bitter like Other Medicinal Detox Teas
review_body: In my quest to try all of Republic of Tea's \\"Get ___\\" herbal teas, this was the second one I tried (after \\"Get Gorgeous\\"), and like \\"Get Gorgeous\\" it is one of the few I've tasted that I'll buy again.  I was mainly interested in \\"Get Clean\\" because of its purported liver-detoxing properties, as problems with the liver have been associated with poor skin.  I have been trying to develop a healthy lifestyle that will help me overcome the persistent mild-to-moderate acne I've had for many years, and so far my changes have made a significant difference.  One of my changes has been to reduce caffeine intake (i.e., give up coffee and begin to replace caffeinated teas with herbal teas), drink more water (herbal tea helps me achieve this goal), and drink specifically skin-beneficial teas.  What I especially like about \\"Get Clean\\" in comparison to other teas I've seen recommended for clear skin is that it contains a nice mixture of multiple beneficial herbs.  For example, I drink plain dandelion root tea regularly for its liver-detoxing and skin-clearing properties, but I don't have readily available any plain milk thistle or burdock root tea.  \\"Get Clean\\" contains all three and yet lacks the strong, bitter taste of some plain medicinal teas due to its lovely rooibos base tinged with almond and vanilla.  Also, I think you will like \\"Get Gorgeous\\" and \\"Get Clean\\" almost interchangeably; I take a baggie of tea bags to work every day to sip, and if they are not individually packaged, I smell them briefly to determine which is the one I'm looking for.  Whereas I can easily smell the differences between \\"Get Happy,\\" \\"Get a Grip,\\" \\"Get Lost,\\" etc., I cannot smell the difference between \\"Get Clean\\" and \\"Get Gorgeous.\\"  You can enjoy them both if you like one or the other.  :)

product_title: Glutino Gluten Free Pasta, Spaghetti, 8 Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_body:
Most of the time when you think of gluten free pasta, you think yuck. I mean, let's face it, gluten free sometimes gets a bad name because it doesn't taste as good as the original. But I have to say, that this pasta is exceptionally done, and a moderate price for a gluten free product.

I don't have Celiac's, or even Gluten Intolerance, but I do think that wheat is very prevalent in the average diet anymore. Also, my dad has MS which is sometimes linked to gluten intolerance. So I try to use gluten free products once in awhile, just to cut back on wheat sometimes. And often times he is not happy with the result. But this time, he didn't even know until I told him that the noodles were gluten free. They had the same texture as regular noodles, soft and flexible, yet firm to the bite, and they held sauce very well. The taste was a standard noodle taste, nothing outrageous, but still good and it didn't have that funny aftertaste that gluten free sometimes has.

Cooking was much the same. Simply throw into a pot of boiling water. I do think they took a minute or two longer than normal noodles, but it wasn't any huge difference. I also don't think they stick quite as much after cooking, which is another plus.

I liked the ingredient list. It was short. Whole Grain Brown Rice Flour, Niacin, Ferrous Sulfate, Thiamine Mononitrate, and Riboflavrin. Ok, so there are some unpronounceables in there, but really, it's not any worse than regular noodles. In a box there is 4 servings and 200 calories per servings. It has low fat and sodium though, and 4 grams of protein. So really, not that bad on the nutritional side for a pasta product.

I would definitely buy and use these again. You can't notice the difference and it cuts some of that gluten out of the diet. Not a bad deal.

Review by M. Reynard 2013

product_title: Ips the Original Egg White Chips, 1 Ounce (Pack of 24)
review_body:
I'm a huge fan of alternative snacking. But I still stay away from that stuff because after digested, is usually carbs, fat and salt. Popcorners, pirates booty, lentil chips, snap peas are all made of some form of processed grain. This is also made with cornmeal, but the egg whites give it a nice nutrition boost which is a HUGE plus in my book. Sure, they're not as healthy as say, eating actual egg whites. And you don't get as much protein from say, a serving of peas or yogurt. But how often can you find something that's actually CRUNCHY and nutritious? Because I really just yearn for the crunch. And the salt.

I especially love the cinnamon sugar flavor! It reminds me of cinnamon toast crunch a little, except with signicantly less sugar. Only 3 gs per serving, which is less than my Cascadian Farms cereal! That may be the reason the reviewer below didn't find it very cinnamony. What I like most about Ips is that there are a lot of chips per serving. Usually with popcorners I'm through eating maybe in 2 minutes and I'm wondering where the rest of it went. Ips actually last me quite a while. I think the size of the chips are perfect, and they're not TOO salty or sugary to kick your senses into overdrive and that prevents me from overeating (maybe it's the absense of oil). Nor are the flavors so weak that you keep eating mindlessly. Overall, the perfect snack! This is my favorite flavor along with salt and pepper. I haven't tried the BBQ yet.

product_title: Ras El Hanout 2.0 Oz - Zamouri Spices
review_headline: Fabulous dry-rub for meats and seasoning for ethnic dishes (review includes Morrocan Beef recipe)
review_body:
Ras el hanout is a blend of spices originally from North Africa and is used in many savory dishes and also as a dry-rub for meat. A blend of up to 25-30 different ingredients, it's considered a mixture of the best spices a spice shop has to offer and a seller's recipe for the mix is often a closely-guarded secret. A good Ras El Hanout is highly aromatic with intense flavors.

The label of the Zamouri Spices bottle lists their ingredients: turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, fennel, anise seed, cardamom, galangal, star anise, cayenne pepper, garlic, nigella, paprika, rose buds, salt, ajwan seeds, lavender blossoms, mace, and other spices.

The following is a delicious, highly-flavored recipe that my family loves for Moroccan Beef Tagine using the ras el hanout spice mix.

Spice Rub for meat: 1 level tablespoon *each* of ras el hanout, cumin, ground cinnamon, ginger, and sweet paprika.
Mix all spices together.

1.5 lbs of stewing beef (or lamb), cut into 2\\" chunks
3-4 Tablespoons olive oil
One yellow onion, chopped
1 (14-oz) can garbanzo beans
1 (14-oz) can fire-roasted tomatoes
4 cups stock (beef or vegetable)
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
1 butternut squash (seeded and cut into 1\\" chunks)
4 oz. pitted prunes (cut in half)
½ cup chopped cilantro leaves

Mix all of the spices together in a zip-lock bag and add the meat chunks and massage the spice mixture throughout the surface of the meat. Refrigerate and wait at least 4 hours or overnight before cooking.

To cook, heat the olive oil in a [[ASIN:B001IKK2EK Tagine]] or dutch oven and brown the spiced meat over a medium heat for a few minutes. Add the chopped onion and sauté for another 5 minutes. Add the garbanzo beans and tomatoes, then pour in 2 cups of stock and stir. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then put the lid on the pan and reduce to simmer for 2-3 hours. Add extra broth if it starts getting too dry.

After 2-3 hours of cooking, add the squash, prunes, and the rest of the stock. Cover and continue cooking for 1 more hour.

At the end of cooking time, check the consistency. The beef should fall apart and be extremely tender. If there's too much liquid, simmer uncovered for 5-10 minutes. Check to see if it needs additional salt. Add the cilantro and serve with pearled couscous or rice. Wonderful!unes, and the rest of the stock. Cover and continue cooking for 1 more hour. review_body:
The texture of this ginger candy is fantastic: chewy, but it softens quickly in the mouth. This actually tastes like real high quality ginger. There is pleasant heat to it, but it's not just sugar and blazing fire. I ❤ this candy!
The taste evolves from an early soft heat, to a light ginger taste, into a deep ginger flavor; the taste keeps going, and the heat stays pleasant, never overwhelming. I ❤ this candy!
If you want a ginger flavored candy without ginger's heat and full taste... this is not for you. If you hate any kind of heat then this is not for you, although it's not a punishing heat. If you enjoy a delicious mellow heat and the subtle flavor of ginger snaps that lasts a long time after the candy is gone, this is for you. I ❤ this candy!

review_headline: Verify Lot Number with Heinz Before Using!
review_body:
Please check the lot number (hard to read, but on the bottom of each packet) with Heinz via their website: [...] or by calling 1-800-255-5750.

Regrettably we did not check the reviews on this page before ordering, but upon receiving the package we noticed how much darker the packets were compared to some fresh ones from Chick-fil-a we had left over. This piqued our interest, and so we contacted Heinz with the lot number. To our horror, the product was manufactured on November 3rd, 2011 and has a 270 shelf life (9 months), putting the expiration date at 7/30/2012 - 1 year ago!

Immediately I contacted Amazon customer service, and they were extremely helpful in facilitating a full refund. However, I would really appreciate Amazon following up with this vendor on how they are selling such large quantities of this product for so cheap. Of course I want the best price for a product, but I don't want that product to be expired.

review_headline: Exactly what I was looking for
review_body:

No foul smells like many new plastic products when they first come out of the box. I gave it a quick rinse and it was good to go. After 10 days and 10 gallons, I couldn't be happier. If you're looking for a simple, one gallon water bottle, I'd certainly recommend this one!

UPDATE: After almost exactly two years with this thing, it finally cracked. A tiny crack, about half an inch long, formed about half an inch from the bottom. Just enough for a small trickle of a leak, nothing catastrophic, but I'll need to replace it. I was nowhere near gentle with this through the course of its life, often carelessly tossing it into my car while completely full. Other than that, it has survived dozens of drops onto hard surfaces. For the price, I'm still extremely satisfied with it and won't hesitate order another if I don't decide to cough up some extra cash for a 64oz Kleen Kanteen (or two).

product_title: Ekobrew Coffee Reusable Filter, Small, Violet
review_body:
When I first opened the package, I was a little disappointed because I thought I was getting two pods, not one. But that was my fault- I had read so many reviews before ordering and some of the brands have 2 pods in the package. My mistake.
Although I LOVE coffee, I am not a Keurig fan. Let me explain-I am not bashing the brand, it's just because I have never found any pods that I really like enough to justify the price. My personal coffee taste runs toward Dunkin Donuts, as opposed to Starbucks which is too strong (is that really the right word?) for me. So- that comparison may help you understand why I'm not crazy about Keurig coffees. Again, not the brand or the coffee- just me.
This pod works great in the Keurig coffee maker. You put the pod in the coffee maker the same way you would a regular pod. I have used Folgers and Maxwell House coffee and both make a surprisingly good cup of coffee. You can adjust the strength by how much coffee you put in the basket/pod.
You do get a little sediment in your cup. For anyone that drinks French press coffee, you're already used to that. It doesn't affect the flavor.
It rinses clean nicely. I don't know how long it will last, but if you get more than a couple weeks use out of it, I think it's worth the price. And if you are \\"green\\" then that's another plus.
Also- this item qualifies for Super Saver shipping. I bought it when I needed to add something to my order to make the minimum.

Update 5/17/14 - I have been using this pod every day at work for over a year. Still works great, still rinses clean, although a little lime scale became noticeable on the top. Fixed that by soaking in vinegar and rinsing completely. I certainly have gotten my money's worth out of this!

review_headline: Yummy and A Good Sized Box
review_body:
I love to serve spaghetti for dinner. And lunches. And snacks. I love it because it's tasty (if you buy the right brand) and I love it because it's super easy to make and very, VERY affordable. And these days pasta is stretching my budget very well, thank you.

Certainly everyone in my household-- from dad to picky tween and picky teen to dogs-- eats this spaghetti with gusto. Some with Barilla sauce; some with just butter, depending on their mood.

Highly recommend. 6 Minutes cooking time and with a minimum of fuss you can throw a warm meal on the table. The 32-ounce size I thought was fantastic as the kids are starting to eat more. And it never hurts to have one small bowl leftover for lunch the next day.

review_headline: Excellent Peanut Butter - First Roast Then Vitamix
review_body: Just a quick note to say that these peanuts make the best peanut butter EVER.  Roast them first at 325 for about 20 minutes, let them cool in a paper grocery sack then shake loose the skins.  Fill your Vitamix about 3/4 full then start blending.  Use the reamer to jam the mix around until it starts to come together.  Once it does, the speed and power of the Vitamix will start to emulsify the mix and after a couple minutes you'll have the most amazing peanut butter ever.  Add nothing to the mix, except a little salt if you think you need it.

These are really good noodles. You wouldn't even know they're whole wheat; they don't have that grainy texture and sour taste that some whole wheat noodles have. They have just a little more nutty flavor than traditional noodles. They cook up really nice & taste delicious.

My favorite lasagna recipe is the \\"America's Test Kitchen - Simple Meat Lasagna\\" from their \\"Family Cookbook\\". This recipe calls for oven-ready lasagna noodles. I often swap out the ground beef/pork mixture with all ground turkey OR half Italian sausage/ground turkey. The all cheese version is also good.

product_title: Pure Matcha, Premium Ceremonial Grade Matcha
review_body:
I have tried numerous other matchas, and for the most part have been satisfied. This one, however, is easily my favorite. Being that it is ceremonial grade, I would expect a higher quality than other standard versions. Where it really stands out, though, is its quality for the price. The actual powder is among the most vibrant green that I have seen (tea leaves were young and harvested well), and it has a nice \\"bright\\" herbal fragrance. The taste is outstanding (sweet, rich, and fresh), and it blends very easily. The top on the container seals very well, and eliminates the messiness of the inner bag that other brands have. I don't know if it makes sense to describe a tea as \\"convenient\\", but this really is. The only other matcha that comes close is the DoMatcha 1st or 2nd harvest, but they are priced in an almost laughable range. They don't taste any better; they just cost more.

I had e-mailed the seller for any tips he had on the best method of preparation, and I actually felt he shared the same love for tea that my wife and I have. Very fast shipping, and good communication. Kudos...

product_title: Runa Amazon Guayusa, 1 Pound
review_headline: A delicious new choice for tea lovers
review_body:
If you're like me, you were hesitant to buy this one. Surely it would be just another weak and geriatric herbal drink trying to market itself as a proper tea? If that's the case, I'm going to give you the same advice I give everyone- don't be like me!

Give this beverage a go, it's certainly cheap enough to be a safe experiment and I would be shocked if it disappointed any tea lover.

I would describe the flavor as almost like a blend of different styles of tea. It has the light, almost crisp earthiness and rich color of a darjeeling; the light grassiness of your favorite green, and the floral/minty notes of the better herbal teas. It's unique, yet more familiar than you may be expecting. And it's goooood.

I don't get much caffeine benefit from this one, though. The effect is present, but it's not something that would get me out of bed in the morning like coffee or black tea would. This is more of an afternoon/evening pick-me-up. Still good!
