product_title: Nestle Bottled Water 16.9oz Per Bottle, 24 Bottle Case (Brand Varies By Region)
review_body: Nestle sends different water per your region. Here in Michigan I received Ice Mountain water. I'll have to say without a doubt this is excellence beyond compare. It's refreshing and light without a hint of heaviness due to chemicals. I received my cases a few days after ordering which was another plus.

product_title: Mighty Leaf Tea Mighty Leaf Variety
review_body:
This tea lacks um, flavor. At first I thought it was me. I brewed again using about half the water I've used in other teas. Still no flavor. The citrus notes were completely missing from the Earl Grey. The Orange Dulce tasted like very weak orange spice tea. I did not expect the tea to hold up to loose leaf tea blends, but I've have had far better luck with Twinings or Tazo. Even Stash or Bigelow are superior to me.

It was so mediocre and the other reviews have generally been positive so I double checked the expiration date on my box. I thought perhaps it was just very, very old tea that had once been good. But no, I have well over a year before it should have expired.

product_title: Quaker Soft Baked Oatmeal Cookie, Chocolate Almond, 8.8 Ounce
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:moN2D17TCLHA9S]]These cookies have an earthen texture and consistency that conjures up images of the mud pies and beach sand cakes my sons used to make. The ingredients note no less than three preservatives (TBHQ, BHT and citric acid) and nearly as many adjectives as nouns - Modified, Enriched, Bleached, Reduced and Artificial.

Ugh.

Instead of referencing my thesaurus for more words to express the crumbly-blandness of these cookies, I decided to make a short video. I'm sure it better illustrates the appetite-suppressing texture. As for the underwhelming taste, I turned to another resource: my sons (ages 9 and 8) are excellent food critics, albeit not the most discerning ones. I need only leave a plate of food within arm's reach while they play board games, their Xbox 360 or watch a movie. Snacks like watermelon, popcorn or licorice, disappear quickly.

However, both boys passed on the Quaker Soft Baked Oatmeal Cookie opened for the video review. That sums it up for me.

Rating: One star.

Do you need to satisfy a sweet tooth? I recommend [[ASIN:B005BPVB9S Eat. Think. Smile. Crispy Thins, Sweet Cinnamon]] instead.

review_body: While this sausage is not quite the same item as its namesake Gyulai kolbász from Hungary, since it is not a dry sausage, it is nevertheless quite delicious, with the overall flavoring very similar to the original. I however like its consistency as it comes in the packaging, and have been enjoying this great product for years in lieu of real Hungarian made kolbász (smoked sausage) in the US. People with sensitive palates may want to try the mild version of this sausage, although I find the hotness of this variety fairly timid.

product_title: Earth's Best Organic Whole Grain Multi-Grain Cereal, 8 Ounce (Pack of 12)
review_body: This was my son's very first solid food.  He really likes it, and I use it by itself and for mixing different fruits and veggies.  He would not eat green beans until I mixed them with this.  I like the fact that he's not eating single grain white rice which is said to contribute to a preference of processed white bread and pasta later on.  Now suddenly I can't find this on store shelves anywhere except for the local health food store, which means I have to pay a premium for it.  I'm guessing this is due to the recent arsenic scare with brown rice products.  I personally don't understand the hype.  We were told to eat brown rice for years because of the health benefits, and now it's back to white rice?  I would rather feed my son whole grain.  I do try to limit the amount he consumes and I use EB oatmeal with his fruits, but it's still great cereal.  No bugs here, or at least so far!

product_title: Arrowroot Starch/Flour
review_headline: much better than wheat flour and corn starch!
review_body:
After reading Wheat Belly I decided I want to consume much less wheat and wheat flour products for my health. I also realize that until products carry the GMO label that I need to avoid wheat and corn based foods to avoid GMO crops. Arrowroot powder is a very appropriate replacement for flour or cornstarch for thickening, plus it contains other beneficial properties as well.

I discovered through trial and error that it is possible to make a \\"white gravy\\" utilizing arrowroot powder and either nut milk ir coconut milk along with sea salt and other seasonings. Experiment with arrowroot powder and let your creative juices flow. At this price point per pound you cannot go wrong. Sauces and gravies require much less arrowroot powder as a thickener than when using flour or cornstarch.

The texture of the meat itself is great: tender but not mushy, thin but not shredded. I also really appreciate the company using wheat-free soy sauce. But this flavor needs to go back to R&D.

product_title: Pop Secret Popcorn
review_body:
This popcorn is just the right amount of sweet: not so overpowering that it tastes like candy, but you can definitely tell that it's kettle corn!

The portion size is also perfect for one person. I consider myself a relatively big eater, but by the time I'm done with one bag I'm pretty satisfied (mostly because it takes so much time to get through one).

I also like the nutrition breakdown of this popcorn: lots of fiber (4g), a solid amount of protein (3g), and no sugar. Sure, it has ~4g of fat, but overall it's almost a perfect ratio of fat to carbs to protein, with the added benefit of the fiber and lack of sugar. What a great snack! I can't think of any other food item that is only 100 calories, tastes this good, has even a marginally good nutrient breakdown, and tides you over for an hour or more.

product_title: TVP
review_headline: I was sceptical, but I actually like this stuff
review_body:
I was told by a friend that TVP of any kind tastes nasty and looks worse. Well, she was wrong and so was I, for being sceptical.

I used this to make sloppy joes. After I rehydrated it with a 1:1 ratio of water to TVP, I stirred in chopped-up onions and green peppers with a can of Hunt's sloppy joe mix. (Yes, I'm a bachelor and I cook stuff from cans rather than from scratch--so sue me.)

My first taste of this vegetarian sloppy joe mix was \\"eh, not bad\\". Then I added some coarsely ground black pepper and some hot sauce to the mix--and et voila! What resulted was a tangy sloppy joe mix that tastes great on a lightly toasted sesame seed bun. I garnished with a slice of fresh tomato and some lettuce (and in the future, a slice of colby jack cheese?), and am very pleased with the results. This tastes almost as good as that ground sirloin sloppy joe mix I made a few nights ago, and that's saying something. I imagine you could even improve the flavor by adding in some browned ground beef. If you don't like spicy food, or your stomach won't tolerate it, do NOT buy this stuff, because adding your own spices is crucial to successfully reaching the center of Flavor Town.

i think that if you put in a little more effort than I did, and made your sloppy joe mix from scratch, this would taste that much better. Don't look to me for the answer on that one: as I said, bachelor, lazy, not going to happen.

I haven't tried any other recipes with this TVP, but I imagine its uses are limited because it just doesn't act like ground beef or even ground turkey. I can't imagine making a meat(less) loaf with it, for example, or a hamburger(less) patty, but I'll Google to see if anyone else has successfully done this. It's obvious this TVP could also be used successfully with spaghetti sauce, whether from a jar or homemade--but again, remember, spices spices spices.

By the way, I was pleasantly surprised to see that TVP is not only high in protein but high in fiber: Bob'sTVP is zero fat, zero cholesterol, and one serving has 16% of the recommended daily fiber and 24% of the recommended daily protein in your diet. All that for only 80 calories!nly high in protein but high in fiber: Bob'sTVP is zero fat, zero cholesterol, and one serving has 16% of the recommended daily fiber and 24% of the recommended daily protein in your diet. All that for only 80 calories!

product_title: Anthony's Blanched Gluten Free Almond Flour
review_body:
I recently moved over to a Paleo diet, not so much from choice but as a necessity. The conversion has been rough, not so much the giving up sugar as it was giving up grains. I miss pizza, muffins, etc., and I was pretty happy to learn that I could use Almond Flour to try and get pretty close to regular flour. Initially I went out and bought [[ASIN:B000EDG598 Bob's Red Mill Almond Meal/Flour, 16-Ounce Packages (Pack of 4)]], used it and made some blueberry muffins. They came out great. The texture was good, the taste was good. The price however was horrible.

I searched Amazon.com. The reviews for Anthony's Almond Flour looked good and of course the price was VERY good. I ordered,it came in the mail, well packaged and sealed, and I on the spot went to making those muffins I mentioned from earlier, same recipe.

The texture however came out...odd. The Muffins this round did not cook as well as the last batch. Not that I care too much what the food looks like as long as it is good. However the taste was BAD. I am not a picky eater and tried to finish off ONE muffin. Could not do it. Reminded me of those old stories of food packaging places cutting the flour with sawdust to make it go farther. It was that bad.

Now I see this product is currently, of the time of this review, not available. Makes me suspect of the product and all the other reviews. But this part is just subjective, I can say that Anthony's Almond Flour did not cook well and tasted horrible. Not bad enough for me to think it was stale, but bad enough to not want to ever use it again.

I will try some other brands, as well as trying to home make some Almond Flour and see how it comes out.

product_title: Hard Rhino Sucralose Powder
review_headline: Perfect and economical replacement for Splenda and store-brand Sucralose
review_body:
This stuff is indistinguishable in taste from the \\"stretched\\" products like granular Splenda and far far less expensive! Once you get used to measuring such tiny amounts, it's very easy to use. To give you some idea of its strength, 1/8 teaspoon is equal to 1.5 cups of sugar. For a bowl of cereal, a match-head worth is plenty. Grab some of the flat, wooden coffee stirrers from your local coffee shop (or buy them) and use the tip as a measure. I use the smallest of a tiny set of measuring spoons available at many places including Amazon. The smallest is called a \\"smidgen\\" and I use about half that for a 12-ounce mug of coffee. And I like my coffee very sweet.

I paid about $37 including tax for 3.5 ounces of sucralose. To get the sugar equivalent, multiply by 600: 3.5*600=2100 ounces of sugar. 2100/16=131.25 pounds of sugar. Splenda granular is sold in 5 and 10 pound equivalent bags. I'll use the larger 10-pound equivalent which is less expensive. One such bag costs a minimum of $13 anywhere I can find it including Amazon with the exception of sales. If you figure the number of 10# equivalent bags: 131.25/10=13.13. Multiply this by $13 to get the amount you'd pay for this much sucralose \\"fluffed up\\" into Splenda: 13.13*$13=$170.00. So you're getting roughly $170 worth of sweetener for a price of around $37. I call that a bargain.

Add to that the absence of maltodextrin which is used to make Splenda Granular \\"fluffy\\". It isn't all that bad for my blood sugar and I'm diabetic; I've heard others claim otherwise. But the stuff gives me gastric \\"issues\\" and I do not miss it! It is known to cause gas and diarrhea in sensitive individuals.

product_title: SNackette Tortilla Chips Family Pack, Multigrain, 5-Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_body:
I have recently been enamored with a new brand of salsa, so when I found these chips on sale, given the price, I elected to overlook the unfamiliar brand, and child targeted packaging; I mean how bad could a tortilla chip be, right?

As it turns out, I am really impressed with this product... I was surprised to find that it contains the very healthy addition of chia seeds, which adds nutrient value, and the last (least) ingredient is salt. To be honest, to my tastes, a little more salt wouldn't be a bad thing, but after getting used to them, it really isn't a negative, even for a salt junkie, and the health benefit is a plus.

I purchased the veggie and the multi-grain varieties of this brand, and like them both, but if I had to choose, I think my favorite would be the veggie. The difference in flavor isn't dramatic, but the veggie chips seem a bit more nuanced in flavor. (If it matters to anyone, the veggie chips are a burnt orange color, whereas the multi-grain are the usual color of a yellow corn tortilla chip). I would, however, recommend them both. I am looking forward to trying some of their other products as well.

The one minus is that they are not organic, so it is not clear if the corn is non-GMO, but they are presented as \\"natural\\" and the product certainly lives up to that claim; there are no chemical ingredients, artificial flavors, or colors. Overall, that one caveat aside, a quality product; and the addition of chia seeds (which would account for some of the fat content, in a healthy way), and pleasing taste with minimal salt, makes this a reasonably healthy sanck at a fair price. I would highly recommend this brand.

product_title: Bigelow Organic Green Tea, 160-Count
review_headline: Let's compare Bigelow Organic Green Tea 160 Tea Bags vs. Bigelow Organic Green Tea 150 Tea Bags
review_body: Let's compare Premium Bigelow Green Tea 100% Organic 160 Tea Bags Individually Wrapped, which is priced at $13.66 with FREE Super Saver Shipping, against Premium Bigelow Green Tea 100% Organic 150 Tea Bags Individually Wrapped, which is priced at $14.99 with FREE Super Saver Shipping.  Both boxes contain tea that is extremely healthy for us to drink.  Both boxes contain tea that was grown and very slightly fermented in China.  Both boxes have tea bags that are exactly the same size.  Both boxes contain tea bags that are individually wrapped in sealed, easy-open, metallic foil pouches.  Although different, both boxes have attractive designs.  Bigelow includes 160 tea bags, not 175 tea bags as falsely pictured, in this product but only 150 tea bags in the other product.  Yes, the design (picture) on each individual tea bag is always exactly the same as the design (picture) on the outside of the box that it came in.  The box provided for the 160 tea bags is slightly more rigid and easier to open and close than the box provided for the 150 tea bags.  After buying both boxes of Bigelow Green Tea, I couldn't find any reason why the 150 tea bags were priced higher than the 160 tea bags.  Although Bigelow Organic Green Tea is still a good deal today, 3 years ago, Bigelow Organic Green Tea was priced at only 6.1 cents per tea bag and had substantially more organic green tea in each metallic foil wrapped tea bag.

product_title: 6 Pack Cincinnati Chili Mix Packets
review_headline: Great flavor, ultimate comfort food ... now doctor it up ...
review_body:
I am a BIG fan of this mix, and I make a lot of different kinds of chili. It creates an awesome flavor and you serve it over pasta. However, I have a very nontraditional recipe which is killer good. I make this often. It is the ultimate comfort food. Some of you purists will hate this, but here is the recipe (try it before you complain):

Doctored Cincinnati chili recipe

1 pkg Cincinnati chili mix, from Skytime
Additional chili powder and cumin (not super spicy), to your preference
1 to 1 ½ pounds ground beef
1 6 oz can tomato paste
1 15 oz can diced tomatoes
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 onion
3 stalks celery
3 carrots
1 green pepper
16 oz mushrooms, sliced
2 15 oz cans of red kidney beans
Chili powder
Cumin
Salt

Step one:

-- In a large pot, combine package of chili mix with can of tomato paste, can of diced tomatoes, 6 cups of water . Can also add a bit of additional red chili and cumin at this point
-- Add the ground beef. Do not brown.
-- Heat to a boil, reduce and simmer about 1 hour

Step two:

-- Saute garlic and onions in a large skillet. After about 3 minutes, when onion gets soft, add celery, carrots and green pepper.
-- After a minute or two, add the mushrooms and a dash of salt. When the mushrooms are just starting to get soft, add chili powder and cumin to the mixture and continue sautéing until the mushrooms have released moisture.
-- Add the sauté mixture to the pot of chili
-- Add the kidney beans to the mixture
-- Simmer until the flavors are well mixed, at least a half hour

Serve over pasta of your choice, garnished with parmesan cheese.

product_title: Indus Organics Ceylon Cinnamon Powder, Premium Grade, High Purity, Freshly Packed
review_body: My husband suffers from type 2 diabetes, and he believes in a pro-active approach to his health care.  He did a great deal of research on the topic of nutrition, supplements, and diabetes and found that cinnamon is recommended for helping to lower and maintain blood sugar levels.  He had been using my baking cinnamon, but the Ceylon Cinnamon was being mentioned in just about every article that he read.  So I searched and found it on Amazon, and at an incredible price.  The order was placed, it arrived as scheduled, and he started using it on his morning cereal.  He uses 1/4 to 1/2 teaspoon per serving, sprinkled over his cold cereal.  Ceylon Cinnamon Powder tastes and smells differently than regular cinnamon (and that includes Saigon cinnamon).  And the taste is very dissimilar to what I use for baking.  And did it help him at all?  Yes, it did and he continues using it daily.  His neurologist and rheumatologist are both supportive since they  are homeopathic doctors, as is his primary care physician.  My husband is diligent about checking his glucose level and he watches what he eats (I do all the cooking, so I purchase and prepare food for BOTH of us, and I simply adjust recipes so that we are each getting the most nutritional benefits).  I do not, however, use this cinnamon when a recipe calls for it, because it definitely does not impart the scent and taste that is associated with regular cinnamon.  The price on the Indus Organic Ceylong Cinnamon is incredibly priced, much lower than I was able to locate anywhere, and you get 2 one pound jars.  So if you know someone with whom you can share, you would each get a jar and cut the cost.  A jar lasts quite a while. It was months before the second jar was opened.  Be aware that you should not figure that if 1/4 to 1/2 tsp is good, that more would be better for you.  Not so --- you could wind up with intestinal problems, for one.  So don't overdo.  And check with your doctor(s) before following any advice given on line.  Good luck in your venture :-)

product_title: Heartland Food Products Signature Recipe Belgian Waffle Mix, Harvest Grain, 5 Pound
review_body:
I agree with another reviewer that this mix is too sweet. A look at the ingredients and nutrition facts explains why. This new \\"Harvest\\" multigrain has 50% more sugar than the old Heartland Malted Multigrain mix (15 grams per serving versus 10 grams in the old version). In addition to sugar the mix ALSO contains dextrose (a sugar) and \\"may\\" contain sucralose (aka Splenda) and or acesulfame potassium (another artificial sweetener). These extra sugars and sweeteners weren't in the old Multigrain mix.

Before buying this I scoured the web in vain looking for the ingredients. Due to positive reviews I bought it anyway. For those who are considering buying this, the ingredients are as follows:

\\"Contains: Wheat flour, whole wheat flour, oat flour, corn meal, may contain one of the following (soybean oil, sunflower oil, or coconut oil), sugar, whole egg, leavening (baking soda, sodium aluminum phosphate, mono calcium phosphate), soy flour, malt, nonfat milk, salt, natural and artificial flavors, dextrose, may contain sucralose and/or acesulfame potassium, soy lecithin, caramel color\\".

The mix isn't terrible, although it's too sweet for me. However, it seems that some reviewers think that it is particularly healthy, I guess because it is called multigrain. Note, however, that this is not primarily a WHOLE grain product: the primary ingredient is plain white flour. Each serving has almost no vitamins or minerals, only 3 grams of fiber, only 5 grams of protein but has a lot of sodium: 910 mg. In fact, if you are interested in healthy eating, the Heartland Malted Vanilla mix has LESS calories, fat, cholesterol, sodium and sugar (plus has one gram more of fiber) than this Harvest Multigrain mix.

In summary, if you like your waffles sweet and don't mind the flavor of artificial sweetener then you may like this mix, but it's nothing special and doesn't make sense to buy in the belief that it is especially healthy.

review_headline: Ok if you like acetone, methanol, ethanol, acetonitrile, and isopropanol.
review_body: Bought this thinking it was natural.  Boy was I wrong, REALLY WRONG!  Came across this AFTER buying the product.  I haven't used any of it nor will I, EVER!  Since I can't return it, it's heading to the trash bin.  I'll stick with my all natural xylitol, thank you very much!!  [...]  \\"First things first, is Truvia made from a leaf?  Well the answer is kinda, sorta.  Truvia has three ingredients:  erythritol, rebiana, and natural flavors.  Rebiana is made from the stevia leaf by soaking it in water.  Although Cargill whitewashes the process as similar to making tea, the truth is revealed in Coca-Cola's patent where it outlines a 40+ step process that includes the use of acetone, methanol, ethanol, acetonitrile, and isopropanol.  I don't know about you, but when I make a cup of tea, I've never used any of those ingredients.\\"

product_title: Hodgson Mill Organic Naturally White Flour, Unbleached All-Purpose, 2-Pounds (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Excellent organic white flour - No more bloating or puffiness after eating flour!
review_body:
I've been using Hodgson Mill Organic Naturally White Flour for about a year now. One of the first things I noticed after baking with this flour is that I no longer \\"bloated\\" or had intestinal distress after eating the foods made with this flour. Soooo nice! My doctor recommended this flour to me, and I'm glad I followed his recommendation. I did an experiment to make sure that it wasn't a coincidence that after eating the Hodgson Mill Organic Naturally white flour I didn't bloat, become puffy, etc. I made some cookies and muffins using the Hodgson Mill flour, and I made the same cookie and muffin recipe with typical white flour (all the rest of the (organic) ingredients were identical). I had intestinal distress, bloated, and had facial and hand puffiness after eating the desserts with the typical flour. When the bloating subsided, I waited an additional 6-8 hours, and I ate the desserts made with the Hodgson Mill flour....nothing happened - no bloating, no puffiness, and I felt great. The Hodgson Mill flour makes you feel good after eating it. I'm delighted to find a flour that doesn't have an adverse reaction on me. ALSO! The flour bakes and cooks great. The texture is wonderful - actually better than typical flour. My cookies, breads, muffins, pie crust, brownies, gravy, etc come out wonderful with this flour. I receive a lot of compliments on my desserts when using Hodgson Mill organic flour. Sometimes people find it hard to believe when I tell them that the flour is organic and naturally white. They can't believe the flour produces such great results.

The flour ships quickly and stores well on your pantry shelf. I keep it in the refrigerator after opening it. I like that it comes in two pound bags - very convenient for me. I definitely recommend this flour.

review_body: I spent quite some time researching the Kippered Snacks available to me online.  I went with this product because it had a lower sodium content, no added ingredients, and I was impressed with Crown Prince seafood company when I went to their website.  An added bonus, the price was very good... even better than some of the companies that added artificial ingredients and tons of salt.  Today, I tried my first can of these Kipper Snacks and was very pleased. I was afraid there would be bones because these weren't advertized as \\"boneless\\" like the Kipper Snacks I used to get.  But there was not a single bone, there was plenty of nourishing \\"fish juice\\" that the kipper was nestled in, and the taste was just as good as the kippers that are packed in tons of salt.  Also, the fish itself was firm, not soft and squishy like the other kippered snacks I was used to. Now I know I've made the right choice and will continue purchasing my Kipper Snacks from Crown Prince from now on.  Would highly recommend this brand to anyone!

review_body: I've been purchasing Morton & Bassett for years and I've never been disappointed.  I love that this is salt free with no preservatives, just unadulterated tasty herbs.  I've tried many other Italian Seasoning but I always come back to this one, it has the perfect blend.  When I make my spaghetti sauce I start with fresh tomatoes or if off season then cans of crushed tomatoes.  Some seasoning leave the sauce seem blah or one note.  Sometimes the problem may be the tomatoes or other aromatics I use but these spices help even out any blandness from the fresh produce and just make the sauce taste complete.  I love that I can add as little as a teaspoon to a whole jar and I don't have to worry about salt or anything else mucking up the flavor of the herbs.  I always make sure I have this on hand and when I get down to one jar I order more.

I have reordered a few times already, and will be doing so again. This is good stuff and a good value.

Being on the road so much has limited my availabity to great indian restaurant and when I saw this on amazon I thought wow I must have these. product_title: Bell Plantation PB2 with Premium Chocolate
review_body: As I said above, I LOVE this stuff. Yeah all capitals on love ;). I have been eating this product for almost a year now, and while I started with the regular peanut butter flavor, I tried the chocolate soon after and never looked back. I use this every morning in my homemade oatmeal. I use instant Quaker multigrain oats about 50 grams(much heartier & filling than regular quick oats), along with some dark brown sugar 6 grams, a sprinkle of Butter Buds season salt, a serving of Chocolate PB2, some kosher salt to taste don't know how much & about 11-12 grams of Ghirardelli 60% bittersweet chocolate chips (they're dark chocolate chips). Overall when I use 50g of instant oats,  it is about 295 calories according to My Fitness Pal calorie counting app on my phone. Using the serving size of 40g is about 262 calories. 40g is 1 serving according to the container I believe but I like just a little more.  I got the idea when I purchased the Quaker instant oatmeal in Chocolate Chip flavor for my kids. I was starting a diet and was eating as healthy as possible, and I thought hey, I can make this but in a healthier form. I have since been eating this and an apple daily for breakfast for about 9 months now and it's the only thing I look forward to eating every morning. That's amazing since I usually get sick of eating the same thing after awhile and need a break. Sometimes I never even crave that particular food again if I've really overeaten on it. I now often eat it as part of my dinner as well since I crave it so often. It's almost like a dessert when I use semi-sweet or milk chocolate chips. I have also used different types of chocolate chips (semi sweet, milk chocolate, Hershey's special dark choc, etc.) but usually go back to using the Ghirardelli due to the so called health benefits of eating small amounts of dark chocolate that is made of at least 60% cacoa. I have maintained my goal weight for the past 9 months and have not gained additional weight eating this, so for meit is not only healthy, but a somewhat guilt free indulgence at times when my body craves a sweet dessert. All good things in moderation though, if I ate this in larger quantities or more often in the day the carbs and sugar Would catch up to me and I would start to gain weight again, so just like everything else you need to be conscious of calories in and calories out if you want to add this to a healthy diet. Love it!!!

product_title: Manitoba Harvest Hemp Pro 50 Protein Supplement, 16 Ounce
review_body:
YES! While this might lack the protein per cup of whey, rice, or soy protein, it has numerous advantages. It is more of a slow digester...and with it's large amount of carbs, it's fitting for a preworkout if you need something in your stomach for energy. It has a ton of fiber per serving, and I need not fill in the blanks as to what that entails. But most importantly, it's PACKED with omega-3's, which is just SUPERB! Word on the street is that when you eat foods rich in omega-3's, you feel less depressed and more PEPPY! Your brain functions just a wee bit better! You might even feel a little....SILLY. It is hemp after all. The negative is that this product has about 6 grams of sugar per 8 grams of protein...which is rather high. Pun intended. Manitoba also sells a non flavored hemp protein which has far less sugar but all the benefits...so that's your solution if this doesn't pan out.

In conclusion...it's a solid protein source that your body will find easy to digest. It's organic, and it's vegan. And for a hemp protein, this is one of the better tasting ones. Manitoba also has a better extraction process than other hemp protein manufacturers...this is a trustworthy brand. Take this ALONG with another protein supplement for best results!

review_headline: Mild, flavorful and not too salty

These are pleasant flavored sardines packed in a fairly flavorless olive oil- still better than the cheap oils used in a lot of canned fish. They're sin on, and bone in, with enough scales left on that you'll certainly want to scrape them off before eating. The bones are soft enough that you don't have to remove them, but they're large enough that they pop right out. I bought mine at Whole Foods, where they were $2.99, which is significantly cheaper than this deal. If you're interested in trying them I'd check your local stores first.

Personally, I prefer the [[ASIN:B000EF3E2W Crown Prince Two Layer Brisling Sardines in Extra Virgin Olive Oil, 3.75-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12)]]. Smaller (and tastier) sardines, packed in extra virgin olive oil, and significantly cheaper, too.

product_title: Ekobrew Coffee Reusable Filter, Small, Violet
review_body:
I had high hopes for the Ekobrew, but it just didn't work for me. The first couple of trials failed due to my \\"operator error\\" in overfilling the cup. After those first tries, I figured out how to fill the Ekobrew, and I still had problems with leakage. Coffee dripped out of the Keurig in all directions, making a huge mess. Grounds spilled into the coffee cup. Worse yet, it tasted nothing like coffee. The color looked good, but.. the flavor of coffee was completely absent...tasted like hot water. I've tried various grinds of coffee from drip to very fine. I cannot recommend this product.

Update: As other reviewers recommended, I took apart a disposable K-cup to study the anatomy and coffee quantity and texture. Now I see why the Ekobrew cannot work as well as a disposable K-cup. First, the disposable K-cup has a paper filter inside, which filters out all of the sludge and dust that is not contained by the Ekobrew. The paper filter does not reach to the bottom of the K-cup, leaving a dead space between the bottom of the filter and the bottom of the cup. Finally, the Ekobrew cannot be watertight at the top because of the closure mechanism, even with the washer add-on suggested by some reviewers. This just can't be leak proof like the disposable K-cup's glued-and-sealed cover. So, I see two key design flaws: The Ekobrew is doomed to leak and has no paper filter mechanism to catch all the unwanted coffee sludge. The Ekobrew is a well-intentioned product, but cannot produce the same quality outcome. Again, I do not recommend this product in its current design state, but I hope that someone can design a re-usable K-cup replacement that will produce the same quality coffee as a disposable.

review_headline: INGREDIENTS & COOKING TIPS; tastes great, my family loves it...
review_body:
My family loves dale's Steak Seasoning and we've been using it for years. The savory flavor tastes great on beef and pork (dale's suggests using it on lamb, poultry, fish, wild game, and vegetables as well, but I haven't). It comes in two blends, regular and a reduced sodium. Both are excellent.

I usually marinate meats for 10-30 minutes if time allows before cooking, but in a pinch I have just applied and cooked. The end result is always flavorful.

Dale's Steak Seasoning is MADE IN THE USA by dale's Seasoning in Birmingham, Alabama and began in 1946 from an old family recipe with secret herbs and spices.

TIPS TO GRILL THE PERFECT STEAK USING DALE'S STEAK SEASONING:
1) Marinate beef in dale's Seasoning 30 minutes to 1 hour prior to grilling. A zip-lock bag works great to ensure even coating.
2) Allow ¾ to 1lb. per person for bone-in steak or ½ lb. per person for boneless steak.
3) Choose steaks that are at least 1 inch thick.
4) Trim off fat to 1/8 inch and score the edges to keep them from curling on the grill.
5) Flip steak when the juices start to bubble on the top (uncooked side).
6) The second side of the steak needs less grilling time than the first.
7) Baste steak with dale's seasoning during cooking to enhance flavor even more.

COOKTIME BASED ON THICKNESS OF STEAK IN INCHES:

*MEDIUM: 1\\" - 20 to 25 minutes; 1 ½\\" - 20 to 25 minutes; 2\\" - 20 to 25 minutes

This is a huge box of SToK shots. They arrive in a case of individually packaged shots of 40mG of caffeine.
My package had 270. I love when manufactures intentionally err on the side of the consumer.

These shots are packages in a small container that looks similar to the usual creamers you receive from a restaurant.
Peel back the top and pour into your beverage. They have a very slight bitter taste but,
I have figured out how to flavor my coffee so I don't even notice it.

As recommended by the manufacturer there is a limit of 2 per day.
I laugh at this when you do the math 40mG x 2 = 80mG. An average energy drink has way more than this.
The smallest 8 oz. Red Bull has 80 mg. A large Monster has over 120 mg.

They do not need to be refrigerated. This vendor sells to Amazon at a great price

product_title: Special K Protein Shake (10-Ounce), 4-Count Bottles (Pack of 6)
review_body:
Although my status as a \\"chocolate milk connoisseur\\" is self-proclaimed, I think my lifetime of daily chocolate milk consumption from dairies all over the United States and Canada probably makes me somewhat of a chocolate milk expert, LOL. Earlier this year, I decided to lose weight, which meant giving up my lifelong vice. As part of my new diet, I substituted my daily quart of chocolate milk for one ten-ounce Special K Protein Shake.

As far as flavor goes, these shakes are excellent. Compared to Slim Fast shakes, the Special K shakes have a more natural, less processed taste. Achieving that taste, however, comes at a price. There's plenty of sugar and calories in these things... much like actual chocolate milk. Thank goodness they come in 10-ounce bottles, because if they came in quart bottles, I'd still be fat.

Do they satisfy hunger? Yeah, but not always for long -- maybe 45 minutes tops for active people, or an hour or two for less active people. Because of that, they don't seem to work as meal replacements. I prefer to think of Special K Protein Shakes as expensive, vitamin-enriched, sensible portions of chocolate milk. They make good snacks and after-meal desserts, and will tide you over until you can eat a regular meal.

I would like to give these shakes five stars, but I think they, like Slim Fast, are literally TOO sweet and chocolatey to be taken seriously by dieters. Sugar just makes you crave more sugar. If Special K took some of sugar out, even though it would affect taste, I think these shakes would have more appeal to dieters. Also, the shakes are needlessly overpriced. A gallon's worth of Special K Protein Shake costs around $24.

I want to alert you to the possibility of getting a bad shake now and then. I purchased three eight-packs from Wal-Mart in Greenfield, Wisconsin earlier this fall. All of the 24 bottles had the same expiration date of 6/7/13, but one or two of the shakes from each box--even though they were sealed like all the others--had soured. Obviously something must have gone wrong at the factory.

If you're wondering how my diet worked, I lost over 50 pounds; I'm now within a healthy weight range for my height. I continue to drink protein shakes in place of chocolate milk, however, I usually opt for Slim Fast over Special K. They are virtually identical in ingredients and nutrition, yet Slim Fast can be found for a significantly less price. I recently found them at Big Lots, six bottles for $4.--even though they were sealed like all the others--had soured. Obviously something must have gone wrong at the factory.

product_title: Whey Low Type D Granules, 1 lb.
review_headline: Barry Farm's Product is not the same as Vivilac Whey Low
review_body:
I read your information about Whey Low being a useless and fraudulent product, but I have a few more questions before I write it off. My experience is only with Vivilac's Whey Low product, so that is what I will discuss:

You say that it is all absorbed as sucrose, lactose and fructose, but the site disputes this. I called the company and read a lot of the University of Maryland research on it and in my opinion, the binding of the sucrose and lactose seems to be a true statement. The information on the site related to the fructose also seems to point to a safe product.

I have been cooking for a diabetic for years and do not see the glucose spikes that would normally be the result of lactose, sucrose or fructose ingestion. Post prandial blood sugars stay within optimal levels... I don't know what to make of your vehement dislike for this product. It has been a godsend for me and I have been using it for at least three years. I am an RN and consider myself to have an extensive knowledge base when it comes to nutrition, endocrinology and the use of diet in integrative medicine.

Although the doctor has never heard of Whey Low, he continues to say to continue with whatever is going on, because the numbers and weight are consistently great. Oral medication for Type 2 Diabetes has now been discontinued... What can I say?

I have asked Whey Low to respond to statements, such as the ones found here, and they can only say that they are obviously not the statements of a a biologist... They wish you would contact them so that they can supply you with the necessary research data for a more informed perspective on the product.

Though not an expert on every aspect of nutrition, Dr. Oz's only objection was the high cost. (If you Google his site, he does have a brief statement related to Whey Low use by diabetics. For the record, I do not agree with his lower cost suggestion!)

What do you think? Is it possible that youare dissing a very useful dietary tool, or do you stand firm on your statements? I do realize that we should take the position to stop trying to find magic products that makes sweets possible - and resign ourselves to treats only now and then, this is easy for me to do, but this is not always possible to convey to the patient... I am faced with a loved one who will resort to Pepperidge Farm cookies if I do not have a good tasting, whole wheat, low glycemic option available.

Please respond!!! Also please review the Vivilac Company's data on Whey Low... really, you might be mistaken on this - or it could be me and Dr. Oz... either way, I need to know! Someone's life might depend on it.

review_body: I won't say it's the absolute best hot sauce, but if you're serious about hot sauces, and you haven't tried Sriracha, you need to add this sauce to your collection now.  What I like most about this sauce is it tastes like my homemade sauce.  I can tell just by the way it tastes and smells that they use the same high quality ingredients that I use when making my sauce.  One whiff takes me back to picking jalapeños out of my garden.  It's delicious blend of peppers, garlic, salt, and just the right amount of vinegar.  This sauce is thick.  This is not some red, runny liquid that you add to your food for heat.  This sauce is more like a thin paste.  I add it to ramen noodles, sushi, and just about anything else you would add hot sauce to, but since it's more like a thin paste than a runny liquid, it really sticks to the food.  It's hard to explain just how good this sauce is.  You have to try it for yourself to see what all the fuss is about.

review_body:
(See update below) Original review October, 2012: TWO STARS- I'm not one to rate things harshly, but I have to say I was more than a little annoyed with the K-Cup Storage Drawer! The metal tracks beneath the drawer do not line up properly, so it scuffs and silver, metal flecks collect on my counter top and the herky jerky movements to get the drawer in and out are super annoying. I'm hoping the seller will be willing to give a refund... or just send a drawer that isn't warped and actually SLIDES.

UPDATE 11-24-12: FOUR STARS- Seller read my review and promptly sent a replacement! The new drawer doesn't get stuck like the first one did, but if I was going to suggest a change to the design, I would say just leave the metal guides off the bottom. The housing for the drawer is really enough to hold it in place and the skinny rails under the drawer and on the bottom of the housing kind of rub together and it's friction that doesn't really need to be there, even when it's working properly. I'm happy with the drawer because I like that it doesn't take up MORE of my counter space to organize my K-cups. Also, the Ekobrews are great! My son is enjoying his favorite blend of coffee in the reusable K-cups. I love putting my favorite Teavana blend (Sakura Allure) in the Ekobrews. Surprisingly good! Get it! review_body:
I've learned that agricultural products vary from year to year - that's nature. I am a first time purchaser of these peanuts and I'm VERY impressed. I'd never used raw peanuts before, so will have some fun playing with them and making up recipes. So far, I've spread a single layer on a cookie sheet (actually a half-sheet baker's pan, which has sides), sprinkled them with sea salt, cayenne and garlic powders, then roasted them dry at 350 degrees for about 15-20 minutes. Then I tossed them with about a half teaspoon, maybe a bit more, of olive oil, and put them back in the oven for about 5 minutes.

YUMMY! I hope to figure out how to keep the seasonings better attached to the nuts without adding lots of oil, but for a first try, I'm very pleased. Looking forward to making my own peanut butter, too.

review_body:
I love pickles and I love turkey. But like the beef trifle in [[ASIN:B001KWTEHC Friends]], sometimes favorite flavors are not complementary. At least the ingredients here are all natural: cooked turkey gizzards, water, vinegar, salt and flavoring. Better still, the manufacturer calls this delicacy the \\"Gizzard Of Ahhhh's\\"! 'Nuf said.

Just remember, Ben Franklin called the turkey the noblest of birds, and surely he would question such treatment of the would-be national symbol. Gobble, Gobble.

>> For in Truth the Turkey is in Comparison a much more respectable Bird, and withal a true original Native of America... He is besides, though a little vain & silly, a Bird of Courage, and would not hesitate to attack a Grenadier of the British Guards who should presume to invade his Farm Yard with a red Coat on. <<

--letter from Ben Franklin to his daughter, January 26, 1784

product_title: Arrowroot Starch/Flour
review_headline: Helpful flour for those with eating restrictions
review_body:
Because I have so many MD- and test-diagnosed food allergies, I REALLY have to rely on alternate flours. Arrowroot is a great flour to add to a flour mixture because it has a couple of good properties:

1) It adds "hold" if you aren't able to have eggs in a recipe. It's good to add to a mixture of rice flours, for example, which do not hold together well on their own.

2) It can also be used as a thickener in lieu of cornstarch.

On the flip side, arrowroot has a very strong flavor, so I would not personally use it as the only flour in a recipe (unless using it as a minor ingredient, such as a cornstarch thickener substitute).

As a helpful tip, often you will see the term "arrowroot powder" in recipes. "Arrowroot flour" is interchangeable with this term.

product_title: Seitenbacher Vegetarian Vegetable Broth and Seasoning, 5-Ounce Cans (Pack of 6)
review_body:
I was looking for a delicious, yet healthful vegan vegetable broth powder and came across this brand. I did my research online and almost every site had favorable reviews for this product. Reading some of the other reviews for other brands (*cough, Vogue, **) I found them suspicious (always need to be careful with reviews, since companies hire people to write positive reviews). I was torn between buying this product or Rapunzel... I was not familiar with this brand, but was familiar with Rapunzel because I bought it in the past at a local Whole Foods and thought it was adequate but did not like the fact that the cubes contained so much palm oil (took forever for a cube to dissolve into boiling water). I am in no means a crunchy granola vegan and think that I am pretty discerning when it comes to taste.

I followed the directions of this product and dissolved 1 teaspoon into 1 cup boiling water.
*Pros* The result was a fine tasting broth... some of the yeast extract did not fully dissolve into the solution (I stirred quite a bit) but the broth was good nonetheless... surprisingly, the broth was not as salty as I thought...
Additionally, you can see all the bits and pieces of the herbs that this product contains.
*Cons* The container is a bit flimsy - it was hard to pull off the inner aluminum foil. If not careful you will have vegetable powder all over yourself. This may be trivial, but the packaging is very outdated. It's 2012 and the company can surely hire a graphic designer that can produce better packaging design than what they have now...

While I was researching, it seemed as though a fair amount of people make their own vegan vegetable powder. Almost all recipes use nutritional yeast as its base, but differ on the rest of the ingredients (for instance, once used powder versions of many ingredients, while another recipe basically took whole vegetables chopped up, cubed, and dehydrated and food processed into powder form).

I prefer powder broth over cubes - it's a lot more convenient, and you have better control and adjust the strength of your broth. With this said, the broth does in some way feel like it is missing something... I might purchase the Rapunzel powder to see how good that product is. I predict that I might get tired of this broth (considering Amazon sells it to you in a pack of 6) it isn't a bad idea to have a back-up brand to change up the flavor. The Rapunzel powder however has more salt, and seems to have less vegetable ingredients (I like the fact that this brand has a lot of vegetable ingredients, and some that are not common in the U.S., like lovage). What Rapunzel has going for it is that it is organic, while this is just \\"all natural\\" (which is fine).

Buy all your vegan broth products on Amazon - you will get an amazing price. I can't find any of these products at a normal supermarket, and Whole Foods charges an arm and a leg for these things. Even with many new Trader Joe's that just opened up in NYC giving Whole Foods competition and a run for its money, TJ just doesn't have the wide variety of niche products that Whole Foods has.

Update**: This product tastes BETTER than the Rapunzel vegetable broth powder (I have both). Using the recommended directions for both products, Seitenbacher has a deeper, more complex flavor whereas Rapunzel's tastes very salty (salt is the #1 ingredient in Rapunzel). If you want flavor, go for Seitenbacher - if you are obsessed about everything being organic, then go for Rapunzel.rm).

product_title: QUEEN ANNE Cordial Blueberries 5.6 OZ Box. Pack of 2 Boxes.
review_headline: Fun to eat but very sweet!
review_body:
Queen Anne Cordial Blueberries are a recent variation on the more familiar cordial cherries sold in drugstores and grocery stores. Each chocolate candy contains a good-sized blueberry swimming in the liquid filling instead of a cherry.

I have come to prefer the dark chocolate cherry cordials much more than the milk chocolate ones but these blueberry cordials are only available in milk chocolate so they are definitely very sweet! They are best with a glass of milk or a cup of coffee or tea to go with them. I enjoy the combination of the blueberry and chocolate and the liquid filling is fun to eat. Children also like these if you are willing to share but the drips can be messy for the youngest ones.

If you have never read about how they get the liquid center into the candy, it is quite interesting. When they are made, the filling is solid and it becomes liquid over time because of the invertase, an enzyme that changes the sucrose into glucose and fructose. Bees also use invertase to make honey from nectar.

The 5.6 ounce (159 gram) box contains ten candies, each with 60 calories. They are packed in two sealed trays which will help prevent you from eating all ten cordials at once. I was worried by the \\"artificial flavored\\" label but it apparently refers to vanillin with the blueberry flavor being natural.

Ingredients: Sugar, milk chocolate (sugar, cocoa butter, milk, chocolate, soya lecithin, PGPR, and vanillin), blueberries (blueberries, high fructose corn syrup, glycerol, citric acid, calcium lactate, potassium sorbate, sodium benzoate, natural blueberry flavor, pectin methyl esterase), corn syrup, dark coating (sugar, partially hydrogenated soybean and cottonseed oils) cocoa, chocolate, soya lecithin), invertase, artificial flavor.

product_title: Kinder Happy Hippo - Cocoa, CASE, 10x(20.7g x 5)
review_body:
I tried these little hippos for the first time while on a trip to Germany and kicked myself for not bringing boxes of them home for gifts. Despite the cute little hippo design of the treat itself, this is not chocolate for the palate of little kiddies. This is not to say that the kids won't love them, because they absolutely will, but this is the kind of chocolate you savor with each bite. So buy the kiddos a Hershey bar and save this for yourself when you want to treat yourself to something special or just need comfort chocolate.

The only disappointment was receiving these with an expiration date that gave me about a month to either eat them or give them away as gifts. I bought an entire case (10 boxes of five hippos) and had hoped to give them away gradually over a few months time for birthdays or special ocassions...if I didn't eat them all myself, anyway. I know that they don't have artificial colors, preservatives or hydrogenated fats, so they have a shorter shelflife, but since I still had two months shelflife on the packages I did bring back from Germany, I just assumed I'd get product with at least a couple of months to go. I'm eating one as I write this, and its very delicious though outdated, but I'm still disappointed because gifting now includes having to explain that even though the expiration date has gone by, they're still awesome. Awkward. Considering that each one of these little suckers has 119 calories, at this point, I'm really trying to control the urge to just eat through the hippos I have left so as not to waste them. :o) Treadmill, here I come!

review_body: I have tried a number of the Kind bars at this point because I have basically fallen in love with their line of products. It started with a Cranberry Almond one from Starbucks and since then, I have started buying several boxes every month. I don't like dark chocolate very much but thought I would give the Peanut Butter Dark Chocolate bar a try this time around.  I'm glad I did! Delicious and not at all bitter like I expected. Overall though, I like the Cranberry Almond the best and repeatedly go back to it as a staple for those times I skipped breakfast, need a snack, I'm on the road, etc. The Madagascar Vanilla is very good as is the Pomegranate Blueberry. Not so thrilled with the Mango and Apricot versions.  I've shopped around locally and online and Amazon seems to be the best place to buy them in terms of price, especially if you put them on Subscription. Kind's line of Grains is also good... The Maple Walnut is perfect heated in the microwave like oatmeal.  Strong excellent flavor and loaded with healthy grains, nuts, etc. Overall, I have been very pleased with Kind and will continue to buy their products as long as they remain available.

product_title: Francesco Rinaldi Hearty Tomato Basil Pasta Sauce
review_headline: At least as good as Ragu, and a real bargain
review_body:
This us not the most flavorful spaghetti sauce although it seems at least as good to me as the case lots of Ragu that I've been buying from Amazon. If you want the top of the line in terms of flavor, then you're also going to be paying top of the line prices--at least twice what this sauce costs. And what really distinguishes this sauce is its low price. It's a terrific bargain.

I don't actually try to get a complete spaghetti sauce when I buy these products, I just want to find a good base to which I can add other ingredients. And this serves very well in that role. It is an excellent base. To this, I typically add: pitted black olives, canned mushroom pieces, sautéed garlic and onion, strained diced tomstoes for body (I prefer the fire-roasted ones), and either sliced Polish sausage or sautéed ground beef. Throw the whole concoction into a slow cooker for five hours, and it's pretty good.

These are just suggestions. The beauty of sauces like this is that you can add whatever in your pantry seems suitable for a spaghetti sauce. As I said, it's a great base. Anything too flavorful might just get in the way, and it would just cost too much besides.
