product_title: Plum Organics Baby Food, Sweet Potato, Corn & Apple, 4.22 Ounce Pouches (Pack of 24)
review_headline: Our Son Loves Them, Very Convenient
review_body: We love these baby food things in a little pouch. Sooooo much easier to feed to a baby or toddler on the go. Our son loves sucking the mish mash out and we are pleased that it is both organic and healthy with nothing added. He'll eat the sweet potato and other veggie pouches when he is more hungry, but probably because of the sweetness of fruit, he far prefers the fruit mish mashes to the veggie ones. For smaller children, not good to let them handle it themselves, because they love to squeeze it, which gets things everywhere. But older ones can feed to themselves. I like the 3 oz size rather than the bigger one like this (4 oz) because it assures that he will eat all or most of it in one sitting rather than having to save some for later. They only keep for 24 hours after opening and need to be refrigerated if not eaten, but then he doesn't like them cold, so they have to be warmed up a bit in warm water to reuse, so a bit of a hassle. You can also take the 3 oz size on airplanes without having to have it tested for explosives - not the case with the bigger 4 oz pouches. I also like that it is BPA free. If your little one likes them, ordering in bulk and with subscribe and save makes them much cheaper than at the store.

product_title: Kraft Macaroni & Cheese Topping, 3-Ounce Cans (Pack of 6)
review_headline: There's DEFINITELY Something Cheesy About THIS Product!
review_body: It started when my niece was five years old and the only way she would eat her sweet potatoes was with \\"shaky cheese\\" on them.  That's all she would eat whenever she was out with the family - sweet potatoes with THIS shaky cheese on them.  Every extended-family meal, this container was on the table.    Fast forward ten years and MY five year old is sitting with his fifteen year old cousin...he doesn't want to eat cauliflower (although he loves broccoli, huh)...she reaches over, with cheese can in hand, and shakes the orange powder onto the previously snow white vegetables...    and he loves it!    From that day forward there's been at least one can, if not two or three cans, in our refrigerator. We use it on vegetables, on onion rings, eggs, macaroni/pasta, pizza, and anything else he can think of.  So, as you can see, losing the availability of this product was pretty traumatic for him!  I searched all over the area and finally found two cans, so I GRABBED them!  LOL!     When those cans were gone (about three months later), I could find no more! I ended-up buying boxes of mac & cheese  - just for the cheese! You can imagine how THRILLED I was to find the cheese here on Amazon. On AMAZON!  Go figure!    I don't care, I would've bought the cheese from the little boy down the street - that's how much my son LOVES this cheese - and if HE loves it, so do I!

product_title: Xylitol Sweetener. Sweet Matters. 100% Xylitol Sugar Substitute. 1LB Bag
review_body: I have tried to stay off of sugar and white refined things for years but giving up the occasional sweet delights was hard.  This amazing \\"smart sugar\\" has changed my life and brought better health and freedom.  Not only have I been able to stabilize my blood sugar which is critical for my weight control and all disease for that matter as Jorge Crews so succinctly presented in his best seller, The Belly Fat Cure, but I have found that substituting Sweet Matters xylitol crystals for sugar in all recipes has completely stopped newly developing joint pain.  Since xylitol, unlike sugar, does not stimulate my pancreas to release insulin and is alkalizing in my system instead of acid producing like sugar,it has been a huge factor in keeping the inflammatory process at bay in my body. Oh yes, this smart sugar is huge in Europe and been the healthy alternative for years. Not only is it not bad for me but it has many health giving benefits. Got to love it!!!

product_title: Reese Quartered Artichoke Hearts
review_headline: Had to downgrade my original review because of declining quality.
review_body:
These artichoke hearts have a nice flavor and are a pretty good value, but there are some very tough leaves in every can. Like the kind you really would rather not try to chew and swallow. I use these artichokes for everyday dinners, but would not serve them to guests.

June 2012 Update:

Over the long span of time that I had these artichoke hearts set up for auto-shipments, the quality continued to decline. The last shipment I received contained product so tough that it was literally inedible. Imagine trying to chew thinly sliced bamboo and you'll get the idea. My husband asked me not to serve them again, and I threw away what remained of the case.

So I've cancelled my subscription to the Reese Artichoke Hearts and lowered my rating to one star. Food that can't actually be eaten isn't a bargain at any price.

product_title: Arizona Green Tea ()
review_body: I've had lots of hot and iced teas, and this is one of my favorite teas.  I prefer iced tea and this is really good for iced tea.  It comes in regular tea bags, but can easily make iced tea by using a few of the bags in hot water, and then once cooled adding with 2 quarts of water.  Arizona did a great job of making a good blend.  I would also recommend trying the AriZona Green Tea with Pomegranate and Acai.

product_title: Betty Crocker Gluten Free Brownie Mix, 16-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6)
review_body:
At first when I saw this in the grocery store, I wasn't sure it would be a good idea. But since I have been recently diagnosed with gluten intolerance and I also LOVE brownies, I decided I would give it a try.

I WAS NOT DISAPPOINTED!!

I followed the directions to the T but also added in some chocolate chunks (about half a bags worth - I LOVE chocolate too!! and some Madegascar vanilla bean paste about 1/4 tsp) and I made this mix in a mini cup cake tray that had about 24 mini cupcakes in it. The entire batter made the 24 mini cupcakes.

The texture was on point - it was moist, tender, decadent and the small mini cupcake servings were just the right portion sizes - two mini cupcake were enough to sate my sweet cravings. And the remaining brownies freeze well.

Betty Crocker has done an awesome job.

I like to boil up a few new potatoes and dice them into the soup while it is simmering. Guess I just like a tad more potato. This soup, as others have stated is a great base for any addins that you would like! Experiment with it and come up with your families favorite mix. My major complaint and what keeps me from giving this 5 stars is the outrageously expensive costs of shipping. Each box weighs .45 ounces so all 32 boxes weighed 14.4 oz.  The cost of the boxes was $79.92. That's quite reasonable and a good buy. review_headline: Best bread mix ever! Sweet and delicious.
review_body: I didn't order it from Amazon directly, but I get it at my local Wegmans, and it tastes great! Just put the three ingredients in the bread machine, walk away, and three hours later, taste the sweetness and lightness of the bread. Still my favorite bread mix. Hard to find! Make sure you use room temperature water, or else it will not rise correctly!

product_title: GoPicnic GoEnergy,  Hummus & Crackers, Ready-to-Eat Meals (Pack of 4)
review_body: I liked this snack, and it's definitely a better choice than a Snackables or other processed foods on the market.  However, it's not as healthy as I would normally eat.  This package includes hummus, crackers, dried fruit, edamame, and Almond Roca.    The hummus was actually quite good.  I make my own hummus, because store bought is usually not very good.  This was a pleasant surprise, and had a nice cumin flavor.  I didn't like the package the hummus was in...it's a squeeze pack which is rather messy when you open it, and difficult to get all the hummus out.  I would have rather seen a dipping type container.    The crackers are mostly white flour (there is some whole wheat flour, but it's 3rd on the ingredients list).  They do contain honey instead of processed sugar.  They are tasty, but very crumbly.  The problem with this is that when I bit into them, they broke apart.  If I hadn't been eating over a plate, I would have ended up with hummus in my lap.    The dried fruit was a mix of cranberries & pineapple.  There is added sugar in this, and I ate very little because they added sulphur dioxide, which I avoid since I'm allergic to sulpha drugs.  Because of this I always eat organic dried fruit.    I only tried one of the Edamames.  I was pregnant when I tried this, and since this is not organic I have to assume the soy is genetically modified.  GMO soy is linked to peanut allergies in children (there is great info about this in several books, including this one: [[ASIN:0767930711 The Unhealthy Truth: How Our Food Is Making Us Sick - And What We Can Do About It]]).  For this reason, I avoided non-organic soy when I was pregnant, and also won't let my 3 year old eat it.  My husband ended up eating most of the Edamame.  It was okay, but a bit dry and not very tasty.    The snack finishes up with Almond Roca, which isn't my favorite candy but is okay.  There is also a moist towelette included to help clean up.    The bottom line:  I tend to eat healthier than this,and would rather make organic hummus and take along some veggies & whole wheat crackers to snack on.  However, if you tend to eat junk food if you don't have a healthy snack available, this may be a great product for you.  It does not contain trans fats, high fructose corn syrup, or MSG, so it's better than most packaged foods on the market.

product_title: Don Enrique Habanero, 0.25-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12)
review_body:
I like spicy food. What can I say? I had heard that habanero chile was pretty spicy and added some real heat to any food. So, when I found this product in my local grocery store, I could not resist!

Hot? As Dizzy Dean used to say, \\"You ain't just a woofin'.\\" The first time I used it, I started off sautéing scallions and teeny flakes of the dry pepper from the habanero chile package. Then, cracked and egg and cooked it over the onion and habanero. In the process, I got a little of the chile on my face a couple inches below one of my eyes. A slow burn for the next ten or so minutes. The egg? After putting some cheese on top to add a nice meltiness, I ate the end result. And a slow heat began to build, not ending for the next several minutes. And all I could think was that I had just used a few flakes that I loosened from the dried peppers with a knife. I had originally thought that there was too little habanero to taste. Wrong!

Anyhow, I have used this a number of times since; I use something to prevent any residue from the habanero getting on my hands and, thence, elsewhere. I have added a wee bit more habanero to dishes than my first experiment, and the end result is that much hotter.

So, if you are interested in heat in your food, here it is!

product_title: Royal Gelatin Assorted Red Gelatin Mix (Cherry, Raspberry, Strawberry), 24-Ounce Packages (Pack of 12)
review_headline: Good Value For Home Gelatin Desserts/Snacks
review_body:
This bundle is a good value for the home consumer if you are not frightened away by the package size. Each bag contains 24 oz. of gelatin mix, and, if you read the directions, makes a bit over a gallon of prepared gelatin. That is too much, at one time, for the average family (unless you are having a party!)
If you keep the unused portion in a zip-lock bag, you should have no problem storing the left-over gelatin mix.
Here is the recipe I use for home preparation:
Place 3/4 cup of the gelatin mix in a large bowl (at least 1 1/2 quart size.)
Add 2 cups boiling water (allow the water to come to a full boil.)
Stir until the gelatin is completely dissolved (about 2 minutes.)
Add 12 large ice cubes and stir until all the ice has melted.
Refrigerate until firm. (Typically 3 - 4 hours)
(Alternately, you can stir in 1 1/4 cups cold water in place of ice cubes, but it will take longer for the gelatin to set.)
This recipe will make about a quart of prepared gelatin.

product_title: Barney Butter Almond Butter
review_body:
Update, August 2012: They've improved both the packaging and the contents since my last review. I don't notice the \\"grittiness\\" much at all, nor does it taste over-toasted, as I'd mentioned in my prior review. The packaging has an updated design and all the packets have a proper tearing point. Definitely recommended! Bumping this from 4 to 5 stars.

-------
These are higher protein, lower sugar, and cheaper than energy bars, and even more portable. They're a great way to stave off hunger, gluten-free. I keep one or two in my bag along with a Larabar or two, but this is the healthier & more economical option. The taste is a little \\"overcooked\\" to my taste - a deeply roasted flavor - so it may not appeal to all kids, but I'm sure many kids would like it. It's great to squeeze onto an apple as you eat it, or just eat it out of the packet.

It does require some kneading before you open the packet - just squish it back and forth for a minute - because it separates like any natural nut butter would. There is a tiny bit of grittiness to the texture, but not really noticeable if you mix it up first. I'd rather have a little grittiness than a ton of shortening added to make it smooth.

The other catch is not all the packets are notched properly, making them near impossible to open without scissors. There is a simple solution - I just take scissors and go through each new box, making a tiny nick on any packet where the cut doesn't go through both layers. It only takes a minute to do the whole box, and then they're all ready to go.

It is worth noting that Maltitol (which can cause \\"gastric distress\\" in some people) is used as one of the sweeteners.

Recommended!

CFH

review_headline: Great with salmon, on sandwiches, and in soups!
review_body: This is my favorite spice to put on fresh salmon. Back in 2004, we took a trip to the Oregon coast, and one night I grilled salmon fillets with this Cajun Creole seasoning, some garlic, Tillamook butter, salt, pepper, and just a tiny bit of lemon. We served it with pine nut cous-cous, grilled vegetables, and northern Italian bread . . .  And my family still talks about the salmon to this day! Every summer they ask me to make it again - in fact, they have even offered to drive two hours to the coast to buy fresh salmon - if only I will agree to cook it.      I also like to sprinkle this on sandwiches when I get tired of the same old thing. I usually put it together with oven-roasted turkey, provolone, lettuce, tomato, red onion, basil, oil, and a dash of vinaigrette. I've used Cajun Creole a few times for various soups, too. You would be surprised what it can do for homemade chicken soup (or waterhole soup for that matter).

product_title: Twinings Prince of Wales Tea
review_body:
As always, the sale went flawlessly and the item was delivered in perfect condition. The little tins are just gorgeous. Very nice way to keep your loose leaf fresh. The lid can be a little tough to open at first, but once you open and close it a few times, it becomes easier.

The reason I deducted two stars was the taste. My first introduction to Earl Grey was from a tin of East India Company's Earl Grey. Just a little tin I picked up from a local T.J. Maxx one day. Divine flavor. Very robust and delicious paired with milk. I had previously had a cup of Twinnings (made with one of those tea bags you find at the local grocery store) and thought the taste was very similar, however, what came in this tin was not. Maybe the recipe has changed or I received a bad batch. Not sure...but the taste is just watered down beyond belief. When paired with milk, all I can taste is the milk. I tried steeping longer (only to get a very nasty astringent taste) and even tried steeping with twice the amount I normally use...but this didn't work b/c though the flavor was more pronounced, it still had this strange mildness to it that lacked the bite of what I come to expect from Earl Grey tea.

Pity. Now I have 6 tins of tea that I have no idea what to do with as all my friends are coffee drinkers. LoL. That will teach me to buy an untested product in bulk. I've since purchased some Republic of Tea Earl Greyer, and I am much more satisifed with the overall quality and flavor ot it than the Twinnings.

product_title: Folgers Simply Smooth Ground Coffee, 23 Ounce Tubs (Pack of 3)
review_body:
I have to say, Folgers Simply Smooth has been the ideal coffee for me. For starters, it does seem to be far easier on my stomach; many other coffees leave my stomach growling/turning, and other undesireable effects. For many, its not the caffeine that causes upset stomachs, but rather just many of the other irritants associated with coffee. For those that don't have those issues, kudos, you can probably buy similar coffee a lot cheaper.

As for the taste, I personally think its great. Its not \\"bold\\", but just right. It doesn't have high hints of bitterness, which I personally associate with bad coffee, others may think is good. I'd say if you're looking for a taste comparison, its close to McDonalds. Then again, I prefer my coffee on the sweet side, and this I don't have to drown out with creamer, but its also not as watery tasting as many of the \\"mild\\" brands. Again, just right for my tastes. I personally recommend combining it with International Delight's Carmel Macchiato, it really tastes like a coffee house drink, with a fraction of the calories and cost.

Now the one downside is the cost/availability. Often, this is double the cost of the regular brew. They also tend to only stock the smaller bins in many retail stores. So, its up to you if its worth the cost. For me, it is, but lately they jacked the price up almost astronomical on all coffees in my area, forcing me to go with the cheapest brands, and here I type morning my beloved coffee while my stomach yells at me.

So, if you're like me, and have any sort of stomach issues associated with coffee, but love coffee, this is probably the product for you. If you're merely looking for a mild coffee, this one has a great taste, better than most mild blends, but the cost probably isn't justified. Keep in mind, this is not decaffinated, they sell a version of simply smooth that is, but I personally like the caffeine to get me going, which is not what upsets my stomach.

product_title: Douwe Egberts Excellent Aroma Ground Coffee, 8.8-Ounce Packages (Pack of 4)
review_body: This is the best coffee for our french press we've ever had, bar none. Very smooth taste, no bitter after taste at all. We've been through many types of coffee, from Lavazza Qualita Rossa to Altura Organic, to Peet's and Diedrich, and the infamous Starbucks and this is on the first, second, and third place, maybe Lavazza comes fourth. We usually drink Nespresso, it's fast to make and has great taste, but on a weekend I would have nothing less than a cup of this Douwe Egberts Excellent Aroma. I have not tried the other Douwe Egberts types, but I have the feeling that this will be THE ONE.   Back in the pre-Nespresso and pre-Douwe Egberts days we enjoyed Diedrich's espresso blend for espresso and Peet's for french press. No going back, though, for either of them. I sure hope that the quality will not decline, I would hate to go back to searching for the holy grail of coffee for the french press... We keep it in the freezer, then straight from the freezer into the french press, temper the grounds then pour the hot water. Two minutes, then, aaahhh, heaven.   When we started buying it, Amazon did not carry the whole bean kind, I think I'll try that as well, even if we had no problems with the ground coffee, it was always fresh and well packed.

product_title: Nabisco Oreo Sandwich Cookies Double Stuf Chocolate - 12 Pack
review_body:
Once there was the Hydrox cookie, way back in 1908. In 1912, the Oreo cookie debuts, and it was downhill for Hydrox from there. The Oreo cookie remained the same until the mid-1970s, when someone realized that some people ate the Oreo cookie in a way that might make a variation of the cookie sell more to some customers.

Some people eat the cookie all at once. Other people eat the cookie dipped in milk, or as part of another food, such as ice cream. However, some people would twist the Oreo cookie apart and then put the icing portions together and eat the reformed cookie. The Double Stuff Chocolate Creme Oreo was born.

According to Kraft, more than 450 billion Oreos were sold in the first 90 years of Oreo's existence. Kraft claims, and with 450 billion cookies sold I tend to agree, that the Oreo cookie is the best selling cookie in the world. The reason for this popularity is the flavor of the Oreo cookie. The chocolate flavor is sharp. The icing is smooth and sweet. The double stuff version of the Oreo cookie gives filling fans that much more of the creamy filling to go with their chocolate outsides.

There are numerous competitors in the cookie world. It is unlikely that anyone will unseat the yummy Oreo cookie any time soon, and the double stuff variation will help assure that Oreo cookies stay on top of the cookie heap. Enjoy!

I have also been known to use oat bran in place of bread crumbs when making things like meatloaf, salmon patties, etc. - much healthier! Also, they print an excellent recipe for oat bran muffins on the side of the box - the only one I've found that doesn't call for any wheat flour.

review_body:
I really do like my Senseo coffee maker. I, like others who have reviewed the Kona Pods here, was always searching for a better tasting coffee pod to use in the machine. I was excited to see that Kona now made pods and was also happy to see that they had a pod that was a '2 cup style'. I have not found it to be a huge deal to use 2 smaller '1 cup' size pods, but it sounded nice to be able to just put one large pod in the machine instead of 2 smaller one.

After reading some of the reviews here, I could not figure out what some of the reviewers meant by the Kona pods making different amount of coffee per cup each time or how the coffee could be strange and undrinkable. It just didn't make sense. Well, it still doesn't make sense, but it certainly happened with the coffee I made using the Kona pods also.

My results were overall poor and it was very disappointing as the Kona pods cost a lot more than Folgers or other pod brands that I can buy locally. The first thing I noticed was that the coffee in the 2 cup sized Kona pods is packed in much more tightly than in any other pod I have ever used in my Senseo. The instructions for the Kona pods say to wiggle the pods to break up the coffee before inserting into the machine. The Kona pods feel very hard when taken out of their package. I always wiggled and jiggled the pods for about 10 seconds before putting them in the Senseo. After my problems with the Kona pods, my husband decided that I was not 'wiggling' them enough. He promptly wiggled one to the point that it broke open. So, there is just so much that can be done to the pod before putting it in the machine.

The first thing that I noticed was that the amount of coffee brewed when using the Kona pod was quite a bit less than when using 2 smaller pods. That did not make much sense, but after several cups of Kona, it was obvious that there was never the amount of coffee coming out as before when using 2 small one cuppods. The best I can figure out is that the Kona pods themselves seem to 'hold' a lot more water. There is more water that remains in the pod itself after the brewing is done. The pod itself is heavier when I take it out to throw it away. So, I believe the reason that there is less actual coffee using Kona pods is that the pods themselves retain a lot more water and it cannot pass through into the coffee cup.

Then, as others have mentioned, there is the problem that happens to me about 1/2 the time when using the Kona pods. The problem is that for whatever reason, the water does not actually go through and penetrate the Kona pods during the brewing cycle. The 'coffee' that is supposed to be coming out of the spout is just water! This problem is one that I still cannot really figure out. The Kona pods are a little smaller in diameter than all the other pods I have tried. So, I guess that somehow the water has enough room to 'go around' the actual pod and come out of the spout without 'going through' the pod to brew coffee. I also wonder if the paper filter of the Kona pods is different than other pods and for some reason the Kona paper is more difficult for water to penetrate. I have tried wetting the Kona pod paper filter right before starting to brew the coffee thinking that perhaps it would help the water to penetrate the paper and pod. But, that has not worked for me.

So, it is back to regular more reasonably priced coffee pods for me. I have wasted too many expensive Kona pods trying to get a proper cup of coffee from them. Even when the Kona pods brew a cup of coffee, it is not as large of an amount of coffee as I get using other brands. So, adding the cost of the Kona pods to the fact that it brews a smaller amount of coffee equals a product that is way too expensive when it does actually work.

I have been reading of a product called an EcoPod. It is a refillable pod for these type of coffeemakers. Itmight be the next thing I try.

These crackers are particularly good to serve with a dip to guests. Of course, you can also treat yourself to this same delight! They taste wonderful with a garlic and herb cheese dip I sometimes use. If you want the same crackers that are a little bigger and easier for people to hold onto while they put some dip on the cracker, try the \\"big\\" version of Wheat Thins.

One small caveat: Eat these before any expiration date printed or stamped on the top of the box. You wouldn't want to eat stale crackers, now would you?

review_body: I was reluctant to try this out, because I've had so many terrible jarred pasta sauces and no one had reviewed this product yet, but my fears were quickly put to rest.  This is the BEST jarred pasta sauce I've ever had.  Actually, it's probably the best pasta sauce I've ever had prepared by someone else, period.  Only a super-fresh homemade sauce, made with wonderful ingredients (San Marzano tomatoes, roasted onions and garlic, etc.) can compete.  Considering that such a sauce really takes hours to make, all told, I'm thrilled to use this instead.  This flavor in particular is an excellent base to use for other sauces - it won't overpower the other ingredients you add, but it has such a fantastic flavor it can easily be used on its own.  One of my favorite things to do is use a half-a-jar of this sauce over organic prepared ravioli - it's a super-quick, somewhat healthy meal that tastes amazing.  The heat from the freshly boiled ravioli is sufficient to warm up the sauce, so there's no need to even cook the sauce separately - you just pour it on and you're done!    The jars are very nice, thick, reusable polypropylene (#5).  I use them to bring my lunch to work everyday - it's pretty surprising how nice they are - they are definitely not disposable junk.  There are some reports of an occasional jar arriving broken if this item is shipped via ground, which is honestly hard for me to imagine.  I use Amazon Prime, so mine arrive via two-day, and the packaging is always flawless.  To address this problem, Amazon had a \\"Pasta Lovers Gift Set\\" from this company with extra packaging, but it doesn't appear to show up in searches anymore.  It contained four flavors - Marinara, Arrabbiata, Tuscan Vodka, and Barely Bolognese, if I remember correctly.  All delicious - the Arrabbiata is fairly spicy, though.    Anyway, buy this sauce!  The more people buy it, the more wonderful flavors Amazon will presumably carry.  One final note - this is a GREAT DEAL for these sauces.  If youdon't believe me, take a look elsewhere on the web for this company's sauces - five bucks a jar is an absolute steal for an all-natural product of this top-notch quality.

product_title: Kellogg's Corn Pops, 19.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 4)
review_headline: An enjoyable breakfast cereal but not the very best health-wise
review_body:
Kellogg's Corn Pops breakfast cereal delivers a delicious and flavorful taste. It contains no cholesterol and it is low in calories and fat. The delicious taste and the nutritional value that it does have make this better for you than skipping breakfast. It is low in carbohydrates and it contains no cholesterol--hooray! It stays crunchy in milk, too! I enjoy the strong corn taste and the milk enhances the excellent flavor of the cereal. It is also certified kosher if that's important to you.

Unfortunately, there are some disappointments. The cereal is only average in terms of vitamin content, reaching at the very best 25% of your recommended daily intake of niacin, vitamins B6 and B12, riboflavin, thiamin and folic acid. It delivers only average value in the vitamin department. Corn Pops cannot be considered a substitute for a morning vitamin if you need one. Therefore I will take off one star to make this a four star review.

Kellogg's Corn Pops cereal is low in carbohydrates; and that is another positive quality. However, it does contain partially hydrogenated vegetable oil and this can convert in your body to trans fat. Be careful!

One more caveat: this product contains traces of soybeans and it is made with wheat. Ask your doctor before eating this cereal if you are unsure if your body can tolerate these ingredients. In addition, consult your doctor about your diet from time to time.

Overall, Kellogg's Corn Pops truly is a delicious breakfast cereal that does have some basic nutritional value. Nevertheless, Kellogg's Corn Pops cereal cannot be a substitute for a daily vitamin.

Aw heck, after all is said and done, I just can't help but love the taste of this cereal. It's really delicious and its' easy availability through the decades proves people like to eat it. Be like me and try some today!

product_title: El Sabroso Original Salsitas, Spicy Salsa Tortilla Rounds, 12-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12)
review_headline: THESE CHIPS HAVE MSG (Monosodium glutamate ) IN THEM!!!!!!!!!!!!!
review_body: Answer  Monosodium glutamate (MSG) is a flavor enhancer commonly added to Chinese food, canned vegetables, soups and processed meats. Although the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has classified MSG as a food ingredient that is \\"generally recognized as safe,\\" the use of MSG remains controversial.    MSG has been used as a food additive for decades. Over the years, the FDA has received many anecdotal reports of adverse reactions to foods containing MSG. But subsequent research found no definitive evidence of a link between MSG and the symptoms that some people described after eating food containing MSG. As a result, MSG is still added to some foods.    A comprehensive review of all available scientific data on glutamate safety sponsored by the FDA in 1995 reaffirmed the safety of MSG when consumed at levels typically used in cooking and food manufacturing. The report found no evidence to suggest that MSG contributes to any long-term health problems, such as Alzheimer's disease. But it did acknowledge that some people may have short-term reactions to MSG. These reactions -- known as MSG symptom complex -- may include:    Headache, sometimes called MSG headache   Flushing   Sweating   Sense of facial pressure or tightness   Numbness, tingling or burning in or around the mouth   Rapid, fluttering heartbeats (heart palpitations)   Chest pain   Shortness of breath   Symptoms are usually mild and don't require treatment. However, some people report more severe reactions. The only way to prevent a reaction is to avoid foods containing MSG. When MSG is added to food, the FDA requires that \\"monosodium glutamate\\" be listed on the label -- or on the menu, in restaurants. At that temp, the oil does not enter the food, saving you excess fat in the diet. It sears the food before it can be absorbed. Fried Chicken has the juices seared in. But remember, at that heat, breading can burn before the oil will smoke, so don't walk away.

The last 'perfect' is that this oil actually does for you what fish-oil does, but without a taste. It help raise your HDL and lower your LDL and that's good for the Ticker and Liver Did I mention that it doesn't smell or taste. The flavor is so subtle, its perfect in a vinegar-oil dressing. This is where it outshines olive-oil. You want to soften butter for dinner rools? Take some of this oil and warm it, and mix at 5 parts butter to 1 part warmed GSO. No one will even know its there.

Great value for price. Great performance for price. Great Health for price. So, why doesn't California, Ohio, and NY make oil from the left-over Grape seeds from their wine? Chile does. And the whole thing is cheaper than mid-quality Olive-oil, and better for you.

review_headline: A Whole New Kinda Sugar-Free "Nutritional Supplement" - From An Ancient Source
review_body:
I, like most Americans, am overweight. When I want a way to satisfy my sweet tooth, I can choose sugar or high-fructose corn syrup, or I can choose a sweetener which occurs in nature, and sweetens about 800 times as well as sugar - I think I'm going for the naturally-occurring one. Less calories in, fewer calories to burn off.
It is stevia, Sweetleaf, or Truvia. It doesn't break down in hot liquids, you can bake with it, put it on your cereal, or sweeten what you like.
If you are an intelligent person, you've gotta ask yourself - what's the catch? I had to find out. So I Googled, went to Ask.com, and WebMd. It was as I thought - bureaucrats and their studies were rather vague and inconclusive, but since no formal study has been done, it could be bad. After all, anecdotal evidence of centuries of the use of the stevia plant's sweetening properties - by older cultures than our own - it can't have any credibility, can it? (I was being facetious...) Anyway, stevia is NOT a food additive - FDA says no. So it is in that huge category of \\"dietary supplements\\". Read about stevia on your own, and take from this what you will.

product_title: Teavana Perfect Tea Maker, 16oz
review_headline: Makes great coffee or tea, but very difficult to clean
review_body: I picked up this Teavana brewer at a tag sale, it had never been used, and I had never heard of it. Since I love coffee and tea, and the directions said it could be used to brew either, I decided to give it a try.     PROS: It appears to be of a sturdy design with a durable look and feel that seems like it would last a long time.  The beverages brewed are very good. In fact, to give a bit more detail, the way this brews coffee is actually ideal according to good brewing procedure.  It allows you to combine the water with the grounds without the use of any paper filter and at a time-controlled interval. The resulting coffee is then released directly into your cup.  Because you get full extraction of the essential oils, the coffee this makes is very similar to a vacuum pot brew, very rich and tasty with not much bitterness. 5 stars on beverage quality.    CONS:  The chief complaint with this little brewer is that it does not come apart for cleaning. I really find this to be UNACCEPTABLE and because of this, even though it produces fantastic beverages, I have given it 2 stars overall.     The main problems with not being able to clean it are as follows:     (1) A search of the web will bring up other review sites, where you will see that many people have ended up having to throw their Teavana brewers away because of mold formation inside the mesh part in between the mesh filter and the stopper. A product like this should be able to be taken completely apart for cleaning. Having to throw away such an expensive product just because of mildew, even in spite of cleaning it, and especially when it is in good condition otherwise, is absolutely unacceptable, IMO.    (2) The amount of water necessary to clean the brewer each time you use it is wasteful, making it environmentally unfriendly.  Since there is no way to remove the mesh strainer, you have to really work hard to get in there and get the tea leaves or coffee grounds out of the strainer and it takes many rinses and washes to do this, which is a complete waste of water. I have tried using different types of small brushes and that has helped, but even then, a lot of water is required.     When the company makes a brewer that can come apart for cleaning, I'll be willing to try it and revise this review as necessary.

product_title: Economist
review_body:
\\"The Economist\\" is by far the best news magazine today, both for the information it provides and for the way it presents that information.

\\"The Economist\\" is able to provide startlingly in-depth and rigorous reports on both American and global news, and perhaps best of all, it avoids showing a bias or privileging any side. This is not to say that the magazine does not provide critical assessments of important issues; the commentary pieces are particularly thought-provoking and well-argued. However, the magazine manages to be critical of all sides equally, allowing for balanced yet engaging news reports.

Although this magazine is quite dense--there are few ads, and no filler articles--reading \\"The Economist\\" never becomes tedious. All reports utilize good economy of language, allowing the reader to quickly get to the heart of the issue. Even so, the writing is still extremely enjoyable and well-written. I keeping returning to \\"The Economist\\" not merely for the wealth of information it provides, but for the fact that reading it is actually pleasurable.

Ultimately, though the price of a year's subscription is not cheap, a subscription to \\"The Economist\\" is worth every penny--particularly since you won't have to spend money any other news magazine.

The manufacturer (the Gruma) company has been making this fine corn flour for over 50 years.

review_body: In a time when everything seems GMO or hybrid-ized to utterly unrecognizable, the ancient strain of wheat -- Spelt is a refreshing find in today's fast food world. product_title: Rishi Tea Organic Black Tea, Earl Grey Loose Tea, 3.3-Ounce Tin (Pack of 3)
review_headline: Not my favorite but pretty good
review_body:
I drink a lot of Earl Grey tea and have tried four or five brands over the years, Bigelow being my favorite. I've been trying this organic Rishi tea for two weeks now and have experimented with different amounts of tea to get the flavor right and have not been able to. It is just okay for me. This tea is advertised as a bold tea and I see that many reviewers agree but I do not. If I add too much tea to try to make it stronger it adversely affects the taste unlike other loose teas I use. Also, this tea requires 1 TBL of dry tea per 8oz of water; I need to use twice that amount for it not to be weak, whereas other loose teas I use only require 1 1/2 tsp. for the same strength, so this Rishi tea would be much more expensive to use regularly. I may prepare it occasionally just to have a change once in awhile.

The packaging is beautiful. It is packed in a very nice earthy looking tin and is slender and tall so fits in the cabinet nicely. The big plus with this tea is that it's organic.

product_title: Chef 5 Minute Meals Beef Stroganoff with Noodles (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Not impressive when compared to similiar products.
review_body:
This meal is fine for what it is, a self heating meal. There's some food, you pour the included salt water on the included heating element, toss the food on top, wait a few minutes, and presto you have a lukewarm meal.

The stroganoff noodles are very edible, perhaps even average, and the meat wasn't overly fatty. Surely it's better than cold canned food (or nothing) nothing in an emergency (which I why I picked it up, as part of a 72 hour kit), but I wouldn't buy one of these just because. Why? Because I've also tried [[ASIN:B0001WWQ22 La Briute Self Heating Meal, Meatballs and Spaghetti, 14 Ounce Meal (Pack of 6)]]. It was way better, please see my full review on the over there for the details.

This thing costs $4.50 a meal, well above the cost of a typical microwave meal so I really don't understand why you'd want to use it at the office. At room temperature the food also didn't get very hot (because it doesn't use a 2nd bag like the La Briute system), so I wouldn't rely on using this product outdoors either.

But overall this product does work, and the food is better than the last time I had an Army MRE ten years ago. I uploaded some product images so you can see what's in the box. I'd say go for it if you're stocking up on provisions, but pass if you're hungry and/or frugal.

product_title: Karen's Naturals Just Tomatoes, Just Peaches 1.2 Ounce Pouch (Packaging May Vary)
review_headline: Sort of like weird fizzy rocks. Expensive Fizzy Rocks
review_body:
Peaches are my favorite fruit, and after having wonderful experiences with the other \\"Just Tomatoes\\" products, I was looking forward to trying these. I expected something like the concentrated flavor of peaches in a tasty, very crunchy package.

Sadly,my expectations were not met. At all.

The package I had was not crunchy in the usual sense: the little cubes were tough to bite into, and little bits of cube stuck to your teeth. The cubes were barely sweet and had no discernable taste of peaches. After an initial handful, no one in our family would go near the things. I ended up throwing the remaining cubes into a batch of cupcake batter, figuring that it might add a bit of extra nutrition. It did that, but even better, the chocolate cupcakes have a mild taste of peach.

But there is no way I would buy these again as a subtle cupcake flavoring. I'll eat the strawberries and blueberries, and leave these peaches to find a nice home with someone else.

I used to be able to find it in grocery stores, but then wasn't able to for a long time. I'm excited that Amazon is carrying this now. It's a great value for the number of cups you can make!

product_title: Kraft  Classic Catalina Dressing, 16-Ounce Plastic Bottles (Pack of 6)
review_headline: New Kraft Catalina Dressing is TERRIBLE!!!
review_body: The New Kraft Catalina Dressing is TERRIBLE and Kraft knows it. There are not any positive comments on it anywhere on the internet including Kraft's own website. Everybody hates it! But Kraft seems insistent that they are going to shove this terrible new stuff down your throat!  The fact that they are sticking with it shows that it must be WAY cheaper to manufacture -and they are so arrogant - and think that they are so big-  that they can dictate to the consumer and not the other way around.

product_title: PowerBar Performance Energy Bar, 2.29 Ounce
review_headline: Decent taste and gives you a definate stamina boost.
review_body: As an athlete, I have used Power Bar products for years.  I have to say this is one of the better tasting Bars.  Has a definite strawberry flavor, without being too sweet.  If you haven't ever had a Power Bar, then you may be surprised at the texture.  These are not candy bars!  They provide a great energy boost when you don't have time for a full meal.  Excellent for slipping in your bike jersey pocket for eating on the road.  Highly recommended.

product_title: Foothill Farms Chili Seasoning (no MSG) Mix, 5.7-Ounce Units (Pack of 6)
review_body: This stuff in one package makes about 4 qts of chili - so I used only half a package.  Its a little pricey for 6 packages but they are so big that it makes it very economical.  The first time I used it, it is great!  I will buy again!

product_title: SF Signature Fondue Chocolate, White Chocolate, 32-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 4)
review_body:
Amazon should remove this item, since they ripped me off and costed me a huge deal of money. I needed this urgently, and placed my order using 2 day shipping. Amazon kept saying every day that my stuff would be delivered the following day.

LONG STORY SHORT = it never came! Amazon is a rip off

product_title: Glutino Gluten Free Pantry Favorite Sandwich Bread Mix
review_headline: Tastes almost the same as white!
review_body: I bought this on recommendation from a customer in the health food store. I was told to add a little extra oil if I baked it in the oven. This was awesome!! After tasting some of the bread that was as hard as a rock I was surprised to find this soft,moist and fluffy. It was delicious hot with butter. I will make this many times and try the raisen and cinnamon additions mentioned on the box.

product_title: Stride Forever Fruit Gum (12 - 14 Stick Packs)
review_body: This is a good gum to chew if you are looking to switch from sugared to sugarless gum. It's sweet, and doesn't have a strong aspartame taste, for being sugar-free. It doesn't last 'forever' like the commercials and 'Forever Fruit' name would lead you to believe, but the flavor lasts longer than a lot of sugarless gums, and it has a nice kick of flavor when you first bite in. Everyone in my family likes this flavor of Stride.     Don't confuse this with the darker-but-similar-colored-packaging 'Mandarin' flavor.

product_title: El Sabroso Jalapenitos, Jalapeno Peppers and Cheese Tortilla Chips, 1.5-Ounce Packages (Pack of 60)
review_body: Great taste,great snack; A very nice compliment to the Salsitas and Guaca chips in the 1.5 oz. package. All vend well, and the new Jalapenitos are doing very well. Thanks much from 'Pappy's Vending', and we are looking forward to the next new flavor in 1.5 oz. packaging.

product_title: Bonnie's Country Classic Mustard BBQ Sauce
review_body: I bought a jar of Bonnie's Country Classic Mustard BBQ sauce after sampling it at a local food fair called Pride of Dakota. Later that week, I used it on ribs in the slow cooker and it was absolutely delicious. I love mustard flavored things, so naturally, I love this BBQ sauce, although the mustard taste is very subtle. Even my husband loves it and he isn't usually a mustard fan. It's just the right mix of tangy, smokey, and sweet. We love it.

product_title: Hain Pure Snax Popped Corn Mini Cakes, Caramel, 3.5-Ounce Bags (Pack of 12)
review_body: I have been consuming these for years, & love them because they are very satisfying but also low fat. Unfortunately, my local Whole Foods stopped carrying them. I am SO GLAD that I can subscribe to them via Amazon - you've saved me!

product_title: Bare Fruit Organic Dried Fuji Apple Chips, 2.6-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 24)
review_body: Measure up very well to the manufacturer claims - it's chewy, crunchy and sweet... there're four apples in a pack and it lasts me less than an hour - if my wife wouldn't stop me - I would go through 5 packs a day... and my argument that it's healthy still doesn't seem to help me...

product_title: Planters Cashews, 1-Ounce Packages (Pack of 48)
review_body: I love nuts, and I also love to eat ...but as we all know one of the most important factors in not being fat (yes I said it; FAT) is portion control. A 1-oz bag is a great snack and cashews are full of good fat and oils (the kind of fat you need to not be fat ...just not too much good fat) so it works well all around.

product_title: Haribo Gummi Candy
review_body: I haven't lived in Brooklyn for over 6 years, but when I did, these were a staple of girls' weekends.  There's nothing quite like Haribo frogs.  I haven't ever seen them anywhere I've lived since, although I'm in Detroit now and we have 7-11 which is where I always got them in B'klyn.

product_title: Planters Salted Peanuts, 1-Ounce Units (Pack of 72)
review_body: i ordered these in august and the expiration date on them was july 8, 2008.  yuck!

product_title: Taylors of Harrogate Yorkshire Gold
review_body:
I ordered this tea for my wife, who is English; she enjoys a good
cup of strong tea. I have often visited web sites specializing in
British goods, particularly food, and have found that AMAZON typically
will have the lowest available price.

product_title: Bare Fruit Organic Dried Mangos, 2.6-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 24)
review_body: I love Bare Fruits dried cherries, my favorite snack.  Full of love and hope, I ordered the dried mangoes and was sorely disappointed.  They are foul to the taste, and smell like froo-froo soap chips.  I regret buying a whole box, but fortunately now have Xmas gifts for people I don't like.

product_title: Arrowhead Mills Organic Quinoa, 14 Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_body: This is fine with just water if you want to put something over it. However, if you want an easy, tasty, healthy side, try tossing around with a little butter and garlic then cook with veggie or chicken broth.     And remember - rinse, rinse, rinse beforehand and stir a few times while cooking.     This has a lot of nutrients, so worth a try and some experimentation.

product_title: Wild Oats Organic Popcorn, Butter, 10.5-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12)
review_body: This popcorn is really tasty and not too buttery.  The kids actually told me they prefer it to the old popcorn (ie, not the healthy type).  It does taste good.  Will buy again.  It came in very handy for halloween treats too when I ran out of candy.  Good buy.

product_title: Dr. McDougall's Right Foods Vegan Tomato Basil Pasta Soup, Lower Sodium, 1.3-Ounce Cups (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Lived on this one during the summer
review_body: I love this soup.  It is light but filling.  It has a wonderful aroma.  Everyone in my office has tried mine and can't believe it is low fat and powered.  If you like Italian or pasta salads you should enjoy this soup.

product_title: Pamela's Ultimate Baking and Pancake Mix
review_body: I have used Pamela's baking mix for pancakes, waffles, biscuits, pizza crust and scones.  I was pleasantly surprised by the wonderful flavor of everything I made using this mix.  There are lots of recipes on Pamela's web site, which is listed on the package.

product_title: Glutino Gluten Free Breakfast Bars, Blueberry, 5-Count Boxes (Pack of 6)
review_body:
I was introduced to these bars at a celiac conference, and later bought a box at a health food store. They are gluten free and they travel well. On the down side, they aren't good and I don't enjoy eating them. I will take them in my purse if I have nothing else, but I only eat them when really, really hungry and there are no other options around.

I much prefer the gluten free lara bars for flavor. These may however be good for those with complex dietary restrictions like Celiac combined with diabetes. But- I wouldn't buy them again.

product_title: EnviroKidz Organic Animal Cookies, Honey Graham, 9-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12)
review_headline: Not very tastey but they're fine for satisfying hunger
review_body: My boyfriend asked me the other day as he was munching on these crackers, \\"Are these dog biscuits?  Well they should be...\\"  That pretty much sums it up.  They taste a little odd - too salty I think.  But we have 12 boxes of it now so we better get used to it (or find some people to hand them off to).  They're fine for making my growling stomach stop during the mid morning hunger periods.

product_title: Fox River Italian Arborio Rice, 8-Ounce Pouches (Pack of 6)
review_headline: Goes great With Veal or Chicken Marsala
review_body: My husband and kids cleaned their plates of the Italian Arborio.  I've made it several times with veal and chicken and the authentic flavor pairs well. Cooked it last night and need to order more. I have always been happy with the Fox River Rice quality and flavor.

product_title: Earth's Best Organic Teething Biscuits, 4.6 Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12)
review_body: As with any teething biscuit you need to have a bib on because they can get messy. My daughter loves these and I feel good about feeding them to her.

product_title: Zhena's Gypsy Tea, Gypsy Love, 36-Count Tins (Pack of 3)
review_body:
The tea is exactly what you expect.
100% organic. The rose petal flavor
is great. Try it!

product_title: Ahmad Tea Black Tea, 20 Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_body: This is a tea you will definitely want to brew up again and again.  What a treat to the senses!  As you pour the boiling water into your cup of Apricot Tea - you will experience an uplifting feeling as you smell the Apricot Aroma drifting from your cup and when you sip your first sip of this delicious tea you can't help but smile - it is sooooooooooo! good!  So, put your feet up put on your favorite movie, or grab your favorite book or better yet just be still and close your eyes and relax as you enjoy this wonderful experience to the senses!

product_title: O.N.E. Drink, Cashew Fruit, 11.2-Ounce Aseptic Containers (Pack of 12)
review_body: Tastes like pineapple juice with a hint of pear.  It has a peculiar finish, which is somewhat nutty.  overall, the juice is very light and crisp.  It is slightly tart but not sour.  I felt it was a nice change of pace and liked the fact that it was not too sweet.

product_title: Peeled Snacks Cashew Later, 1-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 10)
review_body: Finally a snack food that is healthy, tasty, convenient and perfect for seniors. Whoever thought out this product had me in mind! I want something that I can have in my tennis bag, pocket or car that is really fresh and tasty. I mix them with the dried fruit and what a pleasure to have a very healthy mix that is really moist and flavorful with crunchy nuts (not salty!). I hate those dried rinds that most trail mixes contain. This product is more like a \\"luxury mix\\" than those trail mixes. At this point in my life I really would like to spend more time in the \\"mansion\\" than out on the trail! What is really nice about this product is that the freshness and taste is consistant. You really do not get tired of this snack. For those of use a little bit around the age bend, this is the first really appropriate snack I have tried. (If the grandkids don't get there first!) Good job, Peeled Snacks!

product_title: Rishi Tea Organic Silver Needle Jasmine  Loose Tea, 1.9-Ounce Tin (Pack of 2)
review_body: Vegan. Certified Organic. Certified Kosher. Made with 100% organic white tea leaves and 100% organic jasmine flowers. Highest quality. Exquisite white tea leaves blended with beautiful organic jasmine flowers. When the time grows close, each day the patron or patronesse of each tea estate will go into the tea gardens to check. Then, one morning, it is decided that the 'pluckers' with the keenest eyes and most nimble fingers will be sent to begin harvesting the most precious of the 'first flush' of the season from the tops of the mature & most energenic tea bushes. Once upon a time, not so long ago, I had begun the look at marketing ultra premium tea around the world with one of my very good friends from India. We met in Hong Kong. The venture didn't go ahead, but wonderful memories and some tea knowledge remain. Rishi is an ancient sacred word from India which means 'seer.' The Vedas were written long ago by the first Rishis, most of whose names are not even recorded. [Received one 1.9oz (54g) can of this tea at no cost through the Vine program.] This review is out there for those for whom this makes a difference. See all of my reviews and the vegancompassion Profile for more great choices. Check out \\"Vegan Grocery Favorites\\" and \\"Vegan Grocery Top Ten\\" & all the other helpful \\"Vegan Grocery\\" Listmania. Your input counts and will be greatly appreciated to benefit the search of others. Thank you.

product_title: Ralston Hot Cereal
review_body: I have always loved Ralston Hot Cereal. Grocery store owners need to made aware of Ralston and other \\"classic\\" foods that ALWAYS USED TO BE AVAILABLE IN EVERY GROCERY STORE! Now it's impossible to find Ralston in a store. That's why I turned to the internet to find it. It seems very odd to me considering the fact that people want to eat healthy foods. Ralston is and has always been a healthy food. It's all natural, whole grain, no preservatives or additives. It is also quick and easy to prepare. What more could you ask for if you want to eat healthy?

product_title: Kitchens Of India Biryanis Hyderabadi Biryani
review_body: Having tried Vegetable Hyderabadi Biryani in Hyderabad few times, I expected the same taste to atleast some extent.  But this smells very strong in Indian spices (the whole house, including  basement smelled for next 6 hours when microwaved) and when I tasted it, I got the feeling of a non-vegetarian dish. I had to add lots of raitha (side dish made of yogurt, onions, tomatoes, cilantro and diced serrano peppers) to overcome the strong taste. I have tried 3 other items from Kitchens of India and very satisfied and that's why I wanted to try this one. It is not that bad a choice if you have strong preference for that non-veg masala taste.

product_title: Rice Noodle Instant Soup, Garlic & Vegetable, 1.6 oz.
review_body: I got some free samples at a Celiac Awareness walk the other day and was super excited to try them. I was slightly disappointed in the flavor and consistancy. First off, I am big on trying noodles before they are cooked. I strongly urge you DON'T do this, blech! The positive of this product is that it cooked very fast so if you are in a rush that is nice. I don't like broth dripping all over the place when I eat so I drained it off and wish I hadn't. Immediatly it made the noodles clump in one huge gob of stickiness. The flavor was ok, nothing to write home about. I am not sure that I would buy this product or not. If I do, it will only be for the ease of preparation.

product_title: Leonidas Belgian Chocolates: Signature Dark Chocolates Assortment
review_body:
These are definitely \\"mid-range\\" chocolates, not quite as good as Godiva or See's. If you're used to low-end chocolates like Fannie May or Russell Stover, you'll probably find these to be very good. However, if you're used to very good chocolates like La Maison du Chocolat, you'll be sorely disappointed.

I found the chocolate to have unexceptional flavor and a somewhat waxy texture. The fillings were mostly very sweet or alcoholic, which is a common practice to cover up mediocre chocolate.

I guess they're a good value compared to Godiva, although I think See's Candies has an even better value. Don't expect Leonidas to compare to a high-end chocolatier.

product_title: Arrow Spacemaker Deck Box Basket Weave
review_body: This sweetner is so tasty, almost like real maple syrup. As a matter of fact, it is so full bodied, I can add it to coffee with cream and have a taste that reminds me of Starbuck's French Vanilla Latte.  It is low glycemic and safe for diabetics. We love it on yogurt, oatmeal,and foods like that. I am not as fond of it to sweeten tea as it imparts a little vanilla-like flavor.  My whole family loves it and this is the best price I have found.  Caution: not all agave nectars are equal!!! This is a good one.

product_title: Lea and Perrins Traditional Steak Sauce 15 OZ
review_body: Great  I wish it was sold in stores in Montana it wought save shipping.   Agin just a GREAT product

product_title: Ting Ting Jahe Ginger Candy, 5.25 Ounce
review_body: The ginger flavor of this candy is fantastic; mild for a quick second, then nice and spicy, and the flavor lasts in your mouth for a while after you've finished just one piece. They've got the firmness of Starbursts, and are about an inch long with a rice paper wrapper around them. This is the only ginger candy I've ever had, but it's a great starting point! Wonderful stuff.

product_title: Sun Maid Calimyrna Figs, 6-Ounce Bags (Pack of 6)
review_headline: If you like figs, you'll love these
review_body:
I've bought five different growers' figs from Amazon - though I suspect it's one big Fresno cooperative that separates by type and dryness. For sweetness, freshness, and just overall taste, the Sun Maid Calimyrna win hands down, BUT they are the most expensive. They come in a 6-ounce bad instead of everybody else's 8. And be careful: Sun Maid also has the darker figs in 8 ounce packs, and they're plump and sweet as well, but I can only get those in the market right now.

The best buy is Blue Ribbon Orchard Choice Figs. They're quite a bit drier, but taste as good. They're also smaller, so watch the calorie count. There's a tendency to east 8-12 of these little ones without thinking that you're going through 240 calories fairly quickly.

I see no difference between organic and ... what, inorganic ... except that organic costs more. All five that I've bought run between $2.50 and $3.00 a pack, about 60 cents less than market price. But all five have exactly the same calorie count, vitamins, and additives or lack thereof. All come from Fresno, and the two differences are in size and mositness.

If I were a rich man (play Fiddler in the background), I'd buy a truckload of the Sun Main. Oh, yeah, most of the Sun Maid Calimyna don't have stems to worry about. On the other hand, sometrimes stems make for good \\"handles.\\"

product_title: DiabeticFriendly Sugar Free Assorted Fruit Fruit Slices, Orange, Cherry, Lime & Lemon, Individually Wrapped, 1lb Bag
review_body: These were very tasty, individually wrapped, sugar free gummy treats.  I recommend checking out the producer's website - [...] for a boat load of sugar free snacks.

product_title: Bear Naked All Natural Oatmeal, Triple Berry, 8-Count Boxes (Pack of 4)
review_body:
This is delcious tasting stuff - not just oatmeal but flax meal and other all natural ingrediants. The packets themselves are foil-lined so they'll do well in high-humidity environments.
I highly recommend this cereal.

product_title: Quaker Instant Oatmeal Express Cinnamon Roll, 1.9-Ounce Cups (Pack of 12)
review_body: They are great for breakfast and work for a snack when you are in a hurry

product_title: Mi Goreng Instant Noodles
review_headline: The Ramen Revolution will be Indomied
review_body:
Although, I understand that the Goreng part of the name means noodles without broth, I'll never stop calling this ramen (meaning noodles with broth). The Indomie products that I've tried (original, satay, and pedas) are all delicious. Make no mistake, not all oriental noodles do it for me. When our local Asian market ran out of Indomie, the owner told me to get a different brand that he promised I'd like better. I ended up throwing it out, because the taste was just awful. Indomie (original) however, has a mellow taste, with enough spice to keep you interested.

This how noodles are done. Classic.

product_title: Taylors of Harrogate Assorted Tea
review_headline: $24.47, lasted six months but lacks the fragrance and depth of St. James
review_body:
This is a tolerable tea similar to Twinings.

I regret this purchase.

product_title: Arrowhead Mills Gluten Free Chocolate Chip Cookie Mix, 12.9 Ounce (Pack of 6)
review_body: Out of all of the gluten-free cookies that I've tried these are my favorite.  I put in a soy-based butter-alternative and add a little extra to make them very moist.  I'd give it more stars if the product was somehow healthier.

product_title: Emeril's Gaaahlic Parmesan Essence, 3.75-Ounce Unit (Pack of 6)
review_body: I first tried this when I recieved an Emeril assorted 4-pack for Christmas. The others are good, but this stuff is GREAT. I always go down to my local Italian store, where they make homemade bread daily to get my bread. I cut the loaf in half vertically and just follow the directions. I do use A LOT of full flavored olive oil and a let it soak into the bread for a few min before applying the spice. Then I use a LOT of this spice. One thing, the directions say to bake for 10 min. In my oven, it comes out much better if I leave it in for 15 min. Then I just cut it into pieces about an inch or so wide. Any leftovers I just put in a storage bag, and keep in the fridge. It's a great quick late night snack (sometimes with butter),even cold. I've been out of this for a couple weeks, so I can't wait for my shipment to arrive.

product_title: Big Train Vanilla Chai, 1.9-Pound Cans (Pack of 2)
review_headline: Great flavor and a great buy
review_body:
You get to large cans of the powder. The flavor is rich and the best part is you can make it as sweet or as week as you like. One scoop per cup is usually plenty. I mix mine with a little milk to for a more creamy texture. I've tried a few other mixes and some have had a nasty smell and after taste. I used to buy the Target brand in the green can but they discontinued that and now make it in a silver can and its one of those fake chemical smelling and tasting mixes...YUK.

The only complaint about this is that 25% of the can is empty so you really don't get a full can. Other than that the flavor is great. Very close to the Duncan Donuts kind.

product_title: Espressione Classic Coffee Pods, Box of 150
review_body: I am using a Briel espresso machine and these pods are great.  I use the "Classic Espresso" variety, I have not tried the "Arabica" yet.  These are very nice flavor and result in a nice crema (not sure if that is more the result of my machine though).  Much much better than the Illy pods and in my opinion equally as good as the Starbucks pods but much less expensive.

product_title: Loma Linda Vege-Burger, 19-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12)
review_body: This has been used in my family to make \\"hamburgers\\" for as long as I've been alive and I love it.  Like I've said in other reviews for Loma Linda/Worthington foods it's not meat, it is not meant to taste like meat.  I've also stated before that the meat substitutes are an acquired taste and it tends to be like it or hate it.  Vege-Burger is versatile, but it is not something that can be eaten without seasoning as it is not palatable on its own.

product_title: Chef Boyardee
review_body: If you ate this stuff as a kid then you will enjoy it as an adult. Portions were good, heating em up was easy and clean up was a cinch. Grab a couple dozen you wont be disappointed and if you have kids they will like em too.

product_title: Raw Revolution Organic Live Food Bars, 1.8-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12)
review_headline: Doesn't taste like diet food to me
review_body: Regarding my recent purchase of the Raw Revolution Organic Live Food Bars in Raspberry and Chocolate flavored (2.2-Ounce Bars for a pack of 12), I must say this sure does NOT taste like diet food to me. The chocolate rasberry blended together and made a delightful flavor. Even though flax seeds are mixed into this combo, the seeds are ground up enough not to cause any concerns and I really liked the chewy texture. I recommend keeping them in the fridge for a cool treat.

product_title: Health Valley Chunky Chili, Vegetarian Mild, 15 Ounce Tins (Pack of 12)
review_body: The chili is very good, not spicy all, but the shipping was a problem. The first case I got had 8 dented cans and 4 that were ok. I complained, and Amazon replaced the case immediately, but it was the same problem--8 dented cans. Amazon probably would have sent more, but I didn't pursue it    Steve

product_title: Happy Baby Organic Baby Cereals with DHA + Pre & Probiotics, 7 Ounce Canisters (Pack of 6)
review_body: This cereal has a nice texture and taste (yep, I tried it!), and doesn't make my baby constipated, the way rice cereals do.  It's very easy to mix up - use formula, breast milk, or water.   I also add other fruit or vegetable purees or mashes.  The baby gobbles it up, and I love knowing that it's organic.

product_title: Celestial Seasonings Sleepytime Tea Variety Pack
review_body: I use the regular Sleepytime frequently in the evenings, but on those nights when you need a little something extra, this stuff is amazing. Its very nice when travelling and you are having a hard time sleeping in a strange bed.  I don't like taking medications (no Lunestra for me) but with this, don't need to.

product_title: Gustaf's Dutch Licorice Coins,  6 Plastic containers - 7-Ounce each
review_body: While vacationing in Steamboat Springs in 2007, my husband and I stopped into Fuzziwigg's Candy Store. Since my husband likes licorice, but not knowing this particular brand, we bought only 5 licorice coins.  He loved them!  5 coins didn't go very far and I frantically wanted to get him some as a Christmas present.  Amazon, you're amazing!  Not only did he get 1 container of coins... he got 6!  He's in Heaven!  He has about 4 or 5 coins every night - and I'm watching the level of licorice so that he won't run out.  What a great product!

product_title: The Tao of Tea
review_body: I first had this at McMenamin's Kennedy School in Portland, Oregon at breakfast.  I fell in love with this tea instantly.  It's not heavily floral at all.  It has enough rose flavor that it keeps you coming back for more.  I can't find it in our stores in central Ohio, so I'm thrilled I can find this online.  Enjoy!

product_title: Celestial Seasonings Tea
review_headline: Surprisingly good, but could be a bit better
review_body: I'm not usually a Celestial Seasonings fan.  I find many of their offerings decidedly below par.  But Bengal Spice is actually pretty good.  It's perfect for cinnamon fans, as that is undoubtedly the boldest taste in this blend.  And it's true that you don't need to sweeten it; the cinnamon takes care of that itself.    In terms of strength it's nice and bold.  The vanilla smoothes everything out though...it's not too strong, unless you let the bag steep for an inordinately long time.  But Bengal Spice does have one notable weakness....for those looking for a great chai, you might be disappointed.  Because while it's strong and has a nice flavor, the ginger, cardamom, nutmeg etc. is hardly noticeable, masked by the strength of the cinnamon.  It's a shame, because this blend is definitely better-tasting than some, such as Yogi's classic India Spice.  If the other \\"chai spices\\" in this blend had been stronger, this would be a 5-star tea.

product_title: Billington's All-Natural Sugar Crystals, 16-Ounce Cartons (Pack of 10)
review_body: I Love this Sugar. All it is is pure natural cane sugar. It is sooooo delicious in my daily cup of hot tea, with cream, each morning! It makes for a sweet, 'caramelly' flavour and the price is excellent - not expensive like so many of the other fancy import sugars that are dry and tasteless. Just ordered a case!

product_title: illy Medium Roast Ground Coffee for Espresso Machines
review_body: Great espresso, taste great consistantly. Plus, 2-pak deal is great, saves me tax AND no shipping charge.  Great in this economy!

product_title: Nescafe Taster's Choice Instant Coffee, Decaffeinated, .059-Ounce Single Sticks, 80-Count Boxes (Pack of 2)
review_body: This is instant alright but really lacks rich coffee taste or aroma. I tried it out and was truly disappointed by this product. They need to work on making a richer, bolder taste in their future products.

product_title: Cookie of the Month (6 Months)
review_body: Some very nice relatives, trying to come up with a really thoughtful gift, ordered me and my husband these cookies of the month, knowing that I in particular am a HUGE cookie fan. I was very excited -- until I opened up the first box. The first problem is that the cookies, disappointingly small themselves, are packed in a tiny pouch, so you're really not getting much [especially considering that each tin of cookies costs @15 dollars!!!]. However, if the cookies were delectable little treats, who would care? Sadly, though, they are not - my husband and I found the first two varieties [benne cookies and choc mint] edible if uninteresting, but the last four were promptly thrown away upon a first taste. I can't describe how horrible these 4 were: it's as if you took tiny stale Nilla Wafers and dipped them in sugary chemicals of varying hues. [These would be the Key Lime Coolers, the Peach things, some sort of Raspberry or Strawberry/Lime thingie, and some other supersweet flavor I can't recall]. YUCK!!!! All in all, not just a waste of money but a dastardly crime perpetrated against cookie lovers everywhere. What a disappointment!!!!!!

product_title: Dare Whippet Cookies, Original, 8.8-Ounce Packages (Pack of 12)
review_body: The product was shipped by U.P.S.  It was clearly marked \\"Chocolate - Store in a cool dry place.\\"  It was, nonetheless, left at my doorstep when I was not home.  I do not know how long it had been sitting in the Florida heat before I got home, but the product was melted and all but inedible.    It strikes me that I shuld have received a notice of attempt to deliver, and the product should be kept in a \\"cool dry place\\" until it could be accepted by me.

product_title: Alwadi Al Akhdar Baba Ghannouge, Eggplant Dip, 12.75-Ounce Cans (Pack of 12)
review_body: This tastes surprisingly good for something that comes out of a can. However, there is a bit too much \\"citric acid\\" in it, as it does have that slightly sour flavor. Also, you have to watch out for the seeds because they are present in the mix. I'm going to try making this as the directions state (sans more lemon juice). This goes really great with pitas.
